2. When all configured origins are unreachable or invalid, synchronization shall record an unavailable/stale result and readyz shall fail after the declared freshness budget; a genuinely observed equal head shall remain distinguishable from no observation.
3. Wrong genesis/network/sequencer pins, malformed heads, signature failures and discontinuous batch history shall retain explicit refusal without advancing canonical progress.
4. Restart shall retain the last proven head and freshness state, not manufacture a fresh observation; reconnection shall validate continuity before clearing degradation.
5. Explicit local-source-only operation shall use a separately defined local source health/progress contract rather than require nonexistent remote origins; status shall truthfully identify the selected mode.

## Requirement 174: Gate ramp readiness on a healthy durable journal and verified recovery

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Ramp readyz shall require operational durable journal state including the halted/uncertain-write flag; obtaining the mutex shall not by itself imply readiness.
2. Interrupted append, corrupt record, exclusive-writer conflict and ambiguous durable state shall withdraw readiness and preserve mutation refusal without discarding journal history.
3. Restart or explicit recovery shall validate journal framing, identities and external settlement state before clearing the halt; a status read shall not reset a persistent halt.
4. Real provider, compliance decision key, identity, non-exporting signer handles, custody-owner interface, quote catalogue and operator identifiers shall be explicit protected inputs; current chain/network pins and agreeing RPC reads shall be validated.
5. A recovered sandbox ramp journey shall declare external custody and reach done only against the verified LayerX-side receipt; provider pending, reversal and chargeback cases shall retain their declared typed states.

## Requirement 175: Package and qualify redundant pinned relay archives on Fly

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The relay source package shall include an explicit Fly manifest for at least two machines in two regions, each with its own durable archive volume and a bounded resource configuration.
2. A sequencer-colocated LayerX origin shall expose the pinned canonical genesis/network/sequencer data over authenticated TLS, while relay replicas validate those exact pins and continuity before readiness.
3. The public archive route shall expose readyz and sync head and forward original signed activity bytes to the configured unified router, returning its verified verdict without signing/reconstructing the request.
4. The future bringup relay mode shall be registered and shall require every selected replica's genesis equality and lag within one batch of a contemporaneously read origin, refusing missing replicas, wrong pins, stale origins and altered bytes.
5. Existing deployment inventory and image/source identity shall precede runtime changes; restart on each replica shall preserve history and revalidate freshness, and a failed replica shall not cause private origin material or credentials to be exposed.

## Requirement 176: Retain EVM web-attestation work before advancing event cursors

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Confirmed decoded EVM requests and their canonical source identity shall be durably queued before the watcher cursor is committed beyond them.
2. Restart before fetch, during independent attestation, before quorum, after quorum and before signed-transaction journaling shall restore incomplete work and retain or deterministically reconstruct valid partial signature progress.
3. Transient fetch/peer errors shall enter bounded retry state; terminal invalid requests shall have durable explicit refusal, and neither class shall disappear merely because its event range was scanned.
4. Signatures shall remain bound to the exact origin/domain/request/content digest and registered membership; wrong digest, duplicate/unsorted signers and insufficient threshold shall never authorize fulfilment.
5. After signed bytes are journaled, recovery shall reuse their transaction identity and reconcile already-fulfilled/refunded or reorged requests before another economic action, preserving exactly-once completion under the declared finality depth.

## Requirement 177: Recover kernel web requests and submitted observations across restarts

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Kernel event progress shall advance only after every discovered paid request is durable with program/request/topic identity and its exact attestation/submission state.
2. Awaiting-quorum and retryable attestation/post failures shall remain queued across restart; terminal refusal shall be recorded explicitly without silently dropping paid work.
3. Observation submission shall persist exact signed activity bytes and idempotency identity before send, and recover pending/unknown outcomes through committed receipt lookup before deciding to resubmit.
4. Kernel observations shall retain origin2 preimage, program/request/payload-hash binding, ascending registered signers, low-s and majority-threshold checks, and exactly-once fee splitting/intake.
5. A reference program shall request and pay, survive relay restart before quorum and after submit, receive one verified observation and read the same committed data through web_read without duplicate charge or observation.

## Requirement 178: Bind settled payments to durable recoverable search and fetch delivery

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Invalid/missing/duplicate query parameters and malformed resource requests shall be rejected before any settlement draw or receipt consumption.
2. After verified settlement, one receipt shall bind to one canonical request/resource identity and durable delivery state; a handler/index/content-store failure shall preserve a recoverable paid entitlement instead of irreversibly consuming it.
3. A retry of the same canonical paid request shall return its persisted result or resume the same delivery without a second charge; a changed request, foreign receipt, replay for another resource or unverified/pending settlement shall release no content.
4. Crash after settlement, during resource computation, after result persistence and before response acknowledgement shall retain the exact payment/result association, with explicit pending or failed delivery state rather than unbacked success.
5. PAYMENT-RESPONSE and content digest shall name verified evidence and the actual canonical result; configured metered and exact schemes and SID/PAX/USDC/USDL base-unit rules shall remain intact.

## Requirement 179: Advertise paid-web readiness from role-specific usable dependencies

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Serving, attestor and kernel-relay roles shall expose separate bounded readiness reflecting required index/content storage, settlement authority, peer quorum or relay progress, while process liveness remains independent.
2. Empty upstream selection, unavailable required index, unbound settlement trust, insufficient registered peers and stale relay progress shall not produce serving-ready merely because a health handler runs.
3. The search frontend shall route only to eligible serving backends and preserve the same backend/resource binding between PAYMENT-REQUIRED and paid retry; a failed dependency shall not turn a paid retry into a second charge.
4. Restart/recovery shall restore durable pending work before readiness, and recent progress shall have a declared freshness budget rather than be inferred from source presence or an open socket.
5. Private attestor listeners and peer routes shall remain private and authenticated; no public API or DNS relocation shall be introduced to satisfy the readiness check.

## Requirement 180: Provision priced paid search and authorized web-attestor settlement identities

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Search pricing shall use the approved USD0.001 per request at USD13.44/PAX, exactly 1/13440PAX before documented ceiling conversion to configured PAX base units; all accepted asset IDs/decimals and conversion inputs shall be validated against registered kernel metadata.
2. Actual serving receivers, kernel submitter/payout DIDs, payer authority/balance, web signer membership and EVM submitter funding shall be inventoried and reconciled through authorized registration/custody-credit paths; absent amounts or authority shall remain explicit inputs, never invented.
3. The four intended private web-attestor slots shall retain distinct web/submitter/receiver key roles and approved majority membership, protected per-slot volumes and peer connectivity; wallet membership/threshold decisions shall not be borrowed or silently changed.
4. A serving RPC endpoint, the client's redundant path and search.paxeer.network shall each demonstrate a verified paid search at the declared price; the 402 challenge and retry shall remain bound to the same resource/backend.
5. A real EVM request shall produce XWebFulfilled with verified signer membership and callback disposition, and a real kernel paid request shall produce a committed observation and correct payout; insufficient funding/quorum, wrong membership and wrong asset/price shall refuse.
6. Candidate image/config identity, account/registration read-backs and nonsecret receipt references shall be retained after restart; private attestor operation shall not require validator changes or API1 DNS movement.

## Requirement 181: Sponsor a consent-bound first transaction for an undelegated SID holder

### Acceptance Criteria

1. An undelegated EOA holding sufficient six-decimal SID and no PAX shall be able to obtain a valid first-use quote and submit an account-consented sponsor-paid EIP7702 authorization plus batch.
2. Initial nonce/replay state shall derive only from verified account-code/delegation status and the defined authorization semantics; an empty eth_call result shall not be blindly treated as zero for an incompatible or unknown account.
3. Existing incompatible delegation, wrong chain/delegate/account, invalid low-s signature, expired authorization/quote, consumed nonce, wrong sponsor/token or excess signed maximum shall be refused before sponsor funds are committed.
4. Success shall atomically execute the authorized calls and repay the exact governed SID amount; failed SID transfer shall revert the entire batch, and direct account execution shall retain its existing behavior.
5. Restart during first-use submission shall recover the same durable transaction identity and reconcile delegation/receipt outcome before another nonce or charge; client consent shall display amount, maximum and deadline before signing.
6. Sponsored EIP7702 execution shall remain distinct from the native fee-token preference path; native fee preference shall be exposed only under the actual registered upgrade and governed enabled/allowed-denom parameters, with exact six-decimal SID metadata and no inferred parameter activation.

## Requirement 182: Drive sponsored-transaction recovery autonomously from the durable journal

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The actual station binary shall run a bounded single-writer startup and periodic recovery driver over all unresolved submissions without requiring a repeated client POST.
2. Prepared, broadcast, dropped, replaced, cancelled and finalized states shall reconcile exact signed transaction identities against finalized height/canonical block and receipt evidence before allocating or releasing sponsor nonces.
3. A crash before/after broadcast and during replacement/cancellation shall resume exact durable bytes, retain ambiguous liabilities and avoid duplicate execution or SID repayment.
4. Authenticated submission status and same-identity retry shall remain available after quote expiry without requiring fresh signing of the expired quote; new expired authorization shall still be refused.
5. One unreachable RPC or unresolved submission shall yield bounded honest pending/refusal state; competing writers, corrupt journals and divergent majority observations shall fail closed.
6. A real-process restart case shall progress to finalized settlement or verified cancellation without client resubmission and shall unblock the next safe sponsor nonce.

## Requirement 183: Account durably for outstanding gas promises separately from historical usage

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Quote policy shall distinguish active outstanding PAX liability from historical per-account/per-interval usage and finalized spend; capacity shall not remain consumed by safely expired unused or finalized completed/cancelled quotes.
2. Every reservation/release shall have a durable identity and justified terminal event, replay exactly once on restart and preserve liabilities for ambiguous broadcasts, replacements and still-executable promises.
3. Concurrent quote/submit/recovery operations shall enforce configured per-quote/per-account/per-interval limits and the actual sponsor balance floor without overpromising funds.
4. Quote issuance shall have explicit authenticated binding or bounded anti-exhaustion limits appropriate to its public contract; malformed/replayed issuance shall not multiply reservations.
5. Repeated expiry/completion and process restart shall restore the same available capacity; early release, double release, dropped-but-still-valid submission and balance deterioration shall produce refusal rather than a false available balance.

## Requirement 184: Resume governed-rate publications from exact durable signed transactions

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Before broadcast, every rate publication shall durably retain exact signed bytes plus owner/chain/paymaster/nonce/hash/rate/gas/fee identity; no private key or credential shall enter the record.
2. After a crash between append and send, the publisher shall reconcile/rebroadcast that same prepared transaction before constructing another publication; deterministic duplicate hash shall be an idempotent recovery state rather than fatal append conflict.
3. Replacement and cancellation shall retain one coherent nonce/liability history, bounded fee ceilings and canonical finalized outcome checks; different hashes at one nonce shall not create independent unbounded reservations.
4. Published rates shall retain governed age, spread and owner authorization checks; publisher cadence shall be strictly below station maximum age with declared allowance for confirmation/retry, and stale/future/missing rates shall refuse new quotes.
5. Interrupted write, changed owner/paymaster/chain, malformed bytes and uncertain finality shall fail closed while preserving history; a real publisher restart shall recover before rate age expiry when dependencies remain available.
6. Configuration shall supply distinct named sponsor and paymaster-owner key sources, protected persistent journals, owner-controlled rate input and sufficient authorized funding; no address/rate/key shall be fabricated.

## Requirement 185: Serve browser sponsorship requests through an explicit permitted-origin boundary

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The wallet SDK shall complete quote and submission/status requests from the configured wallet origin through an authenticated same-origin gateway or an explicit station origin policy, with documented endpoint configuration.
2. If cross-origin service is selected, OPTIONS shall accept only allowed origin/method/header combinations and return the required exact Access-Control/Vary headers; disallowed origins and unsupported methods/headers shall be refused.
3. Public origin handling shall not bypass account/quote authorization, signature validation, replay protection, request bounds or rate limits; wildcard credentialed access shall not be introduced.
4. A real browser-origin gate shall execute preflight and actual JSON request, then verify typed unavailable/refused/cancelled/pending/completed outcomes and authenticated recovery after restart.
5. Client amounts shall retain SID six-decimal representation, signed maximum/deadline presentation and approved sponsor/token identity; transaction-hash receipt alone shall not be rendered as completed settlement.

## Requirement 186: Admit only mintable recipients before EVM custody moves

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Both deposit entrypoints accept exactly a nonzero EVM address left-padded to bytes32; a nonzero high prefix or zero low address is rejected before balance, nonce, outstanding or event changes.
2. Accepted recipient bytes remain identical through BridgeDeposit, inbound digest, relayer decoding and Keeper.BridgeIn; selectors, event topics and digest layouts remain unchanged.
3. Token and native custody use the same rule, while pause, exact token balance delta, threshold, replay and rescue restrictions remain intact.
4. Any existing incompatible deposit is reported as requiring an explicit authorized recovery disposition; consumers never rewrite signed recipient bytes or manufacture credit.

## Requirement 187: Bind outbound burn admission to the enforceable release amount

### Acceptance Criteria

1. BridgeOut rejects a nonpositive, over-supply or above-registered-per-transaction amount before debiting, burning, incrementing nonce or emitting BridgeOut.
2. Two independently admissible deposits cannot be combined into one burn above the active release cap; a burn at the cap remains valid.
3. The configured Paxeer admission cap is no greater than the foreign release cap; cap changes use an explicit coordination contract that prevents new unfulfillable burns and preserves already-authorized pending releases.
4. EVM and Solana release caps, fixed attested amount and once-only nullifier remain enforced; an existing pending burn receives a visible resolution state rather than a rewritten or split attestation.

## Requirement 188: Advance independent outbound destinations despite item failures

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A destination-specific RPC, receipt or signer error is recorded for the affected item while ready items for other EVM destinations and Solana still advance in the same bounded pass.
2. Corrupt or unwritable shared journal state remains fatal; error isolation never permits signing or sending without a durable valid record.
3. A restart rebroadcasts the identical pending bytes, preserves per-submitter nonce order and never duplicates completed economic effects.
4. Repeated failures remain visible with the item and destination identity and do not cause an unbounded retry loop inside one poll.

## Requirement 189: Provide the approved bridge attestor quorum with durable share delivery

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Inventory the existing bridge relayers, approved attestor membership/threshold, signer handles, share transport and journal ownership before declaring any deployment absent or creating a replacement.
2. The approved threshold is reached through distinct bridge attestors with independent fee-payer handles and journals; wallet membership and xweb attestors remain separate authorities.
3. Share delivery rejects wrong-digest, unknown, duplicate and malformed shares; insufficient quorum stays waiting without submitting a partial authorization.
4. Loss or restart of one operator preserves published valid shares and once-only completion; private keys never enter relayer configuration or shared storage.

## Requirement 189.1: Authenticated durable delivery of bridge cosign shares

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Three real independent transport processes exchange actual signatures through production publish/collect/assemble paths. Two shares remain below a three-signature threshold; three distinct valid shares satisfy it.
2. Mutual TLS1.3, hostname verification and unique pinned SPKI-to-attestor mappings authenticate both endpoints. Foreign CA, unpinned client, incorrect server pin, wrong recipient or signer, invalid signature or digest are refused without share or acknowledgement writes.
3. Bounded length-delimited framing rejects truncation, oversize, malformed magic/version and surplus frame data. Ciphertext modification causes TLS refusal without durable changes.
4. Identical delivery is idempotent; a conflicting signature never overwrites existing bytes. Shares and delivery metadata survive actual process termination and restart on the same disk.
5. Acknowledgements follow authenticated Stored or AlreadyHeld only. Unavailable peers retry after restart; conflicts are durable and explicit. Bounded fair sweeps reach entries beyond the first page. Peer pin changes cannot inherit previous identity acknowledgements.
6. Peer, connection, frame, timeout and sweep bounds are finite and validated. Shared directories hold signatures and public delivery metadata only; private keys stay outside them.
7. Explicitly enabled transport refuses absent or invalid configuration. Container source builds and installs the actual transport binary and supervises its lifetime and shutdown. Missing configured transport never silently becomes standalone mode.
8. Generated fixture keys and placeholder rosters do not establish production membership. Production certificate issuance, network exposure and deployment remain separate.

## Requirement 190: Publish an executable Solana relayer configuration contract

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The operator runbook describes optional solana configuration, reserved chain ID, program/vault identity, commitment, slot depth, RPC quorum and separate ed25519 fee-payer handle.
2. The release_mints activation rule and recipient PDA plus initialized token-account prerequisites are explicit; omission is described as observation-only rather than claimed outbound readiness.
3. The example is accepted by the production configuration validator; unknown fields, wrong chain identity, invalid commitment and attestor/fee-payer handle reuse are refused.
4. Examples carry public identity and handle references only and do not invent production addresses or credentials.

## Requirement 191: Feed public receipt routes from verified kernel receipt provenance

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A real LayerX relay/archive receipt reaches the PostgreSQL receipt projection and list/detail routes with batch, sequence, activity and proof provenance.
2. Kernel-origin receipts do not require fabricated EVM transaction/log/block fields; EVM-derived rows retain their own provenance class.
3. Malformed, mismatched or insufficiently authorized receipt evidence cannot acquire a verified label; no route reads private node internals or user profile data.
4. Durable ingestion resumes after restart, deduplicates replay and rebuilds the projection from the declared public boundary.

## Requirement 192: Restore canonical asset and account projections during rollback

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Rolling back a supply-bearing receipt removes its observed supply metadata and orphan-only asset/account discovery without deleting configured pointer records.
2. A replacement branch containing no supply update derives the last surviving canonical metadata rather than retaining an orphan value.
3. Transfer, event, asset, account, chain-link and cursor changes commit atomically and remain consistent after database reopen.
4. Rollback beyond the finalized boundary remains refused and configured asset metadata has explicit provenance separate from observed updates.

## Requirement 193: Expose source-aware history freshness and readiness

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Health distinguishes process/database liveness from readiness of each required ingestion source, with last successful observation and indexed/source cursor positions.
2. A stalled or repeatedly failing LayerX source makes history readiness degraded or unavailable despite a healthy database; gateway history status preserves that state.
3. Idle but healthy sources remain ready when current head observation succeeds; readiness does not require new transactions.
4. After restart, persisted cursor progress is reconciled with a fresh source observation before readiness becomes positive; stale rows remain labeled with freshness.

## Requirement 194: Return verified LayerX activity and continuation in unified account responses

### Acceptance Criteria

1. GET /v1/accounts/{id}/unified serializes the complete UnifiedAccountView, including LayerX activity, achieved verification level and continuation.
2. Before/limit parameters govern the returned LayerX page with stable ordering, bounded limits and typed invalid-cursor refusal.
3. Identity, balances, settlement and Paxeer activity retain their existing fields; missing or unverified evidence is not upgraded by serialization.
4. A receipt-backed nonempty response survives service restart/rebuild with stable identifiers and no discarded activity page.

## Requirement 195: Run the standalone explorer receipt ingestion lifecycle

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The standalone serving binary retrieves checkpoint/availability data through the node boundary and receipt authority through the independent verifier before publishing receipt-backed activity.
2. An empty or behind projection reports incomplete-from-head rather than complete empty history; missing authority never produces a verified row.
3. Cursors/checkpoints are durable or safely rebuildable, and restart converges without duplicate receipt/activity rows.
4. Program-state refresh and receipt ingestion coexist with bounded retry and shutdown; node internals and private state are never read.

## Requirement 196: Publish explicit index stability and settlement verification levels

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The API distinguishes local reversible-depth stability from independently verified LayerX settlement and identifies the evidence source for each level.
2. No depth-only calculation, challenge-window default or receipt ordering alone sets a settlement-final label.
3. If settlement is claimed, the label requires verified checkpoint/anchor evidence bound to the receipt; unavailable or invalid evidence yields the corresponding lower/unknown level.
4. Rollback and restart preserve provenance and can lower local stability when warranted without silently retaining a stronger unsupported claim.

## Requirement 197: Navigate the complete server-paginated unified account history

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The backend returns a stable continuation for every nonterminal page and the frontend requests that continuation instead of slicing only the first array.
2. An account spanning multiple backend pages exposes every item once in the declared order; concurrent new entries do not create skipped or repeated older entries.
3. Counts are labeled page-local unless an authoritative total is supplied; malformed, expired or wrong-account cursors fail clearly.
4. Back/forward navigation preserves account and page identity and remains usable after reload without silently changing filters.

## Requirement 198: Support the published bounded Programs event query in the CLI library

### Acceptance Criteria

1. RpcClient accepts lx_getProgramEvents using the exact published positional parameter and bound rules and decodes the gateway response.
2. The CLI OpenRPC fixture and strict published-method equality assertions match the authoritative gateway contract without deleting assertions or filtering the new method out.
3. Missing, extra, malformed and out-of-bound arguments are rejected before transport; authenticated subscription behavior remains separate.
4. The change covers the existing library interface and does not claim an unimplemented generic CLI RPC subcommand.

## Requirement 199: Refresh receipt evidence while verification is advancing

### Acceptance Criteria

1. An open nonterminal receipt detail view obtains later indexed verification evidence through bounded polling or a real invalidation subscription.
2. The view displays freshness and distinguishes settlement rung from independently achieved verification; elapsed time alone never upgrades either.
3. Terminal, hidden or unmounted views stop unnecessary refresh work; transient transport failure preserves the last evidence with a visible stale/error state.
4. Reconnection resumes refresh without overlapping unbounded requests or downgrading a stronger verified row to an unsupported claim.

## Requirement 200: Create isolated Human role runtime directories before privilege drop

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every configured Human role receives its own root-created private runtime child owned by the declared role UID/GID and mode0700 before the role drops privileges.
2. A fresh runtime starts each role without requiring world-writable parents or permission broadening; another role UID cannot traverse or modify its child.
3. Restart recreates ephemeral directories safely while preserving durable material/state and refusing symlinks or unexpected ownership.
4. The selected integrated source includes the intended role-directory repair, with unmerged source reconciled explicitly rather than attributed to main.

## Requirement 201: Produce and order the complete Human policy and authority material graph

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every consumed policy, principal-policy, authority, owner/native/naming evidence and registry document has a declared real producer or a named required owner input.
2. Bootstrap ordering from genesis through sequencer identity, registry material, deployment journal, assembled policy and role authority is acyclic and publishes complete validated generations atomically.
3. Missing or inconsistent inputs keep affected roles in a typed waiting/refusal state; no placeholder principal, fabricated deployment evidence or trust bypass is accepted.
4. Restart resumes the existing generation and detects inconsistent partial publication without regenerating identity or abandoning durable Human state.

## Requirement 202: Run the Human movement signer through the intended KMS and CA identities

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The selected kernel candidate launches the Human KMS service expected by movement configuration with declared endpoint/server identity and required executor/client certificate identities.
2. Movement and KMS use the same intended trust relationship; wrong CA, server name, client role or signer policy is refused without relaxing existing equality checks.
3. The KMS starts only after its private role directories and validated material are available, and movement readiness reflects KMS readiness.
4. A restart resumes authorized signing without exposing private key material or converting wallet/xweb authority into Human KMS authority.

## Requirement 203: Require the complete configured kernel service roster for readiness

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The kernel-app gate compares observed roles to an explicit expected roster and refuses a missing, duplicate, unexpected or wrong-UID role.
2. Each role required for usable journeys has its process/material boundary checked; mere existence of one status file cannot establish whole-app readiness.
3. Pre-genesis waiting remains an explicit permitted bootstrap state only where the contract allows it and cannot be reported as fully operational.
4. A missing KMS or another required role fails the gate while a complete valid roster passes; evidence records the candidate identity and role-specific reason.

## Requirement 204: Reconcile persisted Human identity bindings during explicit rotation

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Before explicit key/genesis rotation, the tool inventories persisted trust history, receipt-authority replica bindings and role material and produces a concrete compatibility plan.
2. Incompatible old bindings cannot start consumers against a new identity; they yield a precise refusal until an authorized validated migration completes.
3. Rotation preserves custody, financial and audit state and never blindly deletes durable Human data or regenerates independent trust history.
4. Interrupted rotation/restart resumes or restores one coherent identity generation; unchanged compatible deployments remain idempotent.

## Requirement 205: Recover precisely quiesced Human processes after export refusal

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The exporter records the exact process identities and prior running state it quiesces, with safeguards against PID reuse.
2. An export failure produces a precise safe recovery path that resumes only those recorded processes; interruption and repeated resume are idempotent.
3. A successful export remains quiesced until an explicit migration disposition authorizes resume or cutover, preserving a consistent snapshot.
4. Empty manifests, failed streaming, archive mismatch and interrupted export leave source data intact and never report a successful migration.

## Requirement 206: Verify the complete integrated CA identity roster exactly

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The expected CA roster is an independently declared exact identity set matching the approved integrated services, including Human KMS roles when selected.
2. Every expected row verifies name, ownership, role, EKU/SAN and trust properties; extra, missing, duplicate and incorrectly typed identities are rejected.
3. Cardinality derives from that independently pinned set rather than an obsolete constant or the producer table itself; assertions are strengthened rather than removed.
4. Existing certificate generations remain idempotent and incompatible material is refused without exposing private key values.

## Requirement 207: Deliver one authenticated kernel identity generation to the registry

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The registry receives replica identity and trust history copied byte-for-byte from the selected kernel producer over an authenticated private handoff.
2. An independently generated history, mismatched identity, partial generation or wrong owner/mode is refused before registry readiness.
3. Replaying or restarting the same handoff is idempotent; interrupted publication leaves the prior complete generation usable or the registry explicitly waiting.
4. The producer order is acyclic and each registry consumer can identify which kernel generation its material belongs to without exposing secret values.

## Requirement 208: Include the complete websearch dependency closure in its image build context

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The x-websearch image stage receives its Cargo manifest, lockfile, crate source and all local path dependencies under the Dockerfile-specific ignore contract.
2. The context excludes credentials, private evidence and unrelated large artifacts while preserving every required source input.
3. The selected build stage produces the expected executable from the selected source revision without copying a stale prebuilt binary.
4. A missing required manifest or path dependency is detected before publication with a precise context error.

## Requirement 209: Credit release evidence only to an immutable clean candidate

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every focused result carries machine-readable start/end source identity, commit, clean/dirty status, command, environment, exit status and retained evidence reference.
2. A passing dirty-tree run remains useful development evidence but cannot increase release coverage or evidence rungs.
3. Ledger validation and report generation reject missing, changed, mismatched or dirty candidate identity for every evidence format, including plain-log gates.
4. A source change during execution invalidates release eligibility even when the command succeeds; prior clean evidence at a different revision is never silently reused.

## Requirement 210: Bind ephemeral runner cleanup to actual job assignment

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Finished-job cleanup resolves the GitHub runner identity and actual assigned job, rather than assuming the provisioning trigger is the executing job.
2. Two same-label runners with crossed job assignments and unequal durations cannot lose a machine while its actual job remains active.
3. Unknown or unavailable assignment fails closed for finished-job cleanup; stopped/orphan policy remains explicit and separately bounded.
4. Unmanaged machines are untouched, repeated reconciliation is idempotent and cleanup records the actual assignment evidence without credentials.

## Requirement 211: Bind manually published candidate artifacts to their accepted provenance source

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The publication workflow defines one explicit relationship between dispatch event SHA and accepted candidate SHA before any artifact is pushed.
2. Either differing SHAs are refused before publication, or a supported attestation mechanism binds the exact accepted candidate source digest; image digest, source digest and signer policy all agree.
3. The earlier-default-branch-candidate case has a deterministic accepted-and-verifiable or pre-publication refusal outcome, never an unexplained failure after promotion.
4. Registry digest, signature, SBOM and provenance verification remain mandatory before moving promotion tags; no source-digest check is weakened.

## Requirement 212: Maintain one current CI build and canary contract in the consolidated specification

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The consolidated CI contract uses repository-root build context with docker/flyci-runner/Dockerfile and docker/flyci-controller/Dockerfile, matching their COPY inputs.
2. Canary verification reads runner_name through the supported REST jobs API and binds it to the dispatched run; stale runnerName/old-context commands are not executable tasks.
3. Archived recipes remain archival evidence with explicit supersession; only spec/paxeer-x/spec.kvx supplies pending task commands for the current system.
4. Recipe checks inspect declared source paths and command contracts without dispatching workflows, changing CI_LINUX_RUNNER or claiming a historical gate reran.

## Requirement 401: Qualify complete successor-contract and issue coverage

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every inherited requirement, acceptance clause and leaf contract maps to a retained capability, explicit supersession or deployment profile; every defined integration requirement has a stable identifier and any conditional behavior has reproduction and resolution criteria.
2. Every advertised public/private journey maps to actual entrypoint, producer, consumer, supported version, authority and required release evidence; no silent unsupported surface or empty passing corpus.
3. Copied historical status, observation and source presence cannot mark an application task qualified or the release ready.
4. Every original acceptance criterion, negative case, supported platform/version/environment matrix cell, minimum soak/fuzz duration and performance threshold remains required; evidence validation does not replace execution.
5. Only completed successful execution whose exact candidate, manifest digest, job identity, artifact integrity and complete coverage pass validation qualifies this gate. A running, missing, failed, cancelled, timed-out or incomplete job cannot qualify it.
6. The agent performs only bounded dispatch reconciliation or completed-evidence validation within its 30-minute task budget; the durable external CI job owns the full declared execution duration.

## Requirement 402: Qualify the complete agent and MCP authority boundary

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Real separate node, daemon, SDK and MCP processes execute the advertised catalogue through authorized served paths; read-only MCP advertises no writes.
2. Bad signature/network/domain, stale generation, revoked capability, insufficient budget, malicious tool input, cross-tenant access and unavailable authority refuse with the correct typed outcome.
3. Lost response, duplicate/concurrent submission, process death and restart preserve exact signed bytes, reservations and exactly one economic effect; altered receipts/proofs and withheld availability never raise verification.
4. Every original acceptance criterion, negative case, supported platform/version/environment matrix cell, minimum soak/fuzz duration and performance threshold remains required; evidence validation does not replace execution.
5. Only completed successful execution whose exact candidate, manifest digest, job identity, artifact integrity and complete coverage pass validation qualifies this gate. A running, missing, failed, cancelled, timed-out or incomplete job cannot qualify it.
6. The agent performs only bounded dispatch reconciliation or completed-evidence validation within its 30-minute task budget; the durable external CI job owns the full declared execution duration.

## Requirement 403: Qualify wallet and Human journeys with independent evidence

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Active Supabase wallet and explicitly private Human profile each complete their own onboarding, approval, money movement, withdrawal claim, emergency exit and managed-agent journeys through real services.
2. Success requires exact verified receipt/finality; unknown/reverted/dropped outcomes, planner/submission mismatch, first deposit restart and parent/inner journey reads remain honest and resumable.
3. Independently approved disclosures bind attestor signing; migrated wallets never use retained whole-key fallback. Export exception is isolated to its authorized profile and post-export signing refuses across restart.
4. Cross-principal access, stale JWKS/revoked tokens, wrong network, wrong asset/domain, unauthorized or replayed signing and missing quorum all refuse; actual approved membership is reconciled without changing the code threshold silently.
5. Every original acceptance criterion, negative case, supported platform/version/environment matrix cell, minimum soak/fuzz duration and performance threshold remains required; evidence validation does not replace execution.
6. Only completed successful execution whose exact candidate, manifest digest, job identity, artifact integrity and complete coverage pass validation qualifies this gate. A running, missing, failed, cancelled, timed-out or incomplete job cannot qualify it.
7. The agent performs only bounded dispatch reconciliation or completed-evidence validation within its 30-minute task budget; the durable external CI job owns the full declared execution duration.

## Requirement 404: Qualify published developer surfaces across all ecosystems

### Acceptance Criteria

6. The agent performs only bounded dispatch reconciliation or completed-evidence validation within its 30-minute task budget; the durable external CI job owns the full declared execution duration.

## Requirement 429: Qualify durable recovery, partitions and authorized sequencer handover

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Inject process termination at every distinct log/index/checkpoint/WAL/publication durable write boundary; each activity or transfer set is fully present or absent, with no partial receipt visibility.

3. Replica isolation, loss, reorder and prolonged sequencer loss never finalize conflicting sequence ranges; only authenticated governance handover permits the successor, with old history readable.

## Requirement 430: Qualify adversarial canonical decoding, signatures and transfer sets

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Malformed/truncated/overlong/deep/noncanonical/mutated inputs deterministically refuse without crash, hang, out-of-bounds access, unbounded memory or state change.
2. Reject malleated/truncated/zero/wrong-curve/wrong-domain/wrong-network signatures over the exact canonical bytes and preserve original admission/fee policy.
3. Fuzz real registered decoders, Programs sandbox/lifecycle/ABI boundaries, grant/receive/payment envelopes and atomic transfer sets seeded from real valid activity corpus; every refusal is attributable.

## Requirement 431: Qualify checked arithmetic and complete sanitizer coverage

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every128/256-bit add/subtract/multiply/divide has exhaustive boundaries and machine-checked exact-result-or-error obligations; every rounding direction is explicit and conservation holds.
2. Consensus paths contain no floating-point computation and every supported module/ABI retains integer metering and overflow refusal.
3. The entire production test/fuzz/replay corpus runs under address, undefined-behavior, thread and memory sanitizers plus a leak checker, with zero errors/leaks/races; disabled checks or unreviewed suppression fails.

## Requirement 432: Qualify native custody, guarantor disagreement, availability and exits

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Against the actual approved native custody/anchor configuration, independently replaying bonded guarantors withhold finality below threshold, publish dissent for root mismatch and produce portable equivocation evidence sufficient for the configured slashing path.
2. Withhold each required availability class and reject possession/finality; corruption refuses. Historical finalized evidence remains verifiable through permitted membership changes and restart.
3. Exercise each supported custody asset deposit, proof trust advance and withdrawal at most once; reject wrong-domain, stale/untrusted, changed amount/recipient and reused nullifier proofs; pending challenge windows never become final prematurely.
4. Emergency exit succeeds against approved real custody with sequencer offline/uncooperative, using last finalized proof and unspent nullifier without new batch or live guarantor assistance; preserve payout delays.
5. Reconcile every custody asset exactly across all account classes and outstanding/settled claims with no reserve mirror double-count; native issuance follows its separate supply invariant and every historical transfer conserves.

## Requirement 433: Qualify explicit migration and continuous shadow equivalence

### Acceptance Criteria

2. Any missing/mismatched custody category refuses the whole import, never partial materialization; locked value becomes real accounts and old receipts remain immutable and non-reexecutable.
3. Where authority migration is selected, continuous real accepted legacy activity is shadowed without modifying the legacy system; every outcome/order/balance/fee/result/receipt divergence blocks promotion unless explicitly specified as an intentional version difference.
4. Fresh genesis release declares zero import and proves custody-based initial funding; this is not evidence of a completed legacy migration.

1. Private settlement manifest binds chain/protocol/release/config, deterministic addresses and runtime code hashes, with exact role completeness and collision refusal.
2. Every external state-changing function has unit/fuzz/invariant/negative coverage including migration replay/partial execution/downgrade/storage mismatch/selector bounds/malicious returndata/decimal dust/cross-chain replay and direct/delegated-call rules.
3. Custody conservation, one-time payouts, governance limits, no arbitrary execution or balance writes and exact historical wire bytes remain enforced; this evidence is never labeled native mainnet deployment.

## Requirement 437: Qualify bounded real-value canary and final candidate identity

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Declare approved real-agent canary duration and exposure cap before starting; general availability requires the full elapsed period with zero reserve discrepancy, unrecoverable crash, missed checkpoint deadline or independently unverifiable receipt.
2. Every mandatory gate binds one clean integrated source identity plus built artifacts and actual deployed service identities; dirty development logs, earlier revisions and image publication alone cannot satisfy release.
3. All mandatory matrix members and private/public scope decisions have explicit evidence; unresolved contradiction, missing independent proof or incomplete canary blocks release.
4. Existing running Paxeer nodes/validators remain an established dependency; inventory LayerX roles/routes/current deployment before asserting all subsystems operational.

## Requirement 438: Record the existing LayerX runtime inventory before deployment decisions

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every subsystem/role in the expected roster has a protected inventory entry with observed identity, exposure, state and dependencies or an explicit unknown.
2. Inventory collection is read-only, omits credential values, accepts running Paxeer as established, and performs no API1/validator relocation or liveness campaign.
3. The resulting deployment delta reuses already-correct services and stops dependent mutations for unresolved ownership, state or membership facts.

## Requirement 439: Freeze the full route and role contract for the integrated candidate

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every active product feature has a registered route/backend/auth/receipt mapping at the canonical router; no declared operation is a stub or unconditional unavailable branch.
2. Expected kernel/supporting-service roster is compared by identity rather than enumerating existing status files; omitted/misowned/misconfigured roles fail.
3. Private ingress, signer, KMS/admin and retired private-network routes cannot be reached through the public mainnet router profile.

## Requirement 440: Qualify a preserved-volume bootstrap with exact producers and complete semantic readiness

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Both fresh setup and retained-volume restart reach the complete expected role roster with real identity/authority/profile/journal inputs and correct private ownership.
2. Missing registry material, principals, Human executor, LNI receipt path or custody profile causes specific readiness refusal, not a green fallback or an infinite opaque cycle.
3. A seeded interrupted migration/rotation is resumed or refused with exact recovery instructions while preserving custody state and existing account/receipt bindings.

## Requirement 441: Bind qualification and publication to one immutable complete candidate

### Acceptance Criteria

1. All release-eligible evidence records require matching clean source identity, artifact digests, exact command/exit and timestamped private logs; dirty logs remain development-only.
2. Manual candidate publication proves the selected source digest even when the dispatch event differs; tags are not promoted before required signer/provenance/SBOM verification.
3. All mandatory application fixes and their focused gates are complete before final aggregate/browser/cluster/replay suites; each final gate runs once at the unchanged candidate.

## Requirement 442: Reconcile and prove the operating CI deployment for the selected candidate

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Inventory shows the actual controller/runner image identities and routing variable before any delta deploy; canonical repository-root image recipes are used if changes are needed.
2. A uniquely correlated canary succeeds on an actual fly- runner using REST runner_name/runner_id, and its actual job machine is retired after completion.
3. Fork PRs and excluded jobs retain their previous hosts; two cross-assigned jobs do not cause active-job deletion; controller credentials never enter job machines.

## Requirement 443: Prove every user and agent product journey through the unified router

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Every subsystem route row has a successful authorized full lifecycle through the canonical router using actual provisioned services and independent terminal evidence.
2. Wrong identity/tenant/network, expired/replayed authorization, unavailable backend and interrupted/restarted operation produce their specified bounded refusal/recovery; no timer or200 substitutes for finality.
3. Wallet Supabase/attestor custody, SDK and MCP daemon authority, native finance/market/Programs, custody, paid search/xweb, sponsored gas, bridge, interop/ramp, events and explorer history are all represented; missing owner/provider inputs prevent full-release success.

## Requirement 444: Issue the final full-product operational release verdict

### Acceptance Criteria

1. The post-deployment inventory shows the approved candidate or an explicitly compatible immutable dependency for every required subsystem/role; all route-matrix legs have matching evidence.
2. Every declared replicated service/region, single-writer state boundary, archive copy/freshness guarantee and retained-state recovery contract has required evidence; private control exposure remains refused.
3. The verdict is full operational only when all mandatory features, owner inputs, scoped implementation gates and final release gates pass; otherwise it names exact incomplete contracts without downgrading the product scope or asserting chain failure.

## Requirement 1001: Non-Authority of the Interaction Layer

**User Story:** As an autonomous agent operator, I want the Rust interaction layer to be structurally incapable of inventing protocol state or asserting an unbacked result, so that every effect my agents cause is a protocol effect and every number they act on is evidence rather than an opinion held by middleware.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any component of the interaction layer effects a change of protocol state THE layer SHALL do so exclusively by constructing a canonical LayerX activity, obtaining a signature over its canonical bytes from a key the LayerX state machine binds to the acting identity, and submitting those exact bytes to the core over the node interface, and SHALL possess no other path by which protocol state can change.
2. THE layer SHALL NOT write, cache as authoritative, patch, reconcile or otherwise mutate any protocol state store, SHALL NOT open the node append-only log or SQLite projection for reading or writing, and SHALL treat every protocol value it holds as a copy of core-produced bytes whose provenance and verification status travel with it.
3. WHEN the layer reports a balance, a transfer outcome, an escrow or budget state, a service lifecycle state, a position, a fee charged or any other protocol fact THE layer SHALL return only values decoded from core-produced bytes and SHALL attach a verification status recording exactly which of sequencer signature, activity inclusion proof, state inclusion proof and checkpoint certificate were verified locally for that value.
4. IF a value cannot be verified to the level a caller requested THEN THE layer SHALL either return it explicitly marked unverified together with the reason, or refuse the request, and SHALL NOT silently downgrade the verification level or omit the status.
5. THE layer SHALL compute no protocol outcome of its own, SHALL NOT apply transfers, evaluate module transitions, derive state roots from activities, or determine admissibility as a decision, and WHERE it estimates a prospective result for user guidance THE layer SHALL label the value a projection, SHALL exclude it from every receipt-shaped structure and SHALL never return it in a field a caller could mistake for an executed outcome.
6. IF a submission is acknowledged, times out, fails in transport, or completes with an indeterminate response THEN THE layer SHALL record the terminal state as unknown, SHALL NOT report success and SHALL NOT report failure, and SHALL resolve the state only by retrieving the receipt for that idempotency key from the core.
7. IF the core returns a failure result code for an activity THEN THE layer SHALL surface that exact code and its canonical meaning, SHALL NOT reinterpret, soften, retry-until-success or substitute a locally derived explanation for it, and SHALL NOT present a failed activity as pending merely because a retry is scheduled.
8. THE layer SHALL NOT hold, mint, escrow, net, aggregate or sweep value on behalf of an agent outside protocol accounts, SHALL NOT maintain any internal ledger of owed or owing amounts that is not a mirror of core-produced receipts, and SHALL make any locally tracked amount reconstructible from receipts alone.
9. WHEN the layer is stopped, its databases deleted and its process restarted against the same core THE layer SHALL reconstruct every protocol-derived answer it previously served from the core alone, and SHALL lose only local artefacts such as policy configuration, subscription cursors, audit history and idempotency records that it declares as local.
10. WHERE a component would need to be trusted for a protocol fact to be believed THE layer SHALL provide the caller with the underlying core-produced bytes and proofs sufficient to verify that fact independently of the layer, and the qualification suite SHALL demonstrate that verification succeeding against a hostile layer implementation that alters the reported value.

## Requirement 1002: The Stable Node Interface Boundary

**User Story:** As a protocol operator, I want the agent layer to reach the core only through one versioned protocol boundary, so that the core can be refactored, re-indexed or upgraded without breaking agents, and the agent layer can never quietly grow into a second implementation of consensus.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE layer SHALL communicate with the core exclusively through the LayerX Node Interface, a versioned request, response and streaming protocol whose messages are canonically encoded and whose payloads are canonical LayerX bytes plus the proofs required to verify them, and SHALL define no other channel to the core.
2. THE layer SHALL NOT link a SQLite driver, open the node database file, read the append-only activity log or its segment files, memory-map node state, or depend on any file layout private to the node, and CI SHALL fail the build when a dependency or symbol reference violating this appears anywhere in the agent workspace.
3. THE layer SHALL NOT declare, generate or bind any struct, union or enum layout from include/layerx, SHALL NOT depend on C field order, padding, packing or type widths, and WHERE the optional C ABI transport is used THE layer SHALL exchange only opaque handles and canonical byte buffers through a published stable ABI header that carries its own version.
4. WHEN a connection to the core is established THE layer SHALL perform a version handshake exchanging node interface version, protocol_version, network_id, node role, chain head sequence, latest sealed batch number, latest finalised checkpoint and the sequencer public key currently authorised, and SHALL refuse to operate against a network_id or protocol_version it was not configured for.
5. IF the core advertises a node interface version whose major component differs from the one the layer was built against THEN THE layer SHALL refuse the connection with an explicit incompatibility error naming both versions, and SHALL NOT attempt best-effort interpretation of its messages.
6. WHERE the core advertises a capability the layer does not know, or omits a capability the layer knows, THE layer SHALL continue to operate using the intersection, SHALL report every unavailable capability explicitly through its own status surface, and SHALL fail requests that need a missing capability with an unavailable error rather than emulating the capability locally.
7. IF the core is unreachable, is behind, or reports a degraded mode THEN THE layer SHALL continue to serve reads it can still verify while marking their staleness with the head sequence and checkpoint they are relative to, SHALL refuse to acknowledge submissions it cannot deliver, and SHALL NOT invent an admission decision on the core behalf.
8. WHEN the layer performs any read whose answer is protocol-visible THE layer SHALL request the accompanying proof material and verify it locally through layerx-proof before returning the value, and SHALL treat a core response that lacks requested proof material as an unverified answer rather than as a verified one.
9. THE layer SHALL define the node interface schema as a versioned artefact under source control with golden encoding vectors, SHALL require any change to it to be additive within a major version, and SHALL run a boundary conformance suite against a real running node rather than against any simulated or in-process substitute.
10. IF the boundary does not yet expose a capability this specification requires THEN THE layer SHALL report that gap explicitly in its capability report and SHALL fail the dependent request as unavailable, and SHALL NOT satisfy it by reading node internals, by reconstructing the answer from partial data, or by returning a plausible substitute.

## Requirement 1003: layerx-types: Canonical Domain Types

**User Story:** As an SDK author, I want one Rust type vocabulary that mirrors the protocol structures exactly and refuses to represent anything the protocol cannot express, so that an invalid activity is unconstructible rather than merely rejected later.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-types SHALL define the LayerX domain vocabulary, including the activity envelope with its exact twelve fields, module payload types, the activity receipt, the 402LXP receipt, batch headers, checkpoint certificates, account identifiers, asset identifiers, result codes and verification status, and SHALL derive each definition from spec/layerx-protocol rather than restating it independently.
2. THE crate SHALL represent every consensus-critical numeric value as an exact fixed-width integer type, SHALL provide the 128-bit and 256-bit widths the protocol requires, and SHALL make it impossible to construct a protocol value from a floating-point number anywhere in the public API.
3. THE crate SHALL represent account identifiers only through the protocol namespaces agent main, agent budget, agent escrow, agent margin, system liquidity, system insurance, system fees, system paxeer reserve and system paxeer withdrawals, and SHALL reject construction of any identifier outside that namespace at the type boundary.
4. THE crate SHALL define result codes as an exhaustive typed taxonomy partitioned by the same domains the protocol defines, SHALL preserve the exact numeric code across the boundary, and SHALL provide a total mapping from numeric code to a typed variant that preserves unknown codes verbatim instead of collapsing them into a generic error.
5. WHEN a domain type carries a length-bounded element THE crate SHALL enforce the protocol declared maximum at construction, SHALL reject an over-long value with a typed error rather than truncating it, and SHALL make the bound a compile-time or constructor-time property rather than a runtime convention.
6. THE crate SHALL make every protocol-derived value carry its provenance, so that a value obtained from a verified receipt, a value obtained from an unverified read and a value produced by a local projection are distinguishable by type or by an inseparable status field.
7. THE crate SHALL contain no input or output, no clock read, no network access and no global mutable state, and SHALL depend on no crate that performs any of those, so that types can be used inside signing devices and constrained hosts.
8. WHEN the protocol adds a module, an activity type or a result code THE crate SHALL accommodate it by extension without changing the meaning of existing variants, and SHALL record the protocol version each definition was derived from.
9. THE crate SHALL provide conversions to and from the canonical wire representation only through layerx-wire, SHALL expose no ad-hoc serialisation of consensus-critical structures such as a derived JSON or debug format used for hashing or signing, and SHALL mark any human-readable rendering as non-canonical.
10. THE crate SHALL be validated against the protocol conformance vectors so that every type it defines round-trips the published vectors exactly, and a vector the crate cannot represent SHALL be a build-breaking failure rather than a skipped test.

## Requirement 1004: layerx-wire: Byte-Exact Canonical Codec

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want the Rust encoder to produce exactly the bytes the C core would produce and the Rust decoder to reject exactly what the core rejects, so that a signature made on this side is valid on that side and no representation gap exists between the two implementations.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-wire SHALL implement the canonical binary encoding of every protocol structure such that encoding a value produces bytes byte-identical to those the C reference implementation produces for the same logical value, and SHALL be validated against the published conformance corpora on every build.
2. WHEN layerx-wire decodes bytes it SHALL reject every non-canonical form the protocol rejects, including non-minimal integer encodings, indefinite-length items, duplicate map keys, out-of-order map keys, unused padding and trailing bytes, and SHALL return the same result-code domain the core returns for each rejection class.
3. WHEN a value decodes successfully THE crate SHALL guarantee that re-encoding it reproduces the original bytes exactly, and the round-trip property SHALL be enforced by both the conformance corpora and a property test over generated values.
4. THE crate SHALL compute activity_id, payload_hash and every other identifier as the domain-separated hash of canonical bytes using the same domain tags as the core, and SHALL be proven equal to the core output for every identifier in the conformance corpora.
5. THE crate SHALL enforce every declared length limit during decoding, SHALL reject an over-long element before allocating memory to hold it, and SHALL bound total allocation per decode so that a hostile message cannot exhaust memory.
6. THE crate SHALL contain no panicking path reachable from decoding arbitrary bytes, SHALL return typed errors instead, and SHALL be fuzzed continuously with corpora seeded from the protocol conformance vectors, with any panic, hang, or unbounded allocation treated as a build-breaking defect.
7. IF the crate encounters an unknown protocol version, an unknown activity type or an unknown field identifier in a consensus-critical structure THEN THE crate SHALL reject the input deterministically rather than skipping or best-effort interpreting the unrecognised content.
8. THE crate SHALL provide the exact byte string that a signature covers for every signable structure, SHALL expose it as the only input a signer is given, and SHALL guarantee that the bytes submitted to the core are byte-identical to the bytes that were signed.
9. THE crate SHALL treat any JSON, text or debug rendering as non-canonical and SHALL forbid its use as a hashing, signing or comparison input, and CI SHALL fail if a consensus-critical hash is computed over anything other than canonical bytes.
10. WHEN the differential harness runs THE crate SHALL be compared against the C implementation over both the published vectors and randomly generated structures, and any divergence in produced bytes, computed digests or rejection classification SHALL fail the build.

## Requirement 1005: layerx-crypto: Keys, Signing and Custody

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want signing to happen where the key lives, under an explicit disclosure of what is being signed, so that neither the daemon nor a compromised tool can obtain signing power it was not deliberately given.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-crypto SHALL implement Ed25519 signing and verification for agent identity over domain-separated canonical bytes, SHALL implement secp256k1 verification for Paxeer-facing certificates, and SHALL reject non-canonical or malleable signature encodings exactly as the core does.
2. THE crate SHALL define a signer abstraction with at least a local in-process signer, an operating-system keystore signer and a remote signer that never exports private key material, and SHALL make the signing interface identical across them so that key location is a deployment choice rather than a code change.
3. WHEN a signer is asked to sign THE crate SHALL provide the exact canonical byte string together with a structured disclosure of what those bytes mean, including activity type, actor, authority, amounts, counterparties, fee limit, expiry and idempotency key, and SHALL make signing opaque bytes without a disclosure impossible through the public API.
4. IF the structured disclosure does not decode back to byte-identical canonical bytes THEN THE crate SHALL refuse to sign, because a disclosure that does not match the bytes is a lie about what is being authorised.
5. THE crate SHALL hold private key material only in memory that is zeroized on drop, SHALL exclude key material from every debug rendering, log, metric, trace, error message and panic payload, and SHALL fail a build-time check if a key type implements an unredacted debug format.
6. WHEN keys are stored at rest THE crate SHALL encrypt them under an operator-supplied secret with an authenticated cipher and a memory-hard key derivation, SHALL bind the ciphertext to the identity and network it belongs to, and SHALL refuse to load a keystore whose authenticated data does not match the expected identity or network.
7. WHEN a session key is issued for delegated use THE crate SHALL require an explicit expiry, an explicit permitted activity type set and an explicit revocation sequence to accompany it, SHALL refuse to issue an unbounded session key, and SHALL make the resulting authority exactly the protocol session-key authority rather than a layer-local notion.
8. THE crate SHALL enforce domain separation for every signature purpose, SHALL make it impossible to reuse a signature produced for one purpose or network in another, and SHALL bind every signature preimage to network_id and protocol_version.
9. THE crate SHALL provide constant-time comparison for secrets and digests and SHALL avoid secret-dependent branching and secret-dependent memory access in its own code paths.
10. WHEN a remote signer is used THE crate SHALL treat a refusal, a timeout or an unreachable signer as a refusal to sign, SHALL never fall back to a lower-assurance key, and SHALL surface the failure without producing any partially signed artefact.

## Requirement 1006: layerx-proof: Independent Verification

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want every proof the protocol offers to be checkable by my own process, so that trust in a receipt derives from arithmetic I performed rather than from the reputation of whoever handed it to me.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-proof SHALL verify a signed receipt from its bytes alone by recomputing its canonical encoding, checking the sequencer signature against the sequencer key authorised for that batch, and confirming internal consistency of amounts, before and after balances and chained state roots.
2. THE crate SHALL verify an activity inclusion proof by recomputing activity_merkle_root from the leaf and the proof path under the protocol domain tags, and SHALL reject any proof that relies on reinterpreting an internal node as a leaf or that carries a path length inconsistent with the committed tree.
3. THE crate SHALL verify a state inclusion proof against a named resulting_state_root, SHALL verify that root against the batch header it claims, and SHALL verify the batch header signature against the authorised sequencer identity for that batch number.
4. THE crate SHALL verify a checkpoint certificate by checking that at least the configured guarantor threshold of distinct bonded guarantor signatures verify over the checkpoint identifier, SHALL reject duplicate signers counted twice, and SHALL report the achieved count and threshold rather than a bare boolean.
5. WHEN data availability bytes are retrieved THE crate SHALL verify them by re-hashing the served bytes and comparing against the committed data_availability_root and the corresponding chunk inclusion proof, and SHALL classify a mismatch as an availability failure with the mismatching commitment and the served bytes retained as evidence.
6. THE crate SHALL express the outcome of verification as an explicit level, distinguishing at minimum unverified, sequencer-signed, batch-included, state-proven, checkpoint-finalised and settlement-anchored, and SHALL never collapse those levels into a single verified flag.
7. THE crate SHALL perform verification without contacting the network, without reading a clock for any verification decision, and without requiring any index or database, so that verification succeeds from bytes on disk in an air-gapped environment.
8. IF any verification input is missing, malformed or internally inconsistent THEN THE crate SHALL return a typed verification failure naming the exact check that failed, and SHALL NOT return a partial success or a downgraded level as though the check had been performed.
9. THE crate SHALL be tested against negative corpora containing altered amounts, altered recipients, re-signed receipts, truncated proof paths, sub-threshold certificates, duplicated guarantor signatures, swapped leaf and node domains and mismatched roots, and SHALL reject every one of them.
10. THE crate SHALL expose verification as a public API usable independently of the rest of the layer, so that a counterparty holding only receipt bytes and the published keys can confirm a payment without running agentd, the SDKs or any LayerX node.

## Requirement 1007: layerx-client: Boundary Client

**User Story:** As an SDK author, I want one Rust client that speaks the node interface, submits activities, tracks receipts and returns only verified reads, so that every higher layer inherits the same guarantees instead of reimplementing them.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-client SHALL implement the node interface for submission, receipt retrieval, verified reads, proof retrieval, data-availability retrieval and event streaming, and SHALL be the only crate in the workspace that opens a connection to the core.
2. WHEN the client submits an activity THE client SHALL send exactly the signed canonical bytes it was given, SHALL NOT re-encode, normalise, reorder or augment them, and SHALL fail rather than transmit bytes that differ in any way from the bytes covered by the signature.
3. WHEN a submission is acknowledged THE client SHALL treat the acknowledgement as admission evidence only, SHALL NOT treat it as execution, and SHALL consider the activity resolved only when a core-produced receipt for it has been retrieved and verified.
4. WHEN a submission is retried THE client SHALL resend byte-identical bytes under the same idempotency key, SHALL treat the return of an existing receipt as the correct outcome of the retry, and SHALL NOT construct a new activity, a new idempotency key or a new sequence for a retry of the same intent.
5. IF a submission attempt ends without a determinate outcome THEN THE client SHALL classify it as unknown, SHALL resolve it by receipt lookup under the idempotency key, and SHALL apply bounded jittered backoff to that resolution rather than resubmitting indefinitely.
6. WHEN the client performs a read THE client SHALL request the proof material appropriate to the caller requested verification level, SHALL verify it through layerx-proof before returning, and SHALL return the achieved level with every value.
7. WHEN the client streams events THE client SHALL deliver them in strict global_sequence order, SHALL detect and report any gap in sequence rather than closing it silently, and SHALL expose a resumable cursor that survives disconnection and process restart.
8. THE client SHALL apply explicit deadlines, connection limits and message size limits to every boundary call, SHALL surface backpressure to the caller instead of buffering without bound, and SHALL never let a slow read starve submission delivery.
9. THE client SHALL treat every transport-level error class distinctly, separating connection failure, deadline exceeded, protocol incompatibility, unavailable capability, core-side rejection and verification failure, and SHALL never map a verification failure onto a transport error or the reverse.
10. THE client SHALL be usable directly by an embedding application with no daemon present, so that the guarantees of this layer do not depend on running agentd.

## Requirement 1008: Agent Identity and Sessions

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want the daemon to model agents and sessions explicitly and bind them to protocol identities and session keys, so that authority is always traceable to a DID and a key the state machine can revoke.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an agent is registered with the daemon THE daemon SHALL bind it to exactly one LayerX DID that exists in current protocol state, SHALL verify that binding against the core rather than accepting it as configuration, and SHALL refuse registration for an unknown or frozen identity.
2. WHEN a session is opened THE daemon SHALL record the agent DID, the tenant, the authority the session may present, the permitted activity types, the expiry, the client that opened it and the policy version in force, and SHALL refuse to open a session that omits any of those.
3. THE daemon SHALL derive session authority exclusively from a protocol session key or capability grant already registered in protocol state, SHALL verify that the presented authority is currently valid and unrevoked at open time, and SHALL NOT invent an authority record that has no protocol counterpart.
4. WHILE a session is open THE daemon SHALL re-evaluate the underlying protocol authority before every write it prepares, and SHALL refuse to prepare or submit under an authority that has expired, been rotated out, been revoked, or fallen outside its declared scope since the session opened.
5. WHEN a session expires, is closed, or its underlying authority is revoked THE daemon SHALL immediately refuse further use of it, SHALL cancel pending prepared activities bound to it that have not yet been submitted, and SHALL NOT retroactively affect activities the protocol already executed.
6. THE daemon SHALL issue session tokens that are bound to the tenant, the agent, the scope and the expiry, SHALL treat a token as an authenticator to the daemon only and never as protocol authority, and SHALL make clear in every response which protocol authority was actually used.
7. IF a caller presents a token for an agent in a different tenant, or a token whose scope does not name the requested operation, THEN THE daemon SHALL refuse with an explicit authorisation error and SHALL record the refusal in the audit trail.
8. THE daemon SHALL support many concurrent sessions per agent and many agents per tenant, SHALL keep per-session state independent, and SHALL ensure that closing one session never disturbs another session sequence, budget accounting or subscription cursor.
9. WHEN a primary key rotation or account recovery is observed in protocol state THE daemon SHALL invalidate every session whose authority no longer verifies, SHALL report the invalidation reason to the affected clients, and SHALL NOT continue to serve writes under a superseded key.
10. THE daemon SHALL persist session and identity records durably, SHALL restore them on restart, and SHALL revalidate every restored session against protocol state before honouring it rather than trusting its own stored copy.

## Requirement 1009: Capabilities and Scoped Authority

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want to hand a sub-agent or a tool a narrow capability and know the narrowing is real, so that the worst case of a compromised tool is bounded by both the daemon and the protocol.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE daemon SHALL express a capability as an explicit set of permitted activity types, permitted counterparties, permitted assets, amount ceilings, rate ceilings, purpose constraints and an expiry, and SHALL reject a capability that leaves any of those dimensions unspecified rather than defaulting it open.
2. WHEN a capability is used THE daemon SHALL enforce that the prepared activity falls inside every dimension of the capability, SHALL refuse on the first dimension that is exceeded, and SHALL name the exceeded dimension in the refusal.
3.
