THE daemon SHALL guarantee that a capability can only narrow the underlying protocol authority, SHALL reject at creation time any capability that would permit an activity type, asset, counterparty or amount the underlying protocol authority does not already permit, and SHALL never present a capability as authorisation to the core.
4. WHEN a capability is attenuated to derive a narrower capability THE daemon SHALL compute the intersection of every dimension, SHALL forbid a derived capability from exceeding its parent in any dimension, and SHALL record the derivation chain so that any exercised capability is traceable to the root authority.
5. WHEN a capability, its parent, or the underlying protocol authority is revoked THE daemon SHALL refuse every subsequent use of the whole subtree, and SHALL apply the revocation to prepared but unsubmitted activities.
6. THE daemon SHALL evaluate capability checks deterministically from recorded state and the prepared activity, SHALL NOT consult ambient context such as caller network address, process identity or wall-clock convenience for the decision, and SHALL produce the identical decision for the identical inputs.
7. IF a capability names a spending ceiling THEN THE daemon SHALL account consumption against it from verified receipts rather than from submission attempts, SHALL count a failed activity as unconsumed, and SHALL never let concurrent uses of the same capability exceed the ceiling in aggregate.
8. WHERE the protocol offers an equivalent enforceable construct, including capability grants, session key scopes, budgets and payer grants, THE daemon SHALL prefer to express the restriction in protocol state so that it is enforced by the state machine, and SHALL record which restrictions are protocol-enforced and which are daemon-enforced only.
9. THE daemon SHALL make every capability decision visible in the audit trail with the capability identifier, its derivation chain, the decision, the deciding dimension and the resulting activity identifier when one was produced.
10. THE daemon SHALL treat a daemon-enforced-only restriction as advisory in its reporting, SHALL state plainly in the capability report that it binds only while the daemon is in the path, and SHALL NOT describe it as a protocol guarantee.

## Requirement 1010: Budgets and Spend Control

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want spending caps that hold even when the daemon is bypassed, restarted or raced, so that a runaway agent cannot spend past the limit I set by exploiting a gap between my controls and the ledger.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an operator sets a spending limit THE daemon SHALL offer to express it as a protocol budget or capability grant so that the state machine enforces it, SHALL create that protocol object through an ordinary signed activity, and SHALL report the resulting protocol object identifier.
2. WHERE a limit exists only in the daemon THE daemon SHALL label it explicitly as daemon-enforced, SHALL state that bypassing the daemon bypasses the limit, and SHALL NOT report it as equivalent to a protocol budget.
3. THE daemon SHALL derive budget consumption exclusively from verified receipts and protocol budget state, SHALL treat its own local accounting as a cache that is reconciled against the core, and SHALL correct itself to the protocol figure whenever the two differ.
4. WHEN a prepared activity would exceed a limit THE daemon SHALL refuse to prepare or submit it, SHALL name the limit, the ceiling, the consumed amount and the requested amount in the refusal, and SHALL leave no reservation behind for a refused request.
5. WHILE multiple concurrent requests draw on one limit THE daemon SHALL serialise the reservation decision so that concurrent or reordered requests cannot exceed the ceiling in aggregate, and SHALL release a reservation deterministically when the activity reaches a terminal state or the reservation window expires.
6. IF the daemon cannot determine the terminal state of an activity that held a reservation THEN THE daemon SHALL keep the reservation held and the amount unavailable until the receipt is resolved, and SHALL NOT release it optimistically.
7. WHEN a recurring budget window rolls over THE daemon SHALL take the window boundary and the remaining allowance from protocol state rather than from a local timer, so that its view of the window matches the deterministic protocol view exactly.
8. THE daemon SHALL support limits scoped to a tenant, an agent, a session, a capability and a counterparty simultaneously, SHALL apply every applicable limit, and SHALL refuse if any single one is exceeded.
9. THE daemon SHALL expose the reconciliation state of every budget, including the last verified receipt applied, the protocol figure, the local figure and any divergence, and SHALL raise an explicit alert rather than silently adopting the local figure when they diverge.
10. WHEN the daemon restarts THE daemon SHALL rebuild spend accounting from persisted receipts and protocol state before accepting a write, and SHALL refuse writes against a limit whose accounting has not yet been reconciled.

## Requirement 1011: Policy Enforcement

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want a deterministic, explainable policy engine that refuses by default, so that I can reason about what my agents may do and prove afterwards why any particular action was allowed or refused.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE daemon SHALL evaluate every write request against a policy set before preparation, SHALL deny by default when no rule permits the request, and SHALL never allow a request merely because no rule denied it.
2. THE policy engine SHALL evaluate deterministically from the request, the session, the capability, the reconciled budget state and the loaded policy version alone, SHALL NOT consult wall-clock convenience, random values, load or non-deterministic ordering, and SHALL yield the identical decision for identical inputs.
3. WHEN a policy decision is produced THE daemon SHALL record the decision, the policy version, every rule that matched, the deciding rule and the reason, and SHALL make that record retrievable for the lifetime of the audit retention window.
4. THE daemon SHALL support a dry-run evaluation that returns the decision and its explanation without preparing, signing or submitting anything, and SHALL guarantee dry-run has no side effect other than an audit entry.
5. WHEN a policy set is updated THE daemon SHALL version it, SHALL apply a new version only to requests received after activation, SHALL retain prior versions for audit reconstruction, and SHALL validate a policy set before activation, rejecting one that fails validation while continuing under the previous version.
6. IF policy evaluation fails, times out or encounters an internal error THEN THE daemon SHALL deny the request, because a policy engine that fails open is not a control.
7. THE policy engine SHALL be able to constrain at least activity type, counterparty, asset, amount, cumulative rate, purpose, capability, session, agent, tenant, time window and required approval, and SHALL express thresholds as exact integers rather than floating-point values.
8. WHERE a policy requires human or external approval THE daemon SHALL hold the request in an explicit awaiting-approval state, SHALL expire it deterministically if approval does not arrive within its declared window, and SHALL never auto-approve on expiry.
9. THE daemon SHALL make plain in every policy decision that policy is a local restriction, SHALL NOT represent a policy allow as protocol authorisation, and SHALL still submit only activities the protocol independently authorises.
10. THE daemon SHALL ship a policy test harness that evaluates a policy set against recorded request corpora and reports the decisions, so that an operator can verify a policy change before activating it.

## Requirement 1012: Activity Preparation and Local Signing

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want preparation and signing to be separate steps with a disclosure in between, so that whatever signs can see exactly what it is authorising and the daemon can never obtain a signature for something it did not show.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a caller requests preparation THE daemon SHALL construct the complete unsigned canonical activity, including actor, authority, account_sequence, timestamp_bound, idempotency_key, fee_limit, payload and payload_hash, SHALL return its exact canonical bytes, and SHALL return the domain-separated byte string a signature must cover.
2. WHEN preparation returns THE daemon SHALL accompany the bytes with a structured disclosure of their meaning, including activity type, actor, authority, every counterparty, every amount, the asset, the fee limit, the expiry and the idempotency key, and SHALL guarantee the disclosure was decoded from the same bytes rather than assembled from the request.
3. THE daemon SHALL take account_sequence and every other protocol-derived preparation input from core state, SHALL NOT guess or increment a sequence locally beyond what the core reports, and SHALL fail preparation when the required core state is unavailable rather than assuming a value.
4. WHEN an activity is signed THE signing component SHALL sign exactly the bytes preparation produced, and THE daemon SHALL verify before submission that the signature verifies over the exact bytes it is about to send, refusing to submit otherwise.
5. IF any field of a prepared activity is altered after signing THEN THE daemon SHALL detect the alteration through signature verification against the exact bytes and SHALL refuse submission, so that a modified activity can never be submitted under an earlier signature.
6. THE daemon SHALL support external signing, in which preparation output leaves the daemon, a signature is produced elsewhere and returned, and the daemon submits without ever holding the key, and SHALL treat this as the default posture for agent primary keys.
7. WHERE the daemon is provisioned with a protocol session key it MAY sign directly, and in that case THE daemon SHALL confine its signing to the activity types, expiry and scope the protocol session key declares, and SHALL record every self-signed activity distinctly in the audit trail.
8. WHEN preparation sets timestamp_bound and fee_limit THE daemon SHALL derive them from explicit caller input or explicit configured defaults, SHALL include them in the disclosure, and SHALL never widen a caller supplied bound.
9. THE daemon SHALL expire prepared activities that are not submitted within their declared window, SHALL release any reservation they held, and SHALL refuse to submit a prepared activity whose timestamp_bound has already passed relative to the core reported batch time.
10. THE daemon SHALL NOT store signed activity bytes beyond the retention needed to complete submission and receipt resolution, SHALL store no private key material at any point in this flow, and SHALL redact payload contents in logs according to the configured redaction policy while keeping the activity identifier.

## Requirement 1013: Submission, Idempotency and Receipt Tracking

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want submission to be exactly-once in effect and honest about uncertainty, so that a network failure costs me a retry rather than a duplicate payment or a false report of success.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN an activity is submitted THE daemon SHALL record it in a durable outbox before transmission, SHALL transmit the exact signed bytes, and SHALL retain the record until the activity reaches a terminal state of executed, failed, expired or superseded.
2. THE daemon SHALL track each submission through an explicit state machine of prepared, signed, queued, submitted, acknowledged, unknown, executed, failed and expired, SHALL record every transition with its cause, and SHALL expose the current state and its evidence to the caller.
3. WHEN a submission is retried THE daemon SHALL resend byte-identical bytes carrying the original idempotency_key, SHALL NOT re-prepare or re-sign the activity, and SHALL treat an existing receipt returned by the core as the authoritative outcome of the retry.
4. IF the daemon cannot determine whether a submission was executed THEN THE daemon SHALL hold the submission in unknown, SHALL continue resolution attempts under bounded jittered backoff, SHALL keep any associated reservation held, and SHALL report unknown to the caller rather than success or failure.
5. WHEN a receipt is obtained THE daemon SHALL verify it through layerx-proof before recording a terminal state, SHALL store the exact receipt bytes, and SHALL make the stored bytes retrievable unchanged by activity identifier, idempotency key and global sequence.
6. THE daemon SHALL provide caller-supplied idempotency keys for its own request surface, SHALL return the original result for a repeated request carrying a key already settled, and SHALL reject with a conflict error a repeated key whose request body differs from the original.
7. WHEN the daemon restarts THE daemon SHALL recover its outbox, SHALL resume resolution of every non-terminal submission, and SHALL neither resubmit an activity already executed nor drop an activity that was signed and queued but never transmitted.
8. WHEN a receipt is later covered by a checkpoint THE daemon SHALL augment its stored record with the activity inclusion proof, the state inclusion proof, the checkpoint identifier, the guarantor certificate and the settlement reference, SHALL verify each before recording it, and SHALL NOT alter any pre-checkpoint field of the receipt.
9. THE daemon SHALL expose the verification level of every tracked submission, SHALL allow a caller to wait for a declared level with an explicit deadline, and SHALL return the level actually reached when the deadline elapses rather than an assumed one.
10. IF an activity is rejected by the core THEN THE daemon SHALL record the exact result code, SHALL classify it as retriable or terminal from the protocol taxonomy rather than by guesswork, SHALL NOT retry a terminal rejection, and SHALL surface the code unmodified to the caller.

## Requirement 1014: Verified Reads: Balances, History, Checkpoints and Proofs

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want every read to arrive with the evidence that makes it true, so that my agents act on protocol facts rather than on a cache the middleware assembled.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a balance is requested THE layer SHALL return the value derived from core-produced state together with the account identifier, the asset, the global sequence and the batch or checkpoint the value is relative to, and SHALL return the verification level actually achieved.
2. WHERE a caller requests a proven balance THE layer SHALL retrieve and verify a state inclusion proof against the named state root and verify that root through its batch header signature or its checkpoint certificate, and SHALL refuse to answer at that level rather than downgrade silently.
3. WHEN history is requested THE layer SHALL return core-produced canonical bytes for activities, receipts and events in strict global_sequence order, SHALL provide stable cursors for pagination, and SHALL guarantee that a resumed page continues exactly where the previous page ended with no gap and no repetition.
4. WHEN a caller re-hashes served history bytes THE layer SHALL have preserved them exactly, so that recomputation reproduces the committed activity, receipt, event and oracle roots for the batches covered.
5. WHEN a checkpoint is requested THE layer SHALL return the checkpoint certificate, its header commitments, the guarantor signature set with the achieved count and threshold, and the settlement reference where one exists, and SHALL verify the certificate before returning it.
6. THE layer SHALL expose the current chain head, the latest sealed batch and the latest finalised checkpoint with every read that is sensitive to freshness, so that staleness is a value the caller can see rather than an assumption.
7. WHERE the layer caches a protocol value THE layer SHALL cache the core-produced bytes together with their verification evidence, SHALL revalidate against the core before serving a value past its declared freshness bound, and SHALL never serve a cached value at a verification level higher than the evidence it holds.
8. IF the core cannot serve a read THEN THE layer SHALL return an unavailable error naming the missing capability or range, and SHALL NOT reconstruct the answer from partial data, from its own projection, or from a previous unrelated response.
9. THE layer SHALL never return a computed aggregate as a protocol fact without labelling it, and WHERE it offers derived views such as totals, spend summaries or position rollups THE layer SHALL identify each contributing receipt so the aggregate is reconstructible and auditable.
10. THE layer SHALL provide an export that emits the receipts, proofs, certificates and headers needed for a third party to verify a stated set of facts offline with layerx-proof and no access to the layer.

## Requirement 1015: Data Availability Retrieval

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want to fetch the underlying data behind a checkpoint and confirm it hashes to what was committed, so that I can replay history myself instead of trusting that somebody still has it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE layer SHALL retrieve availability data by checkpoint identifier, batch number, global sequence range or activity identifier through the node interface, and SHALL return the canonical bytes as served.
2. WHEN availability bytes are retrieved THE layer SHALL verify each chunk against its inclusion proof under the committed data_availability_root and SHALL verify the reassembled bytes re-hash to the committed roots before treating the retrieval as successful.
3. IF served bytes do not verify THEN THE layer SHALL classify the retrieval as an availability failure, SHALL retain the served bytes and the mismatching commitment as evidence, SHALL report which check failed, and SHALL NOT return the bytes as valid history.
4. THE layer SHALL retrieve the five availability classes the protocol names, being the activity batch, the receipts, the oracle inputs, the state-diff material and the recovery metadata, and SHALL report which classes were obtained and which were missing.
5. THE layer SHALL support retrieval from multiple providers, SHALL treat a provider that serves non-verifying bytes as failed for that request, and SHALL never merge bytes from two providers into one unverified result.
6. WHEN retrieval is used to support replay THE layer SHALL emit the retrieved history in a form an independent verifier can consume without any index or database, and SHALL document the exact ordering and framing it produces.
7. THE layer SHALL bound retrieval by explicit size, chunk-count and deadline limits, SHALL stream large retrievals rather than buffering them whole, and SHALL surface progress and partial completion honestly.
8. IF availability data behind an unfinalised checkpoint cannot be obtained THEN THE layer SHALL report the checkpoint as unavailable for verification purposes and SHALL NOT report any fact at checkpoint-finalised level against it.
9. THE layer SHALL record every availability failure in the audit trail with the checkpoint, the batch, the chunk index, the provider and the failing check, so that repeated withholding is visible rather than lost in retries.
10. THE layer SHALL make retrieval and verification available as a standalone operation, so that an operator can audit availability without submitting any activity or holding any key.

## Requirement 1016: Streaming Events and Durable Subscriptions

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want an event stream that is ordered, resumable and honest about gaps, so that my agents can react to protocol effects without polling and without silently missing one.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE layer SHALL stream protocol events derived only from core-produced event records, SHALL deliver them in strict global_sequence order, and SHALL NOT synthesize, infer, reorder or enrich an event with a value the core did not produce.
2. WHEN a subscription is created THE layer SHALL record it durably with its filter, its start position, its delivery target and its owning tenant, agent and scope, and SHALL restore and resume it after a daemon restart from its last acknowledged cursor.
3. WHEN events are delivered THE layer SHALL guarantee at-least-once delivery with a monotonic cursor, SHALL include a deduplication identifier derived from the event identity, and SHALL document plainly that consumers must deduplicate on it.
4. IF a gap in global_sequence is detected THEN THE layer SHALL surface it as an explicit gap event naming the missing range, SHALL attempt backfill from the core, and SHALL NOT continue delivering past the gap as though the stream were contiguous.
5. WHEN a subscriber is slow or unreachable THE layer SHALL apply bounded buffering and explicit backpressure, SHALL retry with bounded jittered backoff, SHALL mark the subscription as lagging with its lag in sequences, and SHALL never drop an event silently to keep up.
6. THE layer SHALL support filtering by agent, account, activity type, module, asset, counterparty and result class, SHALL evaluate filters deterministically, and SHALL apply tenant and scope restrictions before any filter so that a filter can never widen visibility.
7. WHEN a subscription is created from a historical position THE layer SHALL backfill from durable history and transition to live delivery without a gap or a duplicate at the seam, and SHALL make the transition point observable.
8. WHERE events are delivered to an external endpoint THE layer SHALL authenticate the delivery, SHALL sign or otherwise bind the payload so a receiver can confirm origin, SHALL include the underlying receipt or event bytes needed for verification, and SHALL retry failures without duplicating side effects on the receiving side beyond at-least-once semantics.
9. THE layer SHALL expose subscription health including cursor position, lag, last delivery, failure count and last error, and SHALL retain undelivered events only within a declared, enforced retention bound after which the subscription is marked truncated rather than silently repaired.
10. WHEN a subscription is deleted or its owning session, capability or tenant is revoked THE layer SHALL stop delivery immediately, SHALL retain its audit record, and SHALL NOT deliver buffered events after revocation.

## Requirement 1017: MCP Servers and Scoped Tools

**User Story:** As an agent operator, I want model-facing tools that are scoped, auditable and incapable of asserting an unbacked result, so that connecting an LLM to my funds is bounded by the same controls as any other client.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-mcp SHALL expose the agent-api contract as MCP tools, SHALL separate read tools from write tools explicitly, and SHALL declare for every tool the scope it requires, the mutations it can cause and the evidence it returns.
2. WHEN an MCP server starts THE server SHALL bind to exactly one tenant and one scope set, SHALL derive its authority from a session and capability created through the normal daemon path, and SHALL expose no tool outside that scope.
3. WHEN a read tool returns THE tool SHALL return only core-produced values with their verification level attached, and SHALL NOT return a summary, an estimate or an inference presented as a protocol fact.
4. WHEN a write tool is invoked THE tool SHALL follow the prepare, disclose, sign, submit and track path exactly as any other client, SHALL return the receipt or the honest non-terminal state, and SHALL NOT report success before a verified receipt exists.
5. WHERE a write tool would exceed a configured threshold THE server SHALL require explicit approval before submission, SHALL present the disclosure to the approver, and SHALL expire an unapproved request deterministically rather than proceeding.
6. THE server SHALL treat all tool arguments and all model-supplied text as untrusted input, SHALL validate them against the contract schema before use, and SHALL NOT allow instructions embedded in data, resource content or tool results to widen scope, alter a capability, change an approval requirement or redirect a counterparty.
7. THE server SHALL apply the same policy, capability, budget, rate limit and audit path as every other client, SHALL be incapable of bypassing them, and SHALL record every tool invocation with its arguments digest, decision and outcome.
8. IF a tool cannot complete THEN THE tool SHALL return a typed error naming the failing stage and the protocol result code where one exists, and SHALL NOT return prose that a model could mistake for a completed action.
9. THE server SHALL bound tool result size, SHALL paginate large results with stable cursors, and SHALL never truncate a result silently in a way that could read as completeness.
10. THE server SHALL support read-only deployment in which every write tool is absent rather than merely refused, so that a read-only integration cannot be talked into a mutation.

## Requirement 1018: Rust SDK and Generated TypeScript and Python SDKs

**User Story:** As an application developer, I want three SDKs that behave identically because they are generated from one contract, so that a guarantee I rely on in Rust is not quietly missing in TypeScript or Python.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE workspace SHALL define the agent-api contract as a single versioned schema artefact from which the Rust SDK types, the TypeScript SDK and the Python SDK are all derived, and SHALL treat that schema as the source of truth for the client surface.
2. THE Rust SDK SHALL expose identity and session management, capability and budget management, policy dry-run, activity preparation, signing integration, submission and tracking, verified reads, proof verification, availability retrieval and subscriptions, and SHALL be usable with or without a running daemon.
3. THE TypeScript and Python SDKs SHALL be generated from the schema by a generator in this workspace, SHALL be regenerated and diffed in CI, and a hand-edit to generated output SHALL fail the build.
4. THE generated SDKs SHALL preserve the guarantees of this layer, including verification levels on every read, honest unknown submission state, idempotency key handling, typed protocol result codes and refusal to present unverified values as results.
5. WHEN a generated SDK represents an amount or any consensus-critical integer THE SDK SHALL use an exact integer representation in that language, SHALL NOT use a floating-point number for it, and SHALL fail rather than lose precision at the language boundary.
6. THE workspace SHALL run a cross-SDK parity suite that exercises the identical scenarios through the Rust, TypeScript and Python SDKs against the same daemon and asserts identical observable behaviour, including identical error taxonomy and identical verification levels.
7. WHEN the contract schema changes THE workspace SHALL enforce compatibility rules, SHALL permit only additive changes within a major version, SHALL fail CI on a breaking change that does not carry a major version increment, and SHALL publish a compatibility matrix of SDK version against contract version against node interface version.
8. THE SDKs SHALL NOT embed private key handling that exports key material, SHALL integrate with external signers through an explicit interface, and SHALL make the default posture one in which the SDK never holds an agent primary key.
9. THE SDKs SHALL ship runnable examples covering payment with receipt verification, an HTTP 402 style settlement, budget-constrained delegated spending, a service lifecycle interaction and offline verification of a receipt by a counterparty.
10. THE SDKs SHALL document precisely which guarantees are protocol-enforced and which are daemon-enforced, and SHALL NOT describe a daemon-enforced restriction as a protocol guarantee anywhere in generated documentation.

## Requirement 1019: Rate Limits, Quotas and Backpressure

**User Story:** As a platform operator, I want limits that protect the node and separate tenants from each other, so that one agent cannot degrade the service for everyone or push load into the core that the core did not ask for.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE daemon SHALL apply configurable rate limits per tenant, per agent, per session, per capability and per operation class, SHALL apply every applicable limit, and SHALL refuse when any one is exceeded.
2. WHEN a limit is exceeded THE daemon SHALL return a typed rate-limit error carrying the limit, the window, the remaining quota and a retry-after hint, and SHALL NOT queue the request indefinitely in place of refusing it.
3. THE daemon SHALL enforce limits deterministically from recorded counters and the request, SHALL make the decision independent of instance-local timing artefacts where the deployment is multi-instance, and SHALL document the consistency model of its counters plainly.
4. THE daemon SHALL apply admission control to outbound boundary traffic so that retries, backfills and subscription catch-up cannot saturate the node interface, and SHALL prioritise submission delivery and receipt resolution over bulk reads under contention.
5. WHEN the core signals backpressure or unavailability THE daemon SHALL propagate it to callers as backpressure rather than absorbing it into unbounded internal queues, and SHALL bound every internal queue with an explicit capacity and a defined overflow behaviour.
6. THE daemon SHALL bound every request by an explicit deadline, SHALL cancel downstream work when a caller disconnects, and SHALL never leave an orphaned submission whose fate nobody is resolving.
7. THE daemon SHALL apply quotas to durable resources including subscriptions, prepared activities, outbox entries, audit retention and stored receipts, and SHALL refuse creation past a quota rather than degrading an existing tenant.
8. IF a retry storm, a hot loop or a pathological client is detected THEN THE daemon SHALL shed load for that client specifically, SHALL record the shedding decision, and SHALL NOT shed load for unrelated tenants to compensate.
9. THE daemon SHALL never let a rate limit, a quota or shedding cause a duplicate economic effect, so that a refused retry leaves the idempotency record and the outbox in a state that resolves to exactly one outcome.
10. THE daemon SHALL expose current limit configuration and live utilisation per tenant so that a limit refusal is diagnosable without reading logs.

## Requirement 1020: Audit Trail and Observability

**User Story:** As a compliance owner, I want an append-only record of every decision and every mutation attempt with its evidence, so that I can reconstruct what happened without trusting a narrative assembled after the fact.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE daemon SHALL record in an append-only audit log every authentication, session lifecycle event, capability decision, policy decision, budget reservation, preparation, signature request, submission, terminal outcome, subscription change, configuration change and administrative action.
2. WHEN an audit entry is written THE entry SHALL carry the tenant, the agent, the session, the capability, the policy version, the request identifier, the idempotency key, the decision, the reason, the resulting activity identifier where one exists and the verification level reached.
3. THE audit log SHALL be append-only and tamper-evident through a hash chain over its entries, SHALL make any excision or reordering detectable, and SHALL be verifiable by a tool shipped with the workspace.
4. THE daemon SHALL never write private key material, full signed activity payload contents beyond the configured retention, session token values, or unredacted secret configuration into audit entries, logs, metrics, traces or error messages.
5. WHEN an activity reaches a terminal state THE audit trail SHALL be sufficient to reconstruct why it was allowed, what exact bytes were submitted, which authority was used, and what the core returned, using the audit entries and stored receipt bytes alone.
6. THE daemon SHALL emit metrics covering submission outcomes by result class, unknown-state population and age, verification levels achieved, boundary latency and error classes, policy and capability decisions, budget utilisation, subscription lag and rate-limit refusals, and SHALL label them by tenant without embedding high-cardinality identifiers such as activity identifiers in metric labels.
7. THE daemon SHALL emit distributed traces that span the request from caller through policy, preparation, signing, submission and receipt resolution, and SHALL propagate a request identifier that appears in logs, traces and audit entries alike.
8. THE daemon SHALL expose health surfaces distinguishing liveness, readiness to accept writes, boundary connectivity, verification backlog, unknown-state backlog and degraded modes, and SHALL report not-ready rather than accepting writes it cannot deliver.
9. IF the audit log cannot be written THEN THE daemon SHALL refuse the operation that would have been audited, because an unaudited mutation attempt is not permitted.
10. THE daemon SHALL support exporting an audit slice for a tenant, an agent or a time range together with the receipts and proofs it references, so that an external reviewer can verify the protocol facts independently.

## Requirement 1021: Tenant Isolation

**User Story:** As a platform operator, I want tenants separated in keys, data, limits and failure domains, so that one tenant can neither observe another nor degrade another through any path the layer exposes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE daemon SHALL scope every stored object, including identities, sessions, capabilities, budgets, policies, prepared activities, outbox entries, receipts, subscriptions and audit entries, to exactly one tenant, and SHALL make a cross-tenant read or write structurally impossible in the storage access path rather than filtered at the edge.
2. WHEN any request is served THE daemon SHALL resolve the tenant from the authenticated principal, SHALL ignore any tenant identifier supplied in the request body or headers as authoritative, and SHALL refuse a request whose target object belongs to another tenant.
3. THE daemon SHALL isolate key material and signer configuration per tenant, SHALL never allow a tenant to use another tenant signer, and SHALL scope every external signer binding to its tenant.
4. THE daemon SHALL apply limits, quotas and load shedding per tenant so that one tenant exhausting its quota does not consume another tenant capacity, and SHALL reserve capacity for submission delivery and receipt resolution across tenants under contention.
5. THE daemon SHALL scope subscriptions, streams and MCP servers to a tenant, and SHALL guarantee that no filter, cursor, backfill or error message can expose an event, an identifier or an existence fact from another tenant.
6. IF an internal error occurs THEN THE daemon SHALL ensure the error message, the trace and the metric labels carry no data belonging to another tenant, and SHALL NOT include raw object identifiers from a failed cross-tenant lookup.
7. THE daemon SHALL support per-tenant configuration of policy, redaction, retention, verification level defaults and approval requirements, and SHALL apply a tenant configuration only to that tenant.
8. THE workspace SHALL include an isolation test suite that attempts cross-tenant access through every public surface, including the API, the SDKs, the MCP tools, subscriptions, exports and error paths, and SHALL treat any leakage, including a distinguishable existence or timing signal in the API surface, as a build-breaking defect.
9. WHEN a tenant is deleted THE daemon SHALL remove or irreversibly key-destroy its data according to the configured retention policy, SHALL retain only what an explicitly configured legal retention requires, and SHALL record the deletion in the audit trail.
10. THE daemon SHALL make tenancy visible in every audit entry, metric and trace so that isolation is observable rather than asserted.

## Requirement 1022: Deployment, Configuration and Degraded Modes

**User Story:** As a platform operator, I want the daemon to be explicit about its configuration and honest when it is degraded, so that a partial outage produces refusals I can see rather than answers I should not have trusted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE daemon SHALL load configuration from explicit files and environment with a documented precedence, SHALL validate it fully at startup, and SHALL refuse to start on an invalid, ambiguous or unsafe configuration rather than substituting a default.
2. THE daemon SHALL require explicit configuration of network_id, node endpoint, expected protocol version, tenant set, policy source, signer configuration and verification level defaults, and SHALL treat an unset security-relevant setting as a startup failure rather than a permissive default.
3. WHEN the daemon starts THE daemon SHALL perform the boundary handshake, SHALL report the node interface version, protocol version, network identifier, capability intersection and any missing capability, and SHALL refuse writes until the handshake succeeds.
4. IF the core becomes unreachable THEN THE daemon SHALL enter a degraded read mode in which it serves only values it can still verify, marks their staleness, refuses preparation that needs live core state, refuses submission acknowledgement, and continues resolving unknown submissions when connectivity returns.
5. IF the core reports a halted, emergency or data-unavailable mode THEN THE daemon SHALL propagate that state in its own health and read responses, SHALL refuse to report facts at a verification level the core state no longer supports, and SHALL NOT continue to advertise finality it cannot verify.
6. WHEN the daemon is upgraded THE daemon SHALL migrate its local stores forward with an explicit versioned migration, SHALL refuse to start against a store from a newer version, and SHALL never require a receipt, proof or protocol fact to be re-derived from anything other than the core during migration.
7. THE workspace SHALL publish a compatibility matrix of daemon version against node interface version against contract version against SDK version, and SHALL verify at least the supported range in CI against a real node.
8. THE daemon SHALL support graceful shutdown that stops accepting new work, completes or durably records in-flight submissions, flushes audit entries, and exits without leaving a submission whose state is unrecoverable from the outbox.
9. THE daemon SHALL provide an operator surface to inspect and act on unknown submissions, stalled subscriptions, budget divergence and verification backlog, and SHALL make every operator action itself audited and non-mutating with respect to protocol state.
10. THE daemon SHALL expose no administrative path that alters a recorded receipt, a verification level, an audit entry or a protocol-derived value, so that no operator action can make the layer assert something the core did not produce.

## Requirement 1023: Agent Layer Qualification and Conformance

**User Story:** As a protocol steward, I want the interaction layer qualified against the real core under adversarial conditions, so that its guarantees are demonstrated rather than described.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE workspace SHALL run a differential conformance suite that compares layerx-wire encodings, digests, identifiers and rejection classifications against the C reference implementation over the published vectors and generated inputs, and SHALL fail the build on any divergence.
2. THE workspace SHALL run a boundary conformance suite against a real running node covering every node interface message, its error cases, its streaming behaviour, its version negotiation and its capability reporting, and SHALL NOT satisfy it with an in-process substitute for the node.
3. THE workspace SHALL run a no-fabrication suite in which a deliberately hostile node returns altered balances, altered receipts, re-signed receipts, sub-threshold certificates, truncated proofs, reordered events and withheld availability data, and SHALL demonstrate that the layer reports a verification failure or unavailability in every case and never surfaces the altered value as a result.
4. THE workspace SHALL run a fault-injection suite covering connection loss at every stage of submission, process kill between signing and transmission, duplicate delivery, delayed acknowledgement, restart mid-resolution and clock disturbance, and SHALL demonstrate exactly-once economic effect and honest unknown reporting in every case.
5. THE workspace SHALL prove idempotency end to end by submitting the same intent through repeated retries, concurrent duplicates and post-restart resubmission and asserting exactly one receipt and one economic effect.
6. THE workspace SHALL run the cross-tenant isolation suite, the policy adversarial suite and the MCP untrusted-input suite as build gates, and SHALL treat any escape as a build-breaking defect rather than a tracked issue.
7. THE workspace SHALL fuzz every parser and every externally reachable decoder, including the wire codec, the node interface framing, the contract request surface and the policy loader, and SHALL treat a panic, hang or unbounded allocation as a defect.
8. THE workspace SHALL run a soak test that sustains submission, streaming and verification load for an extended period and asserts no unbounded memory growth, no unbounded queue growth, no leaked reservations and no growing population of unresolved unknown submissions.
9. THE workspace SHALL forbid unsafe code outside an explicitly enumerated and justified allowlist, SHALL run the test suite under the address and thread sanitizers where the toolchain supports it, and SHALL fail the build on a sanitizer report.
10. THE workspace SHALL publish, as a release gate, a qualification report stating which guarantees are protocol-enforced, which are daemon-enforced, which suites were run, what the results were and which capabilities the node did not expose, and SHALL make an unmet gate block release rather than being waived silently.

## Requirement 1024: Non-Authority and Receipt-Backed Truth

**User Story:** As a person trusting this app with money, I want the human plane to be structurally incapable of telling me something the protocol did not do, so that what the screen says happened is what actually happened, every time.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any component of the human plane effects a change of protocol state THE plane SHALL do so exclusively by compiling a typed intent into canonical module payload bytes through layerx-intents, preparing the activity through the agent layer's prepare operation, obtaining a disclosure-bound signature from the custody service over the exact prepared canonical bytes, and submitting them through the agent layer, and SHALL possess no other path by which protocol state can change.
2. THE plane SHALL render a success or Done state for a money movement or protocol mutation only when a LayerX receipt verified through the agent layer's proof machinery, or a Paxeer finality proof verified by layerx-paxeer-client, backs that exact outcome, and the component that renders success SHALL be structurally unable to render it from any other input.
3. WHEN the plane displays a balance, a movement outcome, an agent state, a budget figure or any other protocol fact THE plane SHALL display only values decoded from core-produced bytes with their verification status attached by the agent layer, SHALL never raise a verification level itself, and SHALL visibly mark any value it cannot verify to the required level.
4. IF a submission's fate cannot be determined THEN THE plane SHALL present it as still checking, SHALL NOT present it as success or failure, SHALL resolve it only by receipt lookup under its idempotency key, and WHILE it remains unresolved THE plane SHALL disable every control that could duplicate the economic effect.
5. IF the core refuses an activity THEN THE plane SHALL surface the refusal honestly, SHALL state in plain language whether any money left the account, and SHALL NOT retry into a different outcome, soften the result, or present a failed movement as pending because a retry is scheduled.
6. THE plane SHALL maintain no ledger of balances or owed amounts that is not reconstructible from verified receipts alone, and WHEN the human-service store is deleted and the service restarted against the same core THE plane SHALL reconstruct every protocol-derived answer it serves, losing only declared local artefacts such as profile data, notification preferences, journey annotations and audit history.
7. WHERE the plane shows a derived or prospective figure such as an estimated fee, an estimated arrival time or a spend projection THE plane SHALL label it an estimate, SHALL exclude it from any receipt-shaped presentation, and SHALL replace it with the receipt-backed actual once one exists.
8. WHEN a read cannot be served fresh THE plane SHALL serve the last verified value marked with its age and the checkpoint or head it is relative to, and SHALL NOT silently present stale data as current.
9. THE plane SHALL provide, for every claimed outcome, access to the underlying receipt or proof material sufficient for independent verification through the public explorer or exported evidence, and the qualification suite SHALL demonstrate that a tampered human-service altering a reported value is caught by independent verification of that evidence.
10. THE plane SHALL treat the agent layer's contract as its only path to the core, SHALL NOT open the node database, read node log files, or link the node's internal structures, and CI SHALL fail the build when a dependency in human/ violates the boundary rules the agent layer defines.

## Requirement 1025: The Simplicity Contract

**User Story:** As a person with no crypto background, I want the app to expose only ideas I already understand, so that I can hold money, run agents and stay in control without learning a protocol.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE app SHALL expose exactly five top-level ideas - log in, add money, move money, manage agents, see what happened - and SHALL introduce no protocol concept as a navigation destination, decision point or required input anywhere on the default surfaces.
2. WHEN a signed-in user initiates a common action - moving money, adding money, starting a withdrawal, creating an agent, acting on an approval - THE app SHALL complete the initiation in at most three decisions, where a decision is a screen requiring user choice or input, excluding authentication challenges.
3. THE app SHALL keep a banned-vocabulary list in the copy catalog containing at least DID, session key, capability, nullifier, checkpoint, payload, canonical, idempotency, attestation and proof, SHALL enforce it with a copy lint that fails the build when a banned term appears on the authenticated plane's default surfaces - Technical details surfaces and the public explorer plane are exempt - and SHALL express every state in plain language instead.
4. THE app SHALL never require a user to transcribe, retype or manually carry any identifier between screens; every identifier SHALL be copyable in one action, every reference SHALL be a link, and every flow that needs an identifier SHALL supply it itself.
5. WHEN money moves between any two endpoints THE app SHALL resolve the protocol mechanism automatically through the route resolver, SHALL describe what will happen in plain language before commitment, and SHALL NOT ask the user to choose a transfer type, bridge, route or mechanism.
6. WHERE an advanced control exists - verification detail, evidence export, audit, emergency exit - THE app SHALL reach it through progressive disclosure, and the advanced surface SHALL never interpose itself on the simple path.
7. WHEN a custody-boundary journey needs the Paxeer wallet THE app SHALL open the wallet only at explicit signing moments, exactly once per signature the custody boundary requires - on a first journey with binding folded in, once for the binding statement and once for the custody signature - each with a plain-language statement of what the signature does, and SHALL never ask for a wallet signature at any other time.
8. THE app SHALL present every protocol state through the normative status translation table in the design document, and a status string not in that table appearing on a default surface SHALL be a build failure.
9. THE onboarding, deposit, move-money and create-agent journeys SHALL each be completable on a mobile device without documentation, and the qualification usability gate SHALL verify this with real participants against a declared success threshold.
10. WHEN the user must wait THE app SHALL say what is happening and roughly how long it takes, SHALL state when it is safe to close the app, and SHALL never present a spinner without words on any journey surface.

## Requirement 1026: Human Identity and Onboarding

**User Story:** As a new user, I want creating an account to feel like any modern app - an email and a passkey - while the system stands up my protocol identity correctly underneath, so that I am protocol-safe without ever seeing the protocol.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a person creates an account THE service SHALL establish a passkey-backed application identity as the primary credential, SHALL support a fallback credential without weakening the passkey path, and SHALL keep the application identity distinct from the LayerX DID and from any wallet.
2. WHEN the application identity exists THE service SHALL generate the human's LayerX signing keys inside the custody keystore, SHALL register the human DID through a typed intent submitted via the agent layer, and SHALL treat the account as active only after the DID registration receipt verifies.
3. WHEN the DID is registered THE service SHALL pre-register a recovery authority in the same onboarding journey through the protocol's recovery pre-registration mechanism - whose challenge delay applies when recovery is later exercised - and SHALL NOT allow the journey to complete silently without recovery in place.
4. WHILE onboarding is in progress THE app SHALL show honest per-stage progress, SHALL present the account as ready only when ac_2 holds, and IF a stage fails THEN THE app SHALL preserve the journey, explain the failure plainly, and offer resumption without restarting completed stages.
5. THE service SHALL make onboarding idempotent: repeating a stage after a crash, a timeout or a duplicate request SHALL converge on one application identity, one DID, one recovery registration and one set of receipts, with no orphaned protocol state.
6. THE service SHALL store profile information such as display name and avatar as declared-local data, separated from protocol identity, editable and deletable without touching protocol state.
7. THE service SHALL record, for the DID registration, the key activation, the recovery registration and any wallet binding, the verified receipt establishing when each became active, and SHALL surface that evidence under Technical details and in the audit export.
8. WHEN a user signs in on a new device THE service SHALL require the passkey ceremony, SHALL record the device in the session inventory, and SHALL emit a security notification carrying an action that opens the device list.
9. THE browser SHALL at no point receive, derive or cache LayerX private key material, and the qualification suite SHALL verify that the web application bundle and its runtime state contain no signing capability.
10. IF the agent layer or the core is unavailable during onboarding THEN THE service SHALL complete the application-identity stage, SHALL queue the protocol stages with honest pending presentation, and SHALL NOT fabricate an active account.

## Requirement 1027: The Key Custody Service

**User Story:** As the owner of accounts and agents whose keys I never see, I want the custody service to guard signing power at least as carefully as a hardware wallet would, so that custody convenience never becomes custody exposure.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE service SHALL hold every human and managed-agent private key inside a KMS-backed keystore, SHALL keep key material out of process logs, error messages, metrics, traces, backups in plaintext and the browser, and SHALL zeroize in-memory key material on release.
2. WHEN anything requests a signature THE service SHALL sign only through the disclosure-bound path: the exact canonical byte string together with a structured disclosure that re-encodes byte-identically to those bytes, and SHALL refuse to sign when the disclosure does not match, exactly as the agent layer's signer contract requires.
3. WHERE an operation is designated step-up - acting on an approval, changing security settings, revealing a secret, initiating a withdrawal or exit, rebinding the payout wallet, archiving an agent - THE service SHALL require a fresh passkey ceremony bound to the specific operation, and SHALL reject a signature request for a step-up operation without one.
4. WHEN a managed agent needs operating authority THE service SHALL provision a protocol session key to layerx-agentd with an explicit expiry, an explicit permitted activity set and a revocation path, SHALL never transfer a primary key, and SHALL propagate revocation promptly when the agent is paused or archived.
5. THE service SHALL enforce per-principal isolation in the keystore so no request path can reach another human's keys or another human's agents' keys, and the isolation suite SHALL prove it adversarially.
6. THE service SHALL append every signing decision - grant or refusal - to the audit log with the disclosure digest, the operation, the principal and the step-up evidence, and SHALL never write payload secrets or key material to the audit log.
7. IF the KMS or keystore is unavailable THEN THE service SHALL refuse to sign with an honest error, SHALL NOT fall back to any lower-assurance key or cached material, and SHALL surface the degradation on its status surface.
8. THE service SHALL support key rotation for human and agent DIDs through the protocol's rotation mechanism, SHALL present the challenge delay in plain time units, and SHALL keep the superseded key usable only for the window the protocol defines.
9. THE service SHALL bound signing throughput per principal with typed refusals, so a compromised session cannot drain an account faster than limits allow, and the limits SHALL be declared configuration, not code constants.
10. THE v1 service SHALL expose no key export path, and any future export SHALL be specified as its own feature; the qualification suite SHALL verify no API surface returns key material.

## Requirement 1028: Paxeer Wallet Binding

**User Story:** As a user with money on Paxeer, I want to link my EVM wallet once, safely, so that deposits and payouts flow to an address I control while my LayerX funds stay beyond the wallet's reach.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user links a Paxeer wallet THE plane SHALL obtain the EVM key's signature over the protocol's domain-separated binding statement naming the DID and network_id, SHALL submit the binding as a typed intent through the agent layer, and SHALL treat the binding as established only when its receipt verifies.
2. THE plane SHALL treat the bound address as a payout and provenance association only, SHALL never accept an EVM signature as authorisation for any LayerX activity, and SHALL state on the binding surface, in one plain sentence, that the wallet cannot move LayerX funds.
3. THE binding journey SHALL be deferred until first needed - the first deposit or withdrawal - SHALL open the wallet exactly once, and SHALL show the full address with a checksum-styled rendering, copy affordance and QR at every confirmation surface, never a truncation alone.
4. WHEN a user replaces a bound wallet THE plane SHALL require step-up authentication, SHALL submit the rebinding through the same receipt-verified path, SHALL keep the old binding effective until the new receipt verifies, and SHALL emit a security notification with an action button.
5. IF the wallet is unavailable, disconnects mid-journey or rejects the signature THEN THE plane SHALL show a designed state naming what happened and offering retry or cancel, and SHALL leave no partially-bound state behind.
6. THE plane SHALL verify that the address that signed the binding statement is the address recorded in the receipt before presenting the binding as active, and a mismatch SHALL surface as a verification failure, never be silently accepted.
7. WHERE no wallet is bound THE app SHALL present deposits and withdrawals as available-but-needs-linking, with the linking step folded into the journey rather than a separate errand.
8. THE plane SHALL support at most one active bound payout wallet per human account in v1, SHALL display which address is bound wherever payouts are discussed, and SHALL record every past binding with its receipts in the audit trail.

## Requirement 1029: Approval Operations in the Agent Contract

**User Story:** As a human governing agents, I want approvals to be first-class operations of the agent layer contract, so that my app can list, inspect and decide holds with the same receipt-grade rigor as every other operation.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE agent-api contract SHALL gain an approval module - list, get, approve, reject - as an additive change within contract major 1, defined in the schema with golden vectors, and SHALL leave every existing declaration unchanged.
2. WHEN a policy hold requires human approval THE daemon SHALL expose it through the approval module carrying the held activity's disclosure and the digest of its exact canonical bytes, and the disclosure SHALL re-encode byte-identically to the digest's preimage or the hold SHALL be reported as defective rather than approvable.
3. WHEN an approval is granted THE daemon SHALL apply it to exactly the held digest - releasing exactly that prepared activity into the submission path - and SHALL treat any change to the underlying activity as voiding the hold, requiring a fresh preparation and a fresh hold.
4. WHEN an approval is rejected THE daemon SHALL cancel the hold, release its reservations deterministically, and report the refusal to the requesting agent with a typed result, and rejection SHALL be final for that digest.
5. THE daemon SHALL expire unactioned holds at their deterministic expiry exactly as the policy engine defines, SHALL release reservations on expiry, SHALL bound a hold's expiry by the held prepared activity's submission validity window so a granted approval is always releasable, and an expired hold SHALL NOT be approvable, with an approval attempt after expiry returning a typed expired result.
6. THE approve and reject operations SHALL be idempotent under their idempotency keys: repeating a decision SHALL return the original outcome, and concurrent conflicting decisions SHALL resolve to exactly one winner with the loser receiving a typed conflict result.
7. THE daemon SHALL emit approval lifecycle events - created, approved, rejected, expired - on the existing event stream so clients track holds without polling, and SHALL record each transition in the audit trail with its digest.
8. THE generated TypeScript and Python SDKs and the Rust SDK SHALL gain the approval module from the same schema in the same build, the cross-SDK parity suite SHALL cover it, and the compatibility matrix SHALL record the minor version introducing it.
9. THE approval surface SHALL be labelled a daemon-enforced restriction in every report, and nothing in it SHALL be described as protocol authority.

## Requirement 1030: Typed Intents and the Intent Compiler

**User Story:** As the operator of a plane whose users cannot inspect bytes, I want every payload built by one audited compiler from typed intents, so that what was described is provably what was signed.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate layerx-intents SHALL define a versioned typed-intent vocabulary covering, at v1: DID registration, key rotation, recovery registration, EVM payout binding, 402LXP send, 402LXP receive under a payer grant, payer grant registration, budget create, budget fund, budget defund, bridge deposit credit and bridge withdraw request, each intent carrying only domain-typed fields from layerx-types.
2. WHEN an intent is compiled THE crate SHALL produce the canonical module payload bytes exclusively through layerx-types and layerx-wire, SHALL introduce no serialisation of its own, and SHALL reject at compile time any intent whose fields cannot produce a canonical payload.
3. THE crate SHALL ship golden vectors for every intent kind proving intent-to-bytes stability across releases, and a vector change without a version bump SHALL fail the build.
4. THE build SHALL run a differential gate proving that for every intent kind, compile then decode then disclosure re-encoding yields byte-identical payloads through layerx-wire, so the disclosure a human approves is provably the bytes signed.
5. THE crate SHALL reject unknown intent versions and unknown intent kinds deterministically with typed errors, and SHALL preserve unknown-version inputs for diagnosis without executing them.
6. THE crate SHALL accept amounts only as protocol integer types, SHALL perform no floating-point arithmetic, and SHALL enforce every protocol length and range bound at intent construction with typed errors.
7. WHEN the service acts on an intent THE plane SHALL submit the compiled payload through the agent layer's existing prepare operation, SHALL verify field-for-field that the returned disclosure matches the originating intent before any signature is requested, and a mismatch SHALL abort the journey as a defect rather than being reconciled silently.
8. THE crate SHALL ship fuzz targets for intent parsing and compilation, treating a panic, hang or unbounded allocation as a build-breaking defect.
9. THE build SHALL fail if any component of human/ other than layerx-intents invokes payload-encoding entry points of layerx-wire, making the compiler the single payload authority for this plane.

## Requirement 1031: The Human API Contract

**User Story:** As the web application, I want one versioned contract that speaks in journeys and receipts rather than protocol structures, so that the browser can be simple, generated and honest.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE contract human-api SHALL be defined as a versioned schema under human/schema/human-api with explicit major and minor versions, SHALL admit only additive change within a major version, and SHALL publish golden request and response vectors for every operation.
2. THE contract SHALL cover identity and sessions, wallet binding, journeys - deposit, withdraw, exit, move - agent lifecycle, approvals, activity and receipts, notifications, settings and support, and each operation SHALL be expressed in journey vocabulary, never raw protocol structures.
3. THE TypeScript client used by the web application SHALL be generated from the schema with a drift gate that fails the build when generated output is stale or hand-edited, and the browser SHALL call the service only through that client.
4. WHEN a mutation could move money or change protocol state THE contract SHALL require an idempotency key, and repeating the request SHALL return the original journey rather than creating a second effect.
5. THE contract SHALL define a typed error model with stable machine codes, a copy-catalog key for the human message, the trace identifier, and a retriability classification, and no operation SHALL return an unstructured error.
6. THE contract SHALL provide resumable streaming of journey progress, approval lifecycle and notification events with stable cursors, so both shells render live state without polling and recover from disconnection without gaps or duplicates.
7. WHEN a response carries a protocol fact THE contract SHALL carry its verification status and, on request, the evidence reference sufficient to fetch receipt or proof material for export and independent verification.
8. THE service SHALL enforce authenticated-principal scoping on every operation, SHALL bind sessions to the passkey identity with anti-forgery protections appropriate to a browser client, and SHALL rate-limit with typed refusals carrying retry timing.
9. THE contract SHALL version its compatibility in a published matrix - schema version, service version, web app version - and the qualification suite SHALL run the generated client against the live schema to prove parity.

## Requirement 1032: Money Movement and the Route Resolver

**User Story:** As a user, I want to say who gets how much and have the system do the rest, so that moving money is one idea regardless of what the protocol does underneath.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE service SHALL reserve deposit and withdrawal for custody-boundary journeys and SHALL name internal movements fund, allocate, return or transfer in every API surface, log and copy string, surfacing them in the UI as Move money.
2. WHEN a user requests a movement THE route resolver SHALL derive the protocol mechanism from source, destination and relationship - human to agent budget funding, human to agent send, agent to human return via budget defunding, an agent-authorised send or a receive under a payer grant, wallet to human deposit, human to wallet withdrawal - and SHALL compose multi-leg journeys automatically.
3. WHEN a movement is reviewed THE app SHALL state in plain language what will happen, the amount, the fee estimate with its ceiling, the arrival expectation and any irreversibility, before the user commits.
4. WHEN a movement executes THE service SHALL run each leg through intent compilation, disclosure-bound signing and agent-layer submission, SHALL verify the leg's receipt before starting the next leg, and SHALL present per-leg progress for multi-leg journeys.
5. IF a leg lands in an unknown state THEN THE journey SHALL pause in still-checking, resolve only by receipt lookup, resume or conclude honestly, and never re-submit a leg whose fate is undetermined.
6. THE service SHALL persist journeys durably so that a service restart resumes every in-flight journey without duplicating any leg, and the fault-injection suite SHALL prove exactly-once economic effect per leg across crashes at every stage.
7. IF a movement is refused by policy, budget, capability or the protocol THEN THE app SHALL name which limit refused it in plain language and link the surface where the user can change that limit, when it is theirs to change.
8. WHEN a movement completes THE app SHALL show the receipt-backed actual amounts and fees, and the journey record SHALL reference every leg receipt in order.
9. THE resolver SHALL be a deterministic function of its declared inputs, property-tested so equivalent requests choose identical routes, and a route the resolver cannot serve SHALL produce a typed unavailable refusal, never a partial attempt.

## Requirement 1033: Deposits

**User Story:** As a user adding money, I want to sign once in my wallet and watch honest progress until the money is verifiably in LayerX, so that I never wonder where my funds are.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a deposit starts THE app SHALL show the bound wallet and amount, open the wallet exactly once for the custody transaction signature, and from that point run the journey server-side with no further user action required.
2. THE service SHALL track the custody transaction to Paxeer finality, obtain the finalised custody proof, submit bridge deposit credit through the agent layer as a typed intent, and treat the deposit as complete only when the LayerX credit receipt verifies.
3. THE app SHALL present the deposit as a staged timeline - waiting for wallet, confirming on Paxeer, crediting, done - where each stage's completion is driven by its own evidence class and the final stage turns complete only on the verified credit receipt.
4. WHILE a deposit is in flight THE app SHALL state that it is safe to close, SHALL continue the journey server-side, and SHALL notify the user on completion or failure with a deep link to the journey.
5. IF the wallet rejects, the custody transaction fails, a reorg displaces it, finality stalls beyond the expected window, or the credit is refused THEN THE app SHALL show a designed per-stage failure state naming what happened, whether funds moved, and the next action - and a stalled stage SHALL read as delayed with a revised expectation, never as silent.
6. THE service SHALL make deposits idempotent end to end: one custody transaction SHALL never produce more than one credit submission, and resubmission after a crash SHALL converge on one verified credit receipt.
7. THE app SHALL NOT add the deposited amount to any balance presentation before the credit receipt verifies, and the pending amount SHALL be visible as in-flight, never merged.
8. WHEN a deposit completes THE activity feed SHALL show one joined entry spanning wallet to credit with each stage's evidence reachable under Technical details.

## Requirement 1034: Withdrawals, Claims and Emergency Exit

**User Story:** As a user taking money out, I want the timeline and the waiting explained honestly, so that a checkpoint wait feels like a scheduled train, not a lost transfer.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a withdrawal starts THE service SHALL first execute the protocol withdrawal debit through the agent layer and verify its receipt, and the app SHALL state before commitment that a committed withdrawal cannot be cancelled, only completed.
2. THE app SHALL present the withdrawal as a staged timeline - processing, waiting for settlement, ready to claim, paid out - with an honest time expectation for the settlement stage derived from declared configuration, never a hardcoded guess.
3. WHEN the checkpoint containing the debit is finalised THE service SHALL construct the claim, and the app SHALL present ready to claim with the wallet opening exactly once for the claim signature, with reminders if the claim remains unexercised.
4. THE plane SHALL present the withdrawal as paid out only when the Paxeer payout transaction is verified final, and the joined journey record SHALL reference the debit receipt, the checkpoint proof and the payout evidence.
5. IF a challenge window holds the payout THEN THE app SHALL say so plainly - why it is held, what is being checked and when to expect resolution - and IF the checkpoint is successfully challenged THEN THE app SHALL surface the protocol's cancellation of the payout with the funds' actual disposition, honestly.
6. THE emergency exit SHALL be a guided flow under Settings framed as getting my money out, SHALL construct the exit against the last finalised checkpoint through layerx-paxeer-client, SHALL require typed confirmation of its irreversibility, SHALL remain operable when LayerX ordinary operation is degraded, and WHERE the protocol has not declared emergency-exit eligibility THE app SHALL state plainly that the exit is unavailable because the network is operating normally and SHALL offer the ordinary withdrawal instead.
7. WHILE an exit is in flight THE app SHALL show staged progress with the same honesty rules as withdrawals, and completion SHALL be presented only on verified Paxeer finality of the exit.
8. THE service SHALL make withdrawals, claims and exits idempotent and crash-resumable, with the fault-injection suite proving no double claim, no lost claimable state and no journey stranded without an owner.

## Requirement 1035: Managed Agent Lifecycle

**User Story:** As a person employing agents, I want creating, funding, limiting, pausing and retiring an agent to be everyday actions with receipts behind them, so that delegation never means losing control.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user creates an agent THE app SHALL ask at most name, purpose and monthly spend limit, and THE service SHALL orchestrate the rest - agent DID registration, custody key generation, recovery authority naming the human, session-key provisioning to layerx-agentd, capability narrowing and protocol budget creation with initial funding - each step receipt-verified.
2. THE app SHALL present the agent as Active only when every orchestration step's receipt has verified, and WHILE creation is partial THE app SHALL show which steps completed honestly and offer resumption, never a phantom agent.
3. WHEN a user pauses an agent THE service SHALL revoke or suspend the agent's operating authority - session keys and daemon-side permissions - promptly, THE app SHALL present pause as reversible with a plain consequence sentence, and resume SHALL restore authority through the same receipt-verified paths.
4. WHEN a user changes an agent's spend limit THE service SHALL change the protocol budget through typed intents where the limit is protocol-backed, SHALL label any daemon-enforced remainder as app-enforced, and SHALL never describe a daemon restriction as a protocol guarantee.
5. WHEN a user takes money back from an agent THE service SHALL use budget defunding, an agent-authorised transfer or a receive under an explicit payer grant only, exactly as the reclaim decision requires, and the app SHALL show the receipt-backed result.
6. WHEN a user archives an agent THE app SHALL require the funds disposition first - returning remaining balances through legitimate reclaim paths - SHALL treat archive as destructive with a red confirm and typed name confirmation, and THE service SHALL revoke authority, retire session keys and retain the agent's history and receipts read-only.
7. WHEN an agent's keys need rotation or recovery THE service SHALL run the protocol rotation or recovery flow under the human's recovery authority, present the challenge delay in plain time, and keep the agent's identity and history continuous across the rotation.
8. THE app SHALL show per-agent spend against limit for the current period computed from verified receipts, with the reconciliation surfaced honestly if local accounting and protocol state diverge, adopting the protocol figure.
9. THE service SHALL bound the blast radius of a compromised agent to its narrowed capability and budget, and the qualification suite SHALL demonstrate that a hostile agent cannot exceed either through any human-plane surface.

## Requirement 1036: The Approval Inbox

**User Story:** As the human in the loop, I want every request for my approval to show exactly what will happen if I say yes, so that my yes means precisely one thing.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE app SHALL present every pending hold from the approval module as an inbox item showing the agent, the counterparty, the exact amount, the reason it was held, a live expiry countdown, and the budget remaining after, computed from agent-layer verified budget reads and displayed with its verification status.
2. WHEN an approval is opened THE app SHALL render the held activity's own facts - amount, counterparty, asset, fees and expiry - only from the disclosure that re-encodes to the held digest, never from a paraphrase or a separate data source, and SHALL source contextual figures such as budget remaining exclusively from verified reads labelled with their verification status.
3. WHEN the user approves THE app SHALL require step-up authentication bound to the held digest, THE service SHALL grant the approval for exactly that digest through the approval module, and the app SHALL then track the released activity to its receipt like any movement.
4. WHEN the user rejects THE service SHALL reject the hold immediately, and the app SHALL confirm that nothing moved.
5. WHEN a hold expires unactioned THE app SHALL show it as expired with the statement that no money moved, and an expired item SHALL offer no approve control.
6. WHEN two devices act on the same hold THE plane SHALL converge on exactly one outcome with the second decision receiving an honest already-decided presentation.
7. WHEN a hold is created THE service SHALL notify the user with the agent and amount and a deep link to the inbox item, and the sidebar, tab and header surfaces SHALL carry a live count of holds awaiting the user.
8. THE service SHALL record every approval decision in the audit trail with its digest, its step-up evidence and its outcome, exportable with the referenced receipts.

## Requirement 1037: Activity and Receipts

**User Story:** As a user, I want one place that tells me what happened in my words with the evidence one tap away, so that I never reconcile my own money across surfaces.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE app SHALL present one activity feed spanning deposits, withdrawals, internal movements, agent actions, approvals and security events, with custody-boundary journeys rendered as single joined entries spanning their stages.
2. THE feed SHALL translate every state through the normative status translation table, SHALL render Done only under the receipt rule, and SHALL render a refusal with an explicit statement of whether money left the account.
3. WHEN an entry is opened THE app SHALL show what happened in one plain sentence, the staged timeline where applicable, the receipt-backed amounts and fees, and a collapsed Technical details section containing identifiers, verification status, checkpoint linkage and the evidence references.
4. THE feed SHALL group by month with per-group subtotals, SHALL filter by type, agent and date through deferred-apply controls, and SHALL echo an applied filter in the content so the active view is always self-describing.
5. WHEN the user exports activity THE service SHALL produce a statement export and an evidence bundle containing the referenced receipts and proofs in their canonical bytes, verifiable independently of this plane.
6. THE feed SHALL paginate with stable cursors, SHALL survive service restart without gaps, duplicates or reordering, and SHALL reflect a new verified receipt within the declared freshness bound.
7. THE feed SHALL render amounts with sign, semantic color and direction word together, in tabular numerals, under the one amount format and one date format the design fixes.
8. WHERE an entry's underlying receipt gains higher verification - batch inclusion, checkpoint finality - THE entry SHALL upgrade its shown verification status without changing its user-facing state except from Done to Done, finalised.

## Requirement 1038: The Public Explorer

**User Story:** As anyone - user or not - I want to look up a receipt, an account or a checkpoint and verify it from public data, so that trust in this plane never has to be taken on faith.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE explorer plane SHALL be public, server-rendered and deep-linkable, requiring no authentication, and SHALL show protocol-public data only, never profile data, notification content or any declared-local artefact.
2. THE explorer SHALL serve checkpoint and batch browsing, receipt lookup by identifier, account activity views and an evidence verifier that accepts pasted receipt or proof bytes and reports the achieved verification level.
3. THE explorer index SHALL be built by layerx-explorer-index exclusively through the node boundary and data-availability retrieval, SHALL be rebuildable from those sources alone, and SHALL never read node internals, inheriting the agent layer's boundary prohibitions.
