4. WHEN the explorer displays a protocol fact THE page SHALL show the verification level achieved for it, and the verifier SHALL perform its verification with the same proof machinery the plane uses, never a lookup of the index's own opinion.
5. THE explorer SHALL state its own freshness - the head and latest finalised checkpoint it has indexed - on every page, and an index that is behind SHALL say so rather than presenting partial data as complete.
6. THE app's Technical details surfaces SHALL link to the explorer for every receipt and checkpoint they reference, and those links SHALL resolve for a signed-out viewer.
7. THE explorer SHALL meet the same design-system, accessibility and performance requirements as the app plane, rendered table-first for scanning.

## Requirement 1039: One Application, Two Native Shells

**User Story:** As a user on any device, I want the app to feel designed for the device in my hands - not a stretched phone app on my monitor, not a shrunken website on my phone - so that both feel native.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE application SHALL ship a mobile shell and a desktop shell that share state management, data access, journey logic and the copy catalog, while rendering device-specific layouts and device-specific components, and no journey logic SHALL be duplicated per shell.
2. THE mobile shell SHALL provide bottom tab navigation, stacked screens, bottom sheets, full-screen one-decision-per-screen wizards and pinned thumb-reach primary actions; THE desktop shell SHALL provide persistent sidebar navigation, master-detail panes, centered modals, anchored popovers, split-pane wizards and a global command bar with keyboard shortcuts.
3. THE application SHALL implement the pattern-pair mapping the design fixes - navigation, primary action, confirmation, detail, filters, money lists, wizards, search, code entry, notifications - such that every pattern has an explicit component in each shell, and a screen using a raw pattern outside the kit SHALL fail the UI gate.
4. WHEN the server renders the first response THE application SHALL choose the shell SSR-safely from viewport and pointer capability hints, SHALL confirm on the client, and SHALL correct a mismatch without layout thrash or a flash of the wrong shell; user-agent strings SHALL never be the sole selector.
5. THE application SHALL give tablets the desktop layout with touch-sized targets, and every interactive element in both shells SHALL meet the touch-target and pointer-affordance rules of its shell.
6. THE two shells SHALL have feature parity over every v1 journey, and the qualification suite SHALL run every journey end to end in both shells.
7. WHEN a deep link or notification link opens THE application SHALL resolve it to the equivalent screen in whichever shell is active, and links SHALL be shareable across shells without loss.
8. THE desktop shell SHALL be fully keyboard-operable with visible focus order, Escape and overlay dismissal for layered surfaces, and focus trapping in modals; THE mobile shell SHALL honour safe areas, on-screen keyboard avoidance and swipe-dismissal conventions.

## Requirement 1040: The Design System

**User Story:** As a user, I want every screen to feel like one calm product, so that nothing visual competes with understanding my money.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE UI SHALL use the exact visual styling of the owner-supplied @layerx/ui package, including its border strokes, dividers, shadows, gradients, layered surfaces, radii and control treatments, in both the mobile and desktop shells.
2. THE application SHALL consume @layerx/ui as its component primitive source, SHALL preserve the package's public component API and token stylesheet, and SHALL not replace package primitives with locally restyled raw equivalents.
3. THE @layerx/ui token stylesheet SHALL be the authoritative source for the application palette, typography, radii, elevation and motion, and application-level styling SHALL compose those exported tokens without silently redefining the library's visual contract.
4. THE UI SHALL use the package's semantic success, destructive, warning, primary and accent treatments, SHALL never use color as the sole carrier of meaning, and SHALL render money with sign, color and direction word together.
5. THE UI SHALL use one fixed type scale, tabular numerals for all figures, one date format and one amount format everywhere, defined once in the design tokens and copy catalog.
6. THE UI SHALL express every control state - hover, focus, active, disabled, loading - through the corresponding @layerx/ui component variant, with disabled states carrying their reason nearby.
7. THE UI SHALL use the package-defined motion durations and easing, SHALL honour prefers-reduced-motion by disabling non-essential animation, and SHALL use the package's skeleton treatment for loading.
8. THE component kit SHALL be the only source of UI primitives in both shells, and a screen composing raw elements where a kit component exists SHALL fail the UI gate.
9. THE confirmation grammar SHALL distinguish reversible actions - neutral primary with consequence sentence - from destructive actions - red primary - from irreversible actions - red primary plus typed confirmation - and the kit SHALL make the wrong grammar unrepresentable.

## Requirement 1041: Nothing Fails Silently

**User Story:** As a user when something goes wrong, I want to be told what happened, what it means for my money and what I can do, so that failure never looks like a broken app or a lost balance.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE application SHALL ship, for every screen, the full state matrix - loading, empty, error, offline, degraded and, where money is in flight, still-checking - and the qualification suite SHALL enumerate every screen's states and fail on a missing one.
2. THE application SHALL render every error state as a designed screen or section following the error anatomy: what happened in plain words, what it means for the user's money, action buttons - Retry where retriable, Reload where structural, Report always available - and a collapsed technical section with the machine code and trace identifier.
3. THE application SHALL wrap every route in error boundaries rendering the same anatomy, and a user SHALL never see a blank screen, a raw stack trace or an unstyled failure.
4. WHEN connectivity is lost THE app SHALL show an offline banner, per-screen offline states with retry, and honest queued presentation for actions awaiting connectivity, and SHALL never let an offline queue duplicate a money movement.
5. WHEN data is stale THE app SHALL present the degraded state with the value's age and reference point, exactly as req 1 ac_8 requires, in amber staleness presentation.
6. WHEN a form field is invalid THE app SHALL show the inline error at the field with how to fix it, keep the primary action disabled with the reason discoverable, and never fail a submission for a reason it could have shown inline.
7. THE application SHALL give every hand-off to an external surface - the Paxeer wallet, an OS share or file surface - designed in-progress, failure and cancel states, and SHALL treat a blank interstitial during a hand-off as a defect.
8. WHEN the user activates Report THE app SHALL submit the trace identifier, machine code and non-sensitive context with user consent, SHALL confirm the report, and support surfaces SHALL be able to retrieve the same trace the user saw.
9. THE still-checking state SHALL lock every control that could duplicate the in-flight effect, state that the money is safe and that the user should not retry, and resolve automatically when the receipt lookup concludes.

## Requirement 1042: Notifications and Alerts

**User Story:** As a user who is not watching the app, I want to be told when something needs me or something landed, so that agents can work while I live my life.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE service SHALL notify on: an approval awaiting the user, money arriving, a journey completing or failing, a claim becoming ready, security events - new device, recovery initiated, key rotation, wallet rebinding - and service degradation, each with a deep link to the exact surface.
2. THE service SHALL support push, email and in-app channels with per-event-class preferences nested under per-channel toggles and a notification detail level controlling how much financial detail payloads carry, and preference changes SHALL take effect immediately.
3. THE service SHALL attach action buttons to security notifications - review devices, pause agent, open approval - that deep-link into the authenticated surface, and SHALL NOT allow security-critical classes including recovery initiation and wallet rebinding to be fully suppressed.
4. THE in-app notification surface SHALL group by recency, distinguish read from unread, deduplicate repeated events, and on desktop appear as a bell popover with a full archive page.
5. THE service SHALL keep notification payloads free of secrets, SHALL bound their financial detail by the user's notification detail level, and SHALL degrade lock-screen presentations gracefully to non-sensitive summaries.
6. WHEN a notification's subject is already resolved THE tapped deep link SHALL land on the resolved state honestly - an expired approval reads expired, a completed journey reads done - never on a stale actionable presentation.
7. THE approval count surfaced on tabs, sidebars and badges SHALL be consistent with the inbox within the declared freshness bound, and SHALL clear when no holds await the user.

## Requirement 1043: Accessibility, Performance and Internationalization

**User Story:** As any user on any device, connection or ability, I want the app to be fast, legible and operable, so that professional quality is a property, not a marketing claim.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE application SHALL meet WCAG 2.2 AA: text contrast at least 4.5 to 1, full keyboard operability, visible focus, focus trapping in layered surfaces, touch targets at least 44 pixels on mobile, and status changes announced through live regions.
2. THE application SHALL label every amount, status and control for assistive technology such that a screen-reader user can complete every v1 journey, and the qualification suite SHALL include assistive-technology runs of the core journeys.
3. THE application SHALL meet performance budgets at the 75th percentile - largest contentful paint at most 2.5 seconds, interaction to next paint at most 200 milliseconds, cumulative layout shift at most 0.1 - enforced in CI on representative pages and monitored in production with real-user metrics against the same budgets.
4. THE application SHALL code-split by route with declared per-route script budgets, SHALL render the explorer plane server-side cacheable, and SHALL load data with skeletons that reserve layout so content arrival shifts nothing.
5. THE application SHALL keep every user-facing string in the versioned copy catalog with ICU plural and selection support and no runtime string concatenation of sentence fragments, and the copy lint SHALL enforce catalog completeness, the banned-vocabulary list and the format rules.
6. THE layouts SHALL tolerate 1.5 times text expansion without truncation or overlap, amounts SHALL render locale-aware with an explicit currency code, and dates SHALL use the single unambiguous format everywhere.
7. THE application SHALL remain usable on slow connections: journey surfaces SHALL function at 3G-class latency with honest progress, and no journey SHALL require a large asset to proceed.

## Requirement 1044: Security UX, Sessions and Privacy

**User Story:** As the person the attacker would target, I want the app's everyday behaviours to be the safe ones, so that security is the path of least resistance.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE app SHALL require step-up authentication - a fresh passkey ceremony - for approvals, withdrawals and exits, security setting changes, secret reveals, wallet rebinding and agent archive, bound to the specific operation as req 4 ac_3 requires.
2. THE app SHALL render every secret-class value - backup codes, recovery evidence, session tokens - masked by default, SHALL reveal it only after step-up and re-mask it on a timer, and SHALL keep it out of the clipboard except by an explicit user action on an explicitly copyable value.
3. THE app SHALL provide a device and session inventory with per-session revoke, show each session's last activity, and revocation SHALL take effect promptly across shells.
4. THE service SHALL emit the new-device notification of req 3 ac_8 and support sign-out-everywhere, which SHALL also invalidate refresh paths, not only active sessions.
5. THE app SHALL provide a privacy mode masking balances and every derived figure - subtotals, spend bars, notification amounts - with one toggle, persisted per user, applying across both shells.
6. THE plane SHALL emit telemetry containing no personal data, no balances, no addresses and no identifiers beyond pseudonymous ones, enforced by a redaction layer with a CI gate over emitted schemas.
7. THE app plane SHALL enforce a strict content security policy, load no third-party scripts on authenticated surfaces, and pin its asset origins.
8. THE 2FA surface SHALL offer authenticator-app methods with one-time backup codes issued at setup, SHALL present disable warnings with consequence copy, and SHALL follow the security-mutation step-up rules.
9. THE app SHALL make session expiry honest: an expiring session warns before it expires where the platform allows, an expired session lands on re-authentication with the intended destination preserved, and no money control SHALL be operable on an expired session.

## Requirement 1045: Isolation, Audit and Observability

**User Story:** As an operator of a multi-tenant human plane, I want every principal's data isolated, every consequential action evidenced and every failure traceable, so that operating at 1M+ users is engineering, not archaeology.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE service SHALL scope every stored row, cache entry, journey, notification and audit record to its authenticated principal, SHALL map each human principal to its agent-layer tenancy so agent-layer isolation guarantees compose, and the adversarial isolation suite SHALL prove no cross-principal read or write path exists.
2. THE service SHALL keep an append-only hash-chained audit log of authentication events, signing decisions, approvals, journey transitions, security changes and notification dispatches, with each entry referencing its evidence, and SHALL detect and refuse silent truncation or reordering.
3. THE user SHALL be able to export their own audit trail with the referenced receipts and proofs as an evidence bundle verifiable independently of this plane.
4. THE plane SHALL propagate a trace identifier from the browser through human-api to the agent layer and back, SHALL show it on every error surface, and SHALL make it the key support uses to retrieve the failure context the user saw.
5. THE service SHALL instrument journey funnels - onboarding, deposit, move, create-agent, approval, withdrawal - with stage-level outcomes so drop-off and failure are measurable per stage without any personal data.
6. THE service SHALL redact secrets, key material, personal data and financial values from logs, metrics and traces by construction with a gate over log and metric schemas, and a redaction failure SHALL be a build defect.
7. THE service SHALL expose health and readiness surfaces distinguishing its own degradation from agent-layer and from Paxeer-side degradation, and the app SHALL translate each into the honest user-facing degraded states.
8. THE service SHALL declare and enforce retention per store - journeys, notifications, audit, telemetry - with expiry that never deletes evidence still referenced by an exportable audit entry.

## Requirement 1046: Qualification and Release Gates

**User Story:** As the person accountable for shipping this to a million people, I want every promise in this specification demonstrated against real systems before release, so that the gate is evidence, not optimism.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE qualification suite SHALL run every v1 journey end to end - onboarding, wallet binding, deposit, move money, create agent, approval grant and reject, withdrawal with claim, emergency exit - against a real node, a real layerx-agentd and a Paxeer test network, with no in-process substitute standing in for any of the three.
2. THE suite SHALL run a hostile-plane test in which a tampered human-service reports altered balances, altered outcomes and fabricated successes, and SHALL demonstrate that exported evidence and explorer verification catch every alteration, and that the untampered UI cannot render Done without a verifying receipt.
3. THE suite SHALL run the fault-injection matrix over every money journey - crash, disconnect and duplicate delivery at each stage - proving exactly-once economic effect, honest still-checking presentation and correct resumption in every case.
4. THE suite SHALL enumerate every screen in both shells and fail on a missing state-matrix entry, SHALL run visual regression across both shells at the canonical @layerx/ui reference viewports, and SHALL run the copy lint, component-library integrity gate and component-kit gate as build gates.
5. THE suite SHALL run automated accessibility checks plus assistive-technology journey runs, and SHALL fail the build on a WCAG 2.2 AA violation on any v1 surface.
6. THE suite SHALL enforce the performance budgets of req 20 ac_3 in CI and SHALL run a soak that holds long-lived journeys - a deposit awaiting finality, a withdrawal awaiting checkpoint, an unactioned approval - across service restarts, proving no journey is lost, duplicated or stranded.
7. THE usability gate SHALL have real participants complete onboarding, deposit, move-money and create-agent on mobile without documentation, against a declared task-success threshold recorded in the report.
8. THE isolation, custody, no-key-export and telemetry-redaction suites SHALL run as build gates, and any escape SHALL be a build-breaking defect rather than a tracked issue.
9. THE release SHALL be gated on a qualification report stating which guarantees are protocol-enforced, which are agent-layer-enforced and which are human-plane-enforced, which suites ran with what results, and every unmet gate, and a release with an unmet gate SHALL be refusable by tooling, not reviewer discipline.

## Requirement 1047: Clean Bootstrap Inputs

**User Story:** As a developer following the published quickstart on a clean machine, I want the canonical commands to actually start the emulator and connect the CLI, so that the five-minute verified-payment promise is reachable through the published path alone.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a developer runs the canonical local setup from platform/docs/content/install.md on a clean profile THE published command sequence SHALL provision a sequencer seed file and a sequencer trust anchor explicitly - through a documented CLI provisioning step whose outputs the following commands consume - and SHALL reach a running emulator and a selected environment with no undocumented input, wrapper or environment variable.
2. THE CLI SHALL keep sequencer_seed_file mandatory for emulator up and SHALL keep endpoint, network id and sequencer trust anchor mandatory together for a new environment; the repair SHALL supply those inputs and SHALL NOT make them optional, default them to an embedded key, or accept an empty anchor.
3. WHEN the provisioning step generates a seed THE CLI SHALL write it under the profile directory with owner-only permissions, SHALL never print seed bytes to stdout, stderr, logs or JSON output, and SHALL refuse to overwrite an existing seed without an explicit force flag.
4. WHEN environment use selects the emulator THE CLI SHALL bind the trust anchor the running emulator published for its sequencer identity, SHALL verify that anchor against the identity the endpoint advertises before saving the environment, and SHALL fail with a typed error naming the missing or mismatched input when any of endpoint, network id or anchor is absent or disagrees.
5. THE repository SHALL carry a clean-profile bootstrap test that extracts the fenced command block from install.md, executes exactly those commands from a fresh temporary profile against the built CLI binary, and asserts the emulator is reachable, the environment is current and the anchor is bound; the doc and the test SHALL share one command sequence so they cannot drift.
6. THE five-minute benchmark SHALL be measured from a clean profile using only the published commands, and the measurement SHALL be recorded as a gate entry in the executed-evidence ledger with the revision it ran against.

## Requirement 1048: Programs Snapshot State

**User Story:** As a node operator restoring from a snapshot, I want deployed program code to come back exactly, so that the restored state root equals the committed root and program calls keep working after restart.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE snapshot format SHALL carry a kernel-blob section holding every module blob the state root commits - key, length and bytes in canonical key order - under a declared bound on blob count and total bytes so that snapshot_size can account for it before write.
2. WHEN a snapshot is written THE writer SHALL serialise the blob section, SHALL include it in sizing, and SHALL refuse with a typed error to write a snapshot whose blob set exceeds the declared bound rather than truncating or omitting blobs.
3. WHEN a snapshot is parsed THE loader SHALL validate the blob section structurally and SHALL recompute the module subtree root from the parsed blobs, rejecting the snapshot with a typed error when it does not reproduce the committed state root, before anything is published.
4. WHEN a snapshot is published THE loader SHALL replace the kernel blob store atomically with the snapshot's blob set, removing blobs the snapshot does not carry, so no stale executable bytes survive restoration.
5. WHEN a restored node resolves a Programs artifact THE resolver SHALL locate and hash-check it exactly as before restoration, and a post-restore CALL SHALL execute under the recorded runtime version with the same receipt shape as before restoration.
6. IF a snapshot omits the blob section while the parsed state carries a Programs module registration or any committed blob key THEN THE loader SHALL reject it with a typed error naming the missing section, and SHALL NOT publish root-inconsistent state; snapshots of states with no committed blobs SHALL remain loadable.
7. THE qualification suite SHALL prove deploy, snapshot, restore into a fresh node, state-root equality, and a successful post-restore CALL, and SHALL prove rejection of a snapshot with a tampered blob, a missing blob and an oversize blob set.

## Requirement 1049: LNI Pre-Queue Authentication

**User Story:** As the operator of a sequencer, I want an activity authenticated before it takes queue capacity or receives an admission acknowledgement, so that a local process cannot exhaust admission with badly signed activities or be told something was admitted that will be rejected.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the native LNI submit handler has validated framing, role, decoding, network, payload hash and activity identity THE daemon SHALL verify the activity signature and signing authority against current state through the existing native verifier before any queue insertion, and SHALL refuse with a typed authentication result on failure without touching the queue.
2. THE admission acknowledgement SHALL be returned only after signature and authority verification succeed and the activity is durably queued; the acknowledgement SHALL never precede verification, and the LNI contract text SHALL define it as authenticated-and-queued.
3. THE batch and WAL validation path SHALL continue to verify signatures independently; pre-queue verification SHALL add a check and remove none.
4. THE daemon SHALL perform pre-queue verification outside the queue's critical section so that a submitter of invalid signatures cannot hold the queue against valid submitters, and SHALL count authentication refusals per LNI peer on its observability surface.
5. THE qualification suite SHALL prove that an invalid signature is refused with zero queue occupancy, that a wrong authority is refused, that a valid activity is acknowledged only after insertion, and that a flood of invalid signatures leaves the full bounded capacity available to a valid submitter.

## Requirement 1050: Agent Session Revocation

**User Story:** As an operator who closes or revokes a compromised agent session, I want every token that session issued to stop working immediately and stay dead across restarts, so that termination actually terminates.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE session registry SHALL maintain a durable revocation generation per session, persisted with the session record and incremented on close, on authority revocation and on any change of the session's permitted scope, and every issued token SHALL carry the generation it was minted under.
2. WHEN a token is authorised THE authorization path used by the common tenant resolver SHALL require the current session record to be open and the token's generation to equal the session's current generation, in addition to the existing tenant, agent, scope and expiry checks, and a mismatch SHALL be a typed revoked result distinct from expired.
3. THE check SHALL apply at every authorization boundary - reads, subscriptions, prepare, export, approvals and writes - by routing through the one common resolver, and the daemon test suite SHALL enumerate every token-gated operation entry point and prove each refuses a revoked token.
4. WHEN the daemon restarts THE persisted generations SHALL be reloaded before any token is accepted, so a token revoked before the restart remains revoked after it.
5. WHEN a session is closed or its authority revoked WHILE a subscription or long-running operation for that session is in flight THE daemon SHALL terminate it at the next boundary with a typed revoked event and SHALL deliver nothing further on it.
6. THE qualification suite SHALL prove post-closure, post-revocation and post-restart refusal for every operation class, SHALL prove that another session's tokens are unaffected, and SHALL prove that closure of a session under one tenant cannot alter generations under another.

## Requirement 1051: Human Evidence Verification

**User Story:** As a person relying on a Verified label, I want the service to have actually run the verifier against the exact record, so that verified means verified.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the authenticated activity-evidence read decodes a cached evidence bundle THE service SHALL invoke EvidenceBundle::verify against the expected activity digest, the requesting principal, the settlement domain and the receipt authority before assigning any verification status.
2. THE service SHALL return receipt-verified only when the verifier succeeds; on tamper, digest mismatch, principal mismatch, settlement-domain mismatch or authority mismatch THE service SHALL return unverified carrying the typed reason; on verifier error or unavailable authority THE service SHALL return unavailable; and no path SHALL return verified for any other reason.
3. THE verification-status value returned by evidence reads SHALL be constructible only from the verifier's result path, so that no other code in the service can produce receipt-verified, and a compile-time or lint gate SHALL enforce the constructor's visibility.
4. THE same rule SHALL apply to custody evidence rows and to exported evidence bundles, so that no export carries a verified label the verifier did not produce.
5. THE qualification suite SHALL prove that an altered cached row, a row bound to another principal, a row carrying a foreign settlement domain and a row signed by a wrong receipt authority are each returned as unverified with the correct reason, and that a genuine row verifies.

## Requirement 1052: Checkpoint Identity and Freshness

**User Story:** As anyone consuming checkpoint evidence, I want one identity and one acceptance rule for a checkpoint across the node, the agent layer, the settlement contracts and the mirrors, so that the same certificate is either valid everywhere or nowhere.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE protocol SHALL use exactly one checkpoint-certificate domain tag and one guarantor-attestation domain tag for protocol version 2, and the native domain table, the layerx-wire Domain enum and the Solidity constants SHALL be byte-identical for those tags, proven by a test that reads all three.
2. THE native and layerx-proof certificate verifiers SHALL enforce the same header-relative attestation freshness window CheckpointRegistry enforces - attested-at not before the header timestamp and not after the header timestamp plus the maximum attestation delay - and the maximum delay SHALL be one declared configuration value consumed by all three verifiers, never a constant private to one.
3. IF retained checkpoint evidence produced under the version 1 domain must remain verifiable THEN THE verifiers SHALL accept it only through an explicit version-keyed path selected by the certificate's protocol version, never by attempting both domains, and OTHERWISE the version 1 tags SHALL be removed from every verifier.
4. THE repository SHALL carry one cross-language checkpoint vector set - header, certificate, attestations, expected digest and expected accept or reject outcome for fresh, too-early, too-late and boundary attestation times - consumed from the same fixture files by the C tests, the Rust tests, the Foundry tests and the mirror verifier tests, so a divergence fails all of them.
5. THE Solidity header encoding prefix and the native header encoding SHALL agree byte for byte, proven by the vector set.
6. THE settlement domain layerx-proof verifies against - contract address, chain id, guarantor set and finality policy - SHALL be sourced from the one declared configuration the beta contract names, so local verification and Solidity registration verify the same deployed registry.

## Requirement 1053: Hosted Reachability and Readiness

**User Story:** As a tester admitted to the hosted testnet, I want readiness to mean my journey's dependencies are actually reachable, so that green means I can pay and get a receipt.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE testnet-control configuration SHALL address every in-cluster dependency on the port its Service actually exposes, and a static topology check over the hosted manifests SHALL fail the build when a configured in-cluster URL names a host or port no matching Service exposes.
2. THE gateway NetworkPolicy SHALL admit ingress from testnet-control and from every other declared in-cluster caller, and the static topology check SHALL fail when a declared dependency edge is not admitted by the policies on both ends.
3. THE testnet readiness endpoint SHALL report per-dependency readiness for identity, faucet, core, receipt authority, registry, Redis, gateway and the Paxeer boundary, and SHALL compute per-journey readiness - funding, payment, receipt inspection, Programs - as the conjunction of that journey's declared dependency set.
4. THE readiness surface SHALL admit a tester into a journey only when that journey is ready, and SHALL present a degraded journey with the failing dependency named; a global ready state with any journey dependency unreachable SHALL be impossible to render.
5. THE hosted smoke test SHALL verify pod-to-Service connectivity for every declared dependency edge and SHALL exercise the complete hosted first-payment path against the beta cluster, and its result SHALL be recorded as a gate entry with the cluster identity; absent a passing record the hosted surface is below its beta rung and the report is no-go.
6. THE hostname, wire protocol version and network id used by testnet-control, the gateway, the install docs and the beta contract SHALL agree, enforced by the beta contract check.
7. THE repository SHALL carry a beta cluster bring-up script that builds the hosted images from their Dockerfiles, creates or targets the beta cluster, applies the real hosted manifests with beta secrets and a beta CA, waits for every journey to report ready, and exports the endpoint, CA and token values the hosted smoke and the qualification runner consume, so that the hosted surface can be stood up from the repository alone given the owner inputs.

## Requirement 1054: Artifact Publication and Provenance

**User Story:** As a developer installing a LayerX SDK, I want to install only artifacts that were really published from the release revision, and to check their digest, signature, SBOM and attestation myself, so that I know what I am running.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE release manifest SHALL declare exactly the artifacts and ecosystems the release workflow publishes, and platform-release-check SHALL fail when an ecosystem is declared without a publication job or a publication job publishes an artifact the manifest does not declare.
2. THE release workflow SHALL publish every declared ecosystem - Rust, TypeScript, Python, Go, JVM, Swift and .NET - under a beta pre-release version with an immutable digest, a signature, an SBOM and a provenance attestation binding the artifact to the source revision, and SHALL run an install check per artifact that installs it from the registry it was published to and verifies the digest.
3. THE release tool SHALL emit one source-bound artifact manifest listing, for every published artifact, its name, version, registry, immutable digest, signature reference, SBOM reference, attestation reference, source revision and the previous version as rollback identity, and SHALL verify each published artifact's bytes against that manifest before the release is marked complete.
4. THE artifact manifest SHALL be retained as a release artifact and referenced from the beta contract, and the docs SHALL name only manifest-listed artifacts, enforced by the beta contract check.
5. THE aggregate Programs acceptance, the sanitizer jobs, the committed long-fuzz corpus and replay on every supported architecture SHALL run as required gates on the release revision before publication, each recorded as a gate entry; none SHALL remain schedule-only or opt-in for the release revision.
6. WHEN a published artifact fails verification THE release SHALL halt before promotion with the failing artifact named, and no partial promotion SHALL be presented as a release.

## Requirement 1055: Registry and Ramp Crash Recovery

**User Story:** As an operator of the hosted registry or a ramp, I want an interrupted write to leave either a complete accepted record or nothing, so that restart never strands a deployment or corrupts provider reconciliation.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE hosted registry journal SHALL publish a deployment record and its admission proof as one commit unit - one canonical envelope replaced atomically, or a two-phase write with a commit marker - such that after interruption at any step startup observes both or neither.
2. WHEN the registry starts THE journal SHALL load complete units, SHALL quarantine incomplete units with a typed per-unit report naming what is missing, and SHALL NOT reject the whole journal or silently drop a unit.
3. THE ramp journal SHALL validate a provider callback completely - transition legality, evidence, provider sequence - against a staged view before any durable append, and SHALL append the callback and apply its index mutations only after validation succeeds, in one step.
4. WHEN a ramp apply fails after validation THE journal SHALL retain no callback event and SHALL leave the callback and provider-sequence maps unchanged, and a retry of the same callback SHALL produce the same outcome under its callback identity.
5. THE qualification suite SHALL inject interruption at every write step of both journals and prove restart recovery without operator repair, and SHALL prove that replaying either journal reproduces identical projections.

## Requirement 1056: Withdrawal Asset Binding

**User Story:** As the holder of an asset-A withdrawal, I want settlement to be able to pay only in asset A, so that per-asset custody balances are conserved and my withdrawal cannot be satisfied with the wrong asset.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN custody settlement is invoked THE asset module SHALL compare the supplied asset identity with the asset recorded at request time and SHALL refuse with a typed mismatch result - performing no transfer and no state mutation - when they differ.
2. WHEN bridge finalization locates a withdrawal by nullifier THE bridge SHALL derive the settlement asset from the stored withdrawal record, SHALL validate any caller-supplied asset for equality against it, and SHALL refuse on mismatch before calling settlement.
3. THE refusal SHALL leave the withdrawal record unsettled and claimable and the per-asset reserve accounting unchanged, proven by state-root equality before and after the refused call.
4. THE qualification suite SHALL prove cross-asset mismatch refusal at both custody settlement and bridge finalization with no-transfer and no-settlement assertions, and SHALL prove the matched-asset path still settles and conserves.
5. THE per-asset conservation property SHALL extend across request, settle and refused-settle, so that the sum of custody balances plus outstanding withdrawals per asset is invariant.

## Requirement 1057: Human API Error Contract

**User Story:** As a user whose request failed, I want the app to tell me whether to retry, sign in again or fix a field, so that a temporary overload never reads as a permanent refusal.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE canonical ResponseEnvelope in human/schema/human-api/v1.kvx SHALL carry the structured ApiError member for failed responses - stable machine code, copy-catalog key, trace identifier, retriability classification, retry-after where applicable and field errors - matching the encoding rule the schema already states.
2. THE generated TypeScript client and every other projection SHALL be regenerated from the schema in the same change, and the drift gate SHALL fail if any generated output is stale or hand-edited.
3. WHEN the explorer verifier responds with HTTP 429 THE browser SHALL map it to an explicit retryable overloaded state that preserves Retry-After, distinct from refused, and SHALL render it with the wait time and a Retry action.
4. THE explorer verify route SHALL keep returning 429 with Retry-After for overload, and the mapping from HTTP status to client state SHALL be tested for 401, 409, 429, 503 and other 5xx so that only a genuine verification failure renders as refused.
5. THE golden request and response vectors SHALL include failed responses carrying the structured error for every operation, and the generated client SHALL decode them into the typed error model.

## Requirement 1058: Executed Qualification Evidence

**User Story:** As the person deciding go or no-go, I want to see what was actually run, on which revision, in which environment, with which result, so that a detailed plan is never mistaken for a passed gate.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE feature qualification ledger SHALL distinguish observation records - assumptions, unrelated failures, conflicts - from gate records, and a gate record SHALL carry the task, the requirements it qualifies, the revision, the exact command, the environment identity, the start time, the outcome as pass, fail or blocked, and the retained evidence path.
2. A gate record SHALL be written only by executing the command it names, and a ledger check SHALL fail when a gate's revision is not a commit in the repository, its command is not an existing make target or script, its evidence path does not exist, its outcome is outside the declared vocabulary, or - where the evidence is a qualification runner status or report - the runner's recorded source revision differs from the record's revision or its source identity shows a dirty tree.
3. THE go/no-go report SHALL be generated from gate records only, SHALL state for every beta surface the highest evidence rung reached against its required beta rung, and SHALL derive no rung from task status, observation narrative or documentation.
4. THE required beta gates SHALL be executed on one immutable revision against the beta stack: the builds; focused negative and fault tests for every register item - invalid LNI signature and queue exhaustion, post-closure, post-revocation and post-restart token use, evidence tamper and principal mismatch, snapshot restore with non-empty blobs, cross-asset withdrawal, registry and ramp interruption, checkpoint freshness bounds; the beta-qualify runner gate covering the human service and web journeys, platform build, lint, tests, SDK conformance, middleware, docs samples, hosted smoke, agent install, emulator conformance, real agent-framework, iOS and Android integrations, Programs tests, interop tests, migration testnets, ramp sandboxes and the release check; the adoption, Programs, interop and multichain external evidence produced by the in-repository driver; the clean-profile end-to-end verified payment with independent receipt verification; the cross-language vectors; artifact publication and verification; and the hosted smoke with cluster identity.
5. THE work the observations in spec/layerx-platform/qualification.kvx describe as designed or simulated but unexecuted - registry isolation and bearer refusal, mTLS and TLS boundaries, cgroup and isolated executor limits, crash and deployment recovery, host provisioning - SHALL be executed on beta infrastructure through the existing boundary, fault-injection and provisioning scripts and linked from gate records; none SHALL be rewritten to read as executed, and a case that cannot execute SHALL be recorded blocked with the owner input named.
6. THE report SHALL list every stop condition - clean bootstrap, independent receipt verification, unknown-outcome reconciliation, effective revocation, journey-transitive readiness, artifact identity, every surface at its beta rung, scope closure - with whether it is clear and the gate record that clears it, and a beta invitation SHALL require every stop condition clear and a recorded owner go decision.

## Requirement 1059: One Canonical Beta Contract

**User Story:** As a beta user or operator, I want one document that says exactly what the beta supports, how it differs from production, and what was proven, and I want every other source to agree with it, so that no doc, manifest or workflow claims more than the executed evidence.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE repository SHALL carry one canonical beta contract naming every surface and journey of the system, the beta endpoints and hostnames, the network id, the wire protocol version, the beta CA, the artifact set by reference to the artifact manifest, the required beta rung and the reached rung per surface, the unknown-state behaviour, the architecture summary, the external dependencies with their beta counterparts - test networks, sandboxes, Paxeer testnet, beta registries - and the beta-versus-production differences.
2. THE contract SHALL be the only source for those values, and the install docs, the hosted manifests, the release manifest, the release workflow and the hosted status surface SHALL be checked against it by a static consistency check that fails the build on disagreement.
3. THE beta-versus-production differences SHALL be limited to polish - UI polish, visual regression, accessibility, usability, performance budgets and soak - an external security audit, and production infrastructure and certification; the contract SHALL mark no functional surface as unsupported, and the consistency check SHALL fail if any surface is listed below its required beta rung while the contract claims the beta is ready.
4. THE contract SHALL state each surface's reached evidence rung exactly as the go/no-go report records it, and the consistency check SHALL fail when the contract and the report disagree.
5. THE docs SHALL describe every journey the contract names as available exactly as the beta stack provides it, and SHALL describe nothing the report has not proven, enforced by the same check.

## Requirement 1060: Trusted-Boundary Services Built From the Repository

**User Story:** As the operator standing the beta up, I want every service the hosted manifests address - the pending-release core and its admin plane, identity, the receipt authority, the agent boundary and the Paxeer boundary - to be built from this repository with real code paths behind them, so that the beta cluster comes up from the repository alone and every journey exercises the real core, the real daemon and a real Paxeer chain.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE repository SHALL build a layerx-node image from cmd/layerxd, cmd/layerx-genesis and cmd/layerxctl, and a node StatefulSet in namespace layerx-testnet that runs the sequencer daemon, the independent receipt-authority replica and the boundary processes in one pod with the pod label layerx-plane: trusted-boundary, bootstrapped from a genesis manifest the bring-up generates, holding a treasury account whose key the admin plane controls, on a persistent volume, with the LNI socket and the loopback listeners reachable only inside the pod.
2. THE layerx-pending-core Service on port 9443 SHALL answer an unauthenticated GET /readyz with 200 and the body {ready, network_id, wire_version, synchronous_receipts, state_snapshot} the gateway parses, only when the daemon handshake, the receipt-authority replica and the durable log are live, and SHALL serve the protocol surface the CLI and the SDKs address at a node endpoint - sequencer identity, activity submission, receipt lookup, state and account reads, program call, simulate, activity status and registry reads - by submitting canonical bytes over the LNI and relaying reads to the daemon, never by executing a transition in-process.
3. THE layerx-pending-core-admin Service on port 9444 SHALL require the backend admin bearer token and an Idempotency-Key on every request, SHALL fund by building, signing with the treasury key and submitting a real SEND over the LNI and answering {funding_id, state: funded, transaction_id} only from the resulting receipt, SHALL reset by stopping the daemons, discarding the data volume contents, rebuilding genesis and restarting, answering {state: reset, reset_id}, SHALL answer admin refusals caused by the request with 4xx and durable-storage faults (journal write or lock failure) with 503 with no state change, and SHALL make a repeated Idempotency-Key return the first outcome without a second economic effect.
4. THE layerx-receipt-authority Service on port 9443 SHALL serve GET /v1/authorized-batches/by-activity/{activity_id} with the eight fields {activity_id, batch_id, asset, previous_state_root, resulting_state_root, sequencer_public_key, network_id, wire_version}, plus batch_evidence only when the batch carries an occupancy-maintenance receipt, containing the maintained batch identity and proof the consumer verifies, deriving batch_id, both roots and the sequencer key from the replica's verified batch evidence and the receipt exactly as layerx-agentd's protocol_evidence does, SHALL relay GET /v1/batches/{batch_id}/receipt-authority to the replica unchanged, SHALL answer GET /readyz with {ready, network_id, wire_version} for the gateway and with 200 for an unauthenticated probe, and SHALL never answer from the sequencer daemon's own store.
5. THE layerx-agent-boundary Service on port 9443 SHALL serve the component contract the gateway and the registry consume - /readyz, POST /v1/activities, POST /v1/programs/call, POST /v1/programs/simulate, GET /v1/programs/activities/{id}, GET /v1/receipts/{id} with result-wrapped bodies and the five account-state read routes relayed to the daemon - over TLS that accepts the gateway's client certificate and two distinct bearer tokens, SHALL submit canonical bytes over the LNI exactly once per idempotency key and answer 202 when the outcome is unknown, SHALL map a typed daemon refusal to 4xx and unavailability to 503, and SHALL answer a request the LNI cannot serve with a typed 503 rather than an invented result.
6. THE layerx-identity Service on port 9443 SHALL hold principals and sessions in a durable store, SHALL mint sessions only through an authenticated provisioning route, SHALL introspect on POST /v1/sessions/introspect and POST /v1/introspect returning per calling service exactly the body that caller parses - the gateway's {active, sub, allowed_signer_public_keys}, the developer plane's {active, sub, csrf_token}, the faucet's {active, sub} and the ramp's audience-bound body - selected by the presented service token, SHALL revoke sessions so that a revoked or expired token introspects inactive, and SHALL answer an unauthenticated GET /readyz with 200 only when the store is writable.
7. THE paxeer-boundary Service on port 9443 SHALL front a real paxd node running the Paxeer EVM chain in the cluster, SHALL answer GET /readyz with 200 only when eth_chainId succeeds against the node and equals the configured chain id, SHALL relay Ethereum JSON-RPC posted to its root to that single node with bounded bodies and the request id preserved, SHALL present a certificate chaining to the beta CA, and the bring-up SHALL deploy the settlement contracts to that chain and record the chain id and the GuarantorBond address in contracts/config/checkpoint-settlement.json as the beta settlement domain.
8. THE bring-up script SHALL build every one of these images from the repository, issue their certificates and tokens from the beta CA, apply their manifests before the existing ones, and remove LAYERX_BETA_EXTERNAL_MANIFESTS as an owner input; the static topology check SHALL check their Services and NetworkPolicies as in-repository edges; the beta contract SHALL list each as a hosted surface; and the qualification URL exports SHALL point at the surfaces the in-repository driver actually exercises.

## Requirement 1061: Public relay and archive nodes

**User Story:** As an independent operator, I can join the existing LayerX network, forward users' signed activities, retain complete canonical history and serve public reads without executing or ordering activities.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Expose versioned public HTTPS synchronization of the signed genesis manifest, genesis snapshot, head and complete canonical batch bodies including every activity, receipt and maintenance record. Preserve native canonical encodings and verify signatures and all committed section roots using native codecs.
2. Provide layerxd --relay-archive CONFIG with independently pinned network, genesis manifest digest and sequencer public identity. Validate downloaded genesis and snapshot before accepting history; never trust an upstream's self-declared identity.
3. Backfill from genesis and continuously follow batches in order. Atomically persist raw bytes, indexes and synchronization position, reject gaps, root discontinuity, tampering and conflicting history, and resume after interruption without duplication.
4. Serve bounded cursor-paginated complete activity, receipt and batch history and filters for actor, account, module and batch. Preserve raw bytes for every protocol kind and label cryptographic inclusion separately from execution replay or settlement finality.
5. Discover compatible peers with bounded advertisements and expiration. Peer discovery cannot replace trust pins, redirect submission credentials or trigger arbitrary private-network probes.
6. Forward original signed activities with durable idempotency and bounded upstream failover, retrying only the identical bytes after transport or availability failure. Preserve definitive refusals and unknown outcomes. Never sign or rebuild activities on behalf of users.
7. Ship an integrity-pinned operator installer, example configuration, systemd and container deployment paths, and an executable real-process integration gate proving installation, bootstrap, backfill, live sync, public reads, forwarding, failover, restart and negative integrity cases.

## Requirement 1062: Beta Surface Expansion

**User Story:** As a user or agent choosing LayerX over a general-purpose chain, I want non-fungible assets, k-of-n and time-locked authority, human-readable names, a program-readable price feed, spot swaps, an uncapped token path and self-custody of my own key, so that the things I can do on a general chain I can also do here, while ordering, fees, guarantors and governance stay exactly as the protocol spec locks them.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE programs SDK and registry SHALL define an LXT721 non-fungible interface (mint, transfer, approve, set_approval_for_all, owner_of, balance_of, token_uri, total_supply, metadata) next to LXT20, with a reference WASM program, a registry-enforced reference interface and a registry test that mirrors lxt20_reference, and ownership SHALL only change through the program's own storage under its namespace; no protocol change.
2. THE authority table SHALL gain two additive kinds: LXP_AUTHORITY_KIND_MULTISIG binding a grant to a k-of-n signer set whose approvals are collected as ordinary signed approvals and resolved by the one common resolver, and LXP_AUTHORITY_KIND_TIMELOCK binding a grant to an earliest-execution sequence or timestamp; existing kinds, encodings, grant ids and resolver results SHALL be byte-identical for existing grants, and a multisig grant below threshold or a timelock before maturity SHALL resolve to a typed refusal, never to success or to an unknown outcome.
3. THE programs SDK SHALL ship a naming registry reference program mapping a UTF-8 NFC-normalised name (3-63 chars, [a-z0-9-], no leading or trailing hyphen) to a DID with register, transfer, renew, resolve and reverse-resolve entry points, first-come ownership, an expiry paid in occupancy through fund_program_402, and a registry test; the human explorer lookup SHALL resolve a name through the program read path when present.
4. THE programs ABI SHALL allocate guest ABI v3 whose new layerx_v3 namespace holds the single host function oracle_read(market_id, out), leaving the frozen layerx_v2 vector and checksum byte-identical, and oracle_read SHALL return the latest committed perps oracle observation (price, timestamp, sequence, source set digest) for a market from the oracle store the batch header already commits under oracle_root, refusing with a typed result when the market is unknown or halted; validate.rs, ABI_MANIFEST, the C host binding, the Rust SDK wrapper and programs-abi-drift SHALL all agree, and a native test SHALL prove a program reads the same observation the perps engine used.
5. THE programs SDK SHALL ship a constant-product swap reference program over two LXT20 tokens or one LXT20 token and one 402LXP asset with add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, swap_exact_in, quote and reserves entry points, LP shares as an LXT20 program token, all value moved only through transfer_program_402 and program_call to the LXT20 programs, a slippage bound the caller supplies and a conservation test in programs/tests/conservation; the program holds no authority beyond its own derived account.
6. THE asset registry SHALL hold at least 1024 assets: LX_ASSET_REGISTRY_CAPACITY rises to 1024 with the state encoding, reserve attestation, genesis builder and every static array sized from it updated so that existing fixtures with fewer than 64 assets decode byte-identically and test-asset-registry, test-asset-reserve and the genesis builder pass; the gateway lx_listAssets SHALL paginate.
7. THE human service SHALL make self-custody the default posture: onboarding SHALL offer key export as the first path and custodial holding as an explicit opt-in; export SHALL be a step-up ceremony in the secret-reveal class bound to one operation digest that returns the DID primary key exactly once, records a durable audit event, and marks the identity self-custodied so the KMS refuses to sign for it afterwards; the existing no-key-export suite SHALL be rewritten to assert that export happens only through this ceremony and never through any other route, and spec/layerx-platform/spec.kvx [contract_context.103.decision] custody and v1_scope SHALL be updated to state the new default.

## Requirement 1063: Paxeer X Fork Surface

**User Story:** As a wallet, trader, token creator, bridge user or agent on Paxeer X, I want the exchange, bridge, launchpad and account history to be native to the chain on the Paxeer side and served by the LayerX kernel and services on the LayerX side, so that one account, one seed and one data source cover both halves of the network without Solidity middlemen or trusted upgrade keys.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE Paxeer node SHALL expose a layerxexchange precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001015 backed by a layerxexchange module: depositMargin, withdrawMargin, placeOrder, cancelOrder and requestSettlement SHALL move funds only through the layerxcustody module account and SHALL emit typed ABI events plus Cosmos typed events that the LayerX intent router consumes; getMarket, getOrder, getPosition and getMargin SHALL read finalized LayerX state through the anchor's finalizedStateRoot with a state proof and never over the network; no matching logic SHALL exist on Paxeer.
2. THE Paxeer node SHALL expose a layerxbridge precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001016 backed by a layerxbridge module holding a per-chain registry (chain id, vault address, finality depth, enabled flag), a bonded attestor set with threshold, per-asset caps and a global pause; an inbound transfer SHALL mint a tokenfactory denom under the module admin only when threshold attestor signatures over (chain, vault, tx hash, log index, recipient, asset, amount) verify and the nullifier is unused; an outbound transfer SHALL burn the denom and emit BridgeOut for the relayer; every cap SHALL default to zero and the registry SHALL be empty at genesis so the bridge ships dormant; registry, attestor and cap changes SHALL be x/gov messages.
3. THE Paxeer node SHALL expose a launchpad precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001017 backed by a launchpad module implementing the KindleLaunch core natively: createMarket mints a fixed-supply tokenfactory denom with an ERC20 pointer and opens a virtual-reserve constant-product curve; buy and sell apply ReserveLib and FeeLib semantics (base fee plus age decay plus volatility over an 8-slot snapshot ring, clamped) with the virtual floor; fees split protocolFeeBps to the treasury module account and the rest to the market's fee-rights holder under one of claim, burn, airdrop or lp-rewards; quoteBuy, quoteSell, getReserves, getPrice, getPriceSnapshots, getMarket, getMarkets and getMarketsByCreator SHALL be views; config lives in module params changed only by x/gov; opticals, router, quoter and the fee NFT remain EVM contracts and are out of scope for v6.6.
4. THE v6.6 upgrade SHALL add the layerxexchange, layerxbridge and launchpad store keys in the existing v6.6 StoreUpgrades block of node/app.go, register the three keepers in node/precompiles.go, list the three precompiles in precompiles/setup.go through generated setup.go files, and a node upgrade test SHALL prove a chain at v6.4.0 state loads under v6.6 with the three stores added and all three precompiles callable.
5. THE LayerX perps kernel module SHALL make matched fills the only source of positions: execute_order_place SHALL open, increase or reduce the taker's and makers' positions at the fill price, POSITION_OPEN SHALL no longer accept a caller-supplied entry_notional, and every fill price SHALL be within the market's oracle deviation limit of the latest committed oracle observation or the order SHALL be refused with a typed result; existing receipts and event codes 0x0601 to 0x060b SHALL keep their encoding.
6. THE LayerX kernel SHALL gain a spot module (module id 7, LXP_MODULE_SPOT) reusing the perps price-time book for two-asset limit and market orders with immediate settlement of both legs through the asset module, ordinals 0x00070001 to 0x00070005 (MARKET_CREATE, ORDER_PLACE, ORDER_CANCEL, MARKET_HALT, MARKET_RESUME), a receipt transfer set per fill, and a conservation test; capacity limits SHALL be compile-time constants.
7. THE intent router in layerx-intents SHALL map the layerxexchange, layerxbridge and launchpad precompile events to signed LayerX activities and back, and the TypeScript and Python agent SDKs SHALL ship typed helpers for every write in ac_1 to ac_3 and for perps and spot activities, so that a human through the EVM ABI and an agent through the SDK reach the same state transition.
8. THE interop workspace SHALL ship a layerx-bridge-relayer service that watches a registered external chain through the layerx-migrate RPC quorum verifiers, signs attestations through layerx-mirror-signer so chain keys never enter the relayer, submits them to the 0x1016 precompile, and executes BridgeOut releases against the Ethereum vault; and interop/contracts/ethereum-bridge SHALL hold a PaxeerXVault contract with deposit, release under threshold attestor signatures, per-asset caps, pause and a nullifier set, with forge tests.
9. THE platform SHALL ship a layerx-indexer service that ingests LayerX through the relay_archive sync protocol and Paxeer through EVM blocks, logs and CometBFT tx_search, decodes every LayerX receipt field set and every precompile and typed module event into a durable SQLite store of per-account, per-asset rows (height or sequence, counterparty, asset, amount, kind, decoded payload), and the gateway SHALL expose lx_getHistory, px_getHistory and px_getUnifiedHistory with cursors and asset metadata, with typed SDK bindings, as the single wallet data source.
10. THE fork SHALL be rehearsed before it is run: a script SHALL export mainnet state from a synced full node, start a disposable single-validator chain from it on the current binary, schedule the v6.6 upgrade at a height, swap to the v6.6 binary at the halt and prove the chain resumes with the three new stores and every precompile answering; the runbook SHALL name the halt height, the UTC time, the binary sha256 and the per-validator steps.
11. THE indexer SHALL backfill Paxeer history before the fork from the paxscan Blockscout Postgres (blocks, transactions, logs, token_transfers, internal_transactions, tokens) read-only through a connection URL from the environment, normalize every row into the same per-account, per-asset history rows the live EVM ingester writes, fill every height missing from paxscan from a node's EVM JSON-RPC, verify each backfilled block's hash against the node, stop at a fixed finalized cutover height and hand the live ingester a cursor at that height so no row is duplicated or skipped; the ingester SHALL treat a node whose CometBFT tx index is off as EVM-only without failing.
12. THE gateway and the human web app SHALL bring each fork surface online only when the chain answers for it: the gateway SHALL probe eth_getCode at the exchange, bridge and launchpad precompile addresses, expose the result as a capabilities method, refuse the write methods of an absent surface with a typed error, and the web app SHALL render history and read-only pages before the fork and switch the launchpad, exchange and bridge write paths on from the capabilities answer without a redeploy.
13. THE fork SHALL be driven on chain by governance: a software-upgrade proposal named v6.6 at the halt height whose voting period ends before the halt, a script that submits it, votes from every validator and confirms the scheduled plan, and a consensus-parameter proposal that lowers timeout commit (bypass on) and timeout vote to the values the latency benchmark proves, both with deposits, tallies and abort conditions written into the runbook.

## Requirement 1064: Non-Authority and Receipt-Backed Truth

**User Story:** As a person trusting this app with money, I want the human plane to be structurally incapable of telling me something the protocol did not do, so that what the screen says happened is what actually happened, every time.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN any component of the human plane effects a change of protocol state THE plane SHALL do so exclusively by compiling a typed intent into canonical module payload bytes through layerx-intents, preparing the activity through the agent layer's prepare operation, obtaining a disclosure-bound signature from the custody service over the exact prepared canonical bytes, and submitting them through the agent layer, and SHALL possess no other path by which protocol state can change.
2. THE plane SHALL render a success or Done state for a money movement or protocol mutation only when a LayerX receipt verified through the agent layer's proof machinery, or a Paxeer finality proof verified by layerx-paxeer-client, backs that exact outcome, and the component that renders success SHALL be structurally unable to render it from any other input.
3. WHEN the plane displays a balance, a movement outcome, an agent state, a budget figure or any other protocol fact THE plane SHALL display only values decoded from core-produced bytes with their verification status attached by the agent layer, SHALL never raise a verification level itself, and SHALL visibly mark any value it cannot verify to the required level.
4. IF a submission's fate cannot be determined THEN THE plane SHALL present it as still checking, SHALL NOT present it as success or failure, SHALL resolve it only by receipt lookup under its idempotency key, and WHILE it remains unresolved THE plane SHALL disable every control that could duplicate the economic effect.
5. IF the core refuses an activity THEN THE plane SHALL surface the refusal honestly, SHALL state in plain language whether any money left the account, and SHALL NOT retry into a different outcome, soften the result, or present a failed movement as pending because a retry is scheduled.
6. THE plane SHALL maintain no ledger of balances or owed amounts that is not reconstructible from verified receipts alone, and WHEN the human-service store is deleted and the service restarted against the same core THE plane SHALL reconstruct every protocol-derived answer it serves, losing only declared local artefacts such as profile data, notification preferences, journey annotations and audit history.
7. WHERE the plane shows a derived or prospective figure such as an estimated fee, an estimated arrival time or a spend projection THE plane SHALL label it an estimate, SHALL exclude it from any receipt-shaped presentation, and SHALL replace it with the receipt-backed actual once one exists.
8. WHEN a read cannot be served fresh THE plane SHALL serve the last verified value marked with its age and the checkpoint or head it is relative to, and SHALL NOT silently present stale data as current.
9. THE plane SHALL provide, for every claimed outcome, access to the underlying receipt or proof material sufficient for independent verification through the public explorer or exported evidence, and the qualification suite SHALL demonstrate that a tampered human-service altering a reported value is caught by independent verification of that evidence.
10. THE plane SHALL treat the agent layer's contract as its only path to the core, SHALL NOT open the node database, read node log files, or link the node's internal structures, and CI SHALL fail the build when a dependency in human/ violates the boundary rules the agent layer defines.

## Requirement 1065: The Simplicity Contract

**User Story:** As a person with no crypto background, I want the app to expose only ideas I already understand, so that I can hold money, run agents and stay in control without learning a protocol.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE app SHALL expose exactly five top-level ideas - log in, add money, move money, manage agents, see what happened - and SHALL introduce no protocol concept as a navigation destination, decision point or required input anywhere on the default surfaces.
2. WHEN a signed-in user initiates a common action - moving money, adding money, starting a withdrawal, creating an agent, acting on an approval - THE app SHALL complete the initiation in at most three decisions, where a decision is a screen requiring user choice or input, excluding authentication challenges.
3. THE app SHALL keep a banned-vocabulary list in the copy catalog containing at least DID, session key, capability, nullifier, checkpoint, payload, canonical, idempotency, attestation and proof, SHALL enforce it with a copy lint that fails the build when a banned term appears on the authenticated plane's default surfaces - Technical details surfaces and the public explorer plane are exempt - and SHALL express every state in plain language instead.
4. THE app SHALL never require a user to transcribe, retype or manually carry any identifier between screens; every identifier SHALL be copyable in one action, every reference SHALL be a link, and every flow that needs an identifier SHALL supply it itself.
5. WHEN money moves between any two endpoints THE app SHALL resolve the protocol mechanism automatically through the route resolver, SHALL describe what will happen in plain language before commitment, and SHALL NOT ask the user to choose a transfer type, bridge, route or mechanism.
6. WHERE an advanced control exists - verification detail, evidence export, audit, emergency exit - THE app SHALL reach it through progressive disclosure, and the advanced surface SHALL never interpose itself on the simple path.
7. WHEN a custody-boundary journey needs the Paxeer wallet THE app SHALL open the wallet only at explicit signing moments, exactly once per signature the custody boundary requires - on a first journey with binding folded in, once for the binding statement and once for the custody signature - each with a plain-language statement of what the signature does, and SHALL never ask for a wallet signature at any other time.
8. THE app SHALL present every protocol state through the normative status translation table in the design document, and a status string not in that table appearing on a default surface SHALL be a build failure.
9. THE onboarding, deposit, move-money and create-agent journeys SHALL each be completable on a mobile device without documentation, and the qualification usability gate SHALL verify this with real participants against a declared success threshold.
10. WHEN the user must wait THE app SHALL say what is happening and roughly how long it takes, SHALL state when it is safe to close the app, and SHALL never present a spinner without words on any journey surface.

## Requirement 1066: Human Identity and Onboarding

**User Story:** As a new user, I want creating an account to feel like any modern app - an email and a passkey - while the system stands up my protocol identity correctly underneath, so that I am protocol-safe without ever seeing the protocol.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a person creates an account THE service SHALL establish a passkey-backed application identity as the primary credential, SHALL support a fallback credential without weakening the passkey path, and SHALL keep the application identity distinct from the LayerX DID and from any wallet.
2. WHEN the application identity exists THE service SHALL generate the human's LayerX signing keys inside the custody keystore, SHALL register the human DID through a typed intent submitted via the agent layer, and SHALL treat the account as active only after the DID registration receipt verifies.
3. WHEN the DID is registered THE service SHALL pre-register a recovery authority in the same onboarding journey through the protocol's recovery pre-registration mechanism - whose challenge delay applies when recovery is later exercised - and SHALL NOT allow the journey to complete silently without recovery in place.
4. WHILE onboarding is in progress THE app SHALL show honest per-stage progress, SHALL present the account as ready only when ac_2 holds, and IF a stage fails THEN THE app SHALL preserve the journey, explain the failure plainly, and offer resumption without restarting completed stages.
5. THE service SHALL make onboarding idempotent: repeating a stage after a crash, a timeout or a duplicate request SHALL converge on one application identity, one DID, one recovery registration and one set of receipts, with no orphaned protocol state.
6. THE service SHALL store profile information such as display name and avatar as declared-local data, separated from protocol identity, editable and deletable without touching protocol state.
7. THE service SHALL record, for the DID registration, the key activation, the recovery registration and any wallet binding, the verified receipt establishing when each became active, and SHALL surface that evidence under Technical details and in the audit export.
8. WHEN a user signs in on a new device THE service SHALL require the passkey ceremony, SHALL record the device in the session inventory, and SHALL emit a security notification carrying an action that opens the device list.
9. THE browser SHALL at no point receive, derive or cache LayerX private key material, and the qualification suite SHALL verify that the web application bundle and its runtime state contain no signing capability.
10. IF the agent layer or the core is unavailable during onboarding THEN THE service SHALL complete the application-identity stage, SHALL queue the protocol stages with honest pending presentation, and SHALL NOT fabricate an active account.

## Requirement 1067: The Key Custody Service

**User Story:** As the owner of accounts and agents whose keys I never see, I want the custody service to guard signing power at least as carefully as a hardware wallet would, so that custody convenience never becomes custody exposure.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE service SHALL hold every human and managed-agent private key inside a KMS-backed keystore, SHALL keep key material out of process logs, error messages, metrics, traces, backups in plaintext and the browser, and SHALL zeroize in-memory key material on release.
2. WHEN anything requests a signature THE service SHALL sign only through the disclosure-bound path: the exact canonical byte string together with a structured disclosure that re-encodes byte-identically to those bytes, and SHALL refuse to sign when the disclosure does not match, exactly as the agent layer's signer contract requires.
3. WHERE an operation is designated step-up - acting on an approval, changing security settings, revealing a secret, initiating a withdrawal or exit, rebinding the payout wallet, archiving an agent - THE service SHALL require a fresh passkey ceremony bound to the specific operation, and SHALL reject a signature request for a step-up operation without one.
4. WHEN a managed agent needs operating authority THE service SHALL provision a protocol session key to layerx-agentd with an explicit expiry, an explicit permitted activity set and a revocation path, SHALL never transfer a primary key, and SHALL propagate revocation promptly when the agent is paused or archived.
5. THE service SHALL enforce per-principal isolation in the keystore so no request path can reach another human's keys or another human's agents' keys, and the isolation suite SHALL prove it adversarially.
6. THE service SHALL append every signing decision - grant or refusal - to the audit log with the disclosure digest, the operation, the principal and the step-up evidence, and SHALL never write payload secrets or key material to the audit log.
7. IF the KMS or keystore is unavailable THEN THE service SHALL refuse to sign with an honest error, SHALL NOT fall back to any lower-assurance key or cached material, and SHALL surface the degradation on its status surface.
8. THE service SHALL support key rotation for human and agent DIDs through the protocol's rotation mechanism, SHALL present the challenge delay in plain time units, and SHALL keep the superseded key usable only for the window the protocol defines.
9. THE service SHALL bound signing throughput per principal with typed refusals, so a compromised session cannot drain an account faster than limits allow, and the limits SHALL be declared configuration, not code constants.
10. THE v1 service SHALL expose no key export path, and any future export SHALL be specified as its own feature; the qualification suite SHALL verify no API surface returns key material.

## Requirement 1068: Paxeer Wallet Binding

**User Story:** As a user with money on Paxeer, I want to link my EVM wallet once, safely, so that deposits and payouts flow to an address I control while my LayerX funds stay beyond the wallet's reach.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a user links a Paxeer wallet THE plane SHALL obtain the EVM key's signature over the protocol's domain-separated binding statement naming the DID and network_id, SHALL submit the binding as a typed intent through the agent layer, and SHALL treat the binding as established only when its receipt verifies.
2. THE plane SHALL treat the bound address as a payout and provenance association only, SHALL never accept an EVM signature as authorisation for any LayerX activity, and SHALL state on the binding surface, in one plain sentence, that the wallet cannot move LayerX funds.
3. THE binding journey SHALL be deferred until first needed - the first deposit or withdrawal - SHALL open the wallet exactly once, and SHALL show the full address with a checksum-styled rendering, copy affordance and QR at every confirmation surface, never a truncation alone.
4. WHEN a user replaces a bound wallet THE plane SHALL require step-up authentication, SHALL submit the rebinding through the same receipt-verified path, SHALL keep the old binding effective until the new receipt verifies, and SHALL emit a security notification with an action button.
5. IF the wallet is unavailable, disconnects mid-journey or rejects the signature THEN THE plane SHALL show a designed state naming what happened and offering retry or cancel, and SHALL leave no partially-bound state behind.
6. THE plane SHALL verify that the address that signed the binding statement is the address recorded in the receipt before presenting the binding as active, and a mismatch SHALL surface as a verification failure, never be silently accepted.
7. WHERE no wallet is bound THE app SHALL present deposits and withdrawals as available-but-needs-linking, with the linking step folded into the journey rather than a separate errand.
8. THE plane SHALL support at most one active bound payout wallet per human account in v1, SHALL display which address is bound wherever payouts are discussed, and SHALL record every past binding with its receipts in the audit trail.

## Requirement 1069: Approval Operations in the Agent Contract

**User Story:** As a human governing agents, I want approvals to be first-class operations of the agent layer contract, so that my app can list, inspect and decide holds with the same receipt-grade rigor as every other operation.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE agent-api contract SHALL gain an approval module - list, get, approve, reject - as an additive change within contract major 1, defined in the schema with golden vectors, and SHALL leave every existing declaration unchanged.
2.
