1. THE backend SHALL bind its HTTP listener and answer its liveness path after migration completes, under the documented environment of a deployment whose node applies the configured JSON-RPC throttles.
2. THE cause SHALL be found by reproducing the hang locally from the committed image and the documented environment variables, and SHALL be fixed where it is - a start-up path that blocks on a remote call, a supervision child that never reports started, or an initialisation that waits on a throttled node - never by raising a timeout or by moving the failure behind a retry.
3. THE capability probe SHALL do its first remote call outside its initialisation callback, SHALL keep its documented refresh interval, SHALL stay disabled by default, and SHALL leave the rest of the application starting when the node is unreachable or throttled.
4. A regression test SHALL start the affected process against a node that never answers and assert that it reaches its started state within a bounded time and that its state reports the probe as unavailable rather than raising.

## Requirement 1195: One Explorer Surface

**User Story:** As someone following a chain link from the control plane, I want to land in the explorer, so that there is one place where chain and kernel data are rendered and one place to keep correct.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE control plane pages that render batch and checkpoint listings and details themselves SHALL be replaced by links into the explorer's anchor surfaces, addressed through a documented base-URL variable with no literal host.
2. THE journeys the beta contract requires of the control plane SHALL be kept: the account journey, the receipt lookup, and the independent receipt verification with its overload, refusal and retry states exactly as spec/layerx-beta requires them.
3. THE route performance budgets, the copy catalogue entries and the navigation of the control plane SHALL be updated to the routes that remain, with no entry left pointing at a route that no longer exists.
4. THE tests that covered the retired pages SHALL be changed to assert the link surface that replaces them, and no test SHALL be deleted to make the change pass; the verification and account tests SHALL keep asserting what they assert now.
5. IF the beta contract, its consistency check or a documentation journey names a retired route THEN the contradiction SHALL be recorded in the qualification log and the contract SHALL be left intact for its owner rather than edited from inside this feature.

## Requirement 1196: Wave Qualification and Recorded Evidence

**User Story:** As the person deciding whether this feature is done, I want the aggregate suites run once on the merged revision with what ran written down, so that the feature's state is a record rather than a recollection.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE aggregate explorer suites - the backend Paxeer X suites, the frontend type check and vitest suite, and the three lint checks - SHALL be run once, on the merged revision of the feature's waves, through the fleet gates, and never per task.
2. THE run SHALL be recorded in spec/paxeer-x-explorer/qualification.kvx as gate records carrying the task, the requirements the gate qualifies, the revision, the exact command, the exit code and the log path, written only by having executed the command they name.
3. ANY failure the run exposes that belongs to no task in this feature SHALL be recorded once as an observation with its revision, command, exit code, log path, one sentence of what was observed and one sentence of what is assumed, and SHALL NOT be chased.
4. NO gate record SHALL be written for a command that did not run, and no gate that passed at the recorded revision SHALL be rerun to confirm it.

## Requirement 1197: The Scan Shell

**User Story:** As someone moving between the explorer's pages, I want one frame around every page - a utility bar, a brand row, a centred container and a footer - so that the explorer reads as one product instead of a set of screens.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE utility bar SHALL sit above the brand row and SHALL carry, on the left, the Paxeer coin price with its percentage change and the current gas price in small text with the accent value tone, and on the right the desktop search entry on every page except the home page, followed by the settings control, the appearance control and the network control.
2. THE brand row SHALL carry the network mark and wordmark on the left and, on the right, a horizontal menu of dropdown groups - Home; Blockchain with transactions, pending transactions, blocks, top accounts and verified contracts; Tokens with tokens, token transfers and the NFT items where they are enabled; Kernel with the Paxeer X account, anchors and receipts items only while the Paxeer X lists feature is enabled; Resources with charts and statistics and the gas tracker; API with the documentation items; and More with contract verification, CSV export and the account items only while the account feature is enabled - with the group holding the current route rendered in the accent text tone.
3. EVERY page layout - the application layout, the home layout, the error layout and the search-results layout - SHALL place its content in one centred container of a single maximum width over the page background the theme declares, so no page sets its own frame.
4. THE footer SHALL carry a thin top border, the social links on the left and a back-to-top control on the right, then four columns - a brand blurb with the add-network-to-wallet button and three columns of links read from the footer configuration - and a bottom line naming Paxeer X Network and the year.
5. THE home page SHALL open with a hero container above the content holding the page title and the wide search field with its filter selector and its accent submit button, and the search behaviour, the suggestion list and the redirect path SHALL be exactly what they are now.
6. EVERY component of the shell SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
7. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render the shell with every token it uses resolving in each, and neither appearance SHALL be reached by a hardcoded value.
8. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the existing mobile header, mobile navigation and mobile search paths SHALL stay in use with no horizontal page scroll and nothing clipped.
9. EACH changed shell component SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own API payload mocks and asserts the elements the structure demands, their order and their text.

## Requirement 1198: The Scan Primitives

**User Story:** As a developer building any explorer page, I want the repeated pieces of the scan layout to exist once as shared components, so that nine pages cannot drift into nine different cards.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE shared scan components SHALL include a stat card carrying an uppercase label, a value and an optional delta whose sign selects the success or destructive text tone.
2. THE shared scan components SHALL include a table card carrying a header count line, an actions slot beside it, the table body, and a footer holding a show-rows selector and a pagination control; the pagination SHALL read First, a previous control, Page x of N, a next control and Last, and the query hook that drives paging and its existing test SHALL be left exactly as they are.
3. THE shared scan components SHALL include pill section tabs whose selected pill sits on the accent surface, an expander row that reads as a More Details label with a click-to-show-more control revealing its children, a preview button rendered as an eye, a method chip carrying a decoded method name or a raw selector, and a direction badge carrying IN or OUT.
4. THE key-value detail row SHALL be built on the existing detailed-information component and SHALL render a label column whose question-mark icon carries the row's tooltip, a value column, and a divider variant that separates groups of rows.
5. THE entity links for addresses, transactions, blocks and tokens SHALL take the scan link tone, truncation and copy-icon placement, and SHALL keep every route, parameter and feature condition they resolve today.
6. THE table, tabs, badge, tag, stat and button recipes SHALL gain the variants these primitives consume while the theme's token values and the existing token test SHALL remain unchanged and passing.
7. EVERY primitive SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
8. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render every primitive with each token it uses resolving in both.
9. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the list-item variants SHALL stay in use so no table is clipped and no page scrolls horizontally.
10. EACH primitive SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own API payload mocks and asserts its structure, its order and its text.

## Requirement 1199: The Scan List Pages

**User Story:** As someone scanning what the chain is doing, I want the transaction, block, token and account lists to read as the same card with the same controls, so that learning one list teaches me all of them.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE transactions page SHALL open with a row of four stat cards - transactions in the last day, pending transactions in the last hour, total transaction fee in the last day and average transaction fee in the last day - each carrying its delta, fed by the statistics the frontend already reads.
2. THE transactions table card SHALL carry the count line with the record note beneath it, the download action and the pagination in its header, and the columns preview, transaction hash, action chip, block, age, from and to with the direction arrow between them, amount and transaction fee, with the failed-transaction marker kept on the hash.
3. THE blocks page SHALL use the same table card, count line, header actions, show-rows footer and pagination as the transactions page, with the columns the block list already renders.
4. THE token tracker page SHALL render a table card counting the token contracts found, with the columns index, token with its logo name and symbol, price with the coin-denominated price beneath it in the muted tone, change percent in the success or destructive tone, volume over the last day, circulating market capitalisation, onchain market capitalisation and holders.
5. THE top accounts page SHALL render a table card whose count line names the accounts found with the total balance beside it, with the columns index, address, name tag, balance, percentage and transaction count.
6. EVERY changed component of these pages SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
7. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render these pages with every token they use resolving in each.
8. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the existing list-item variants SHALL stay in use with no horizontal page scroll and no clipped table.
9. EACH changed component SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own API payload mocks and asserts the columns, their order and their text.

## Requirement 1200: The Scan Detail Pages

**User Story:** As someone opening a transaction or a block, I want its facts in one labelled card with the rare ones folded away, so that I can read the common case without scrolling past everything else.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE transaction page SHALL open with a title carrying the previous and next controls, pill section tabs for the overview and the logs with their count, and the API entry beside them.
2. THE transaction overview SHALL render the decoded action in its own card above the detail card, and the detail card SHALL carry the hash with its copy control, the status badge, the block with its confirmation chip, the timestamp with its zone control, a divider, the sender and the recipient with the verified mark where the recipient carries one, a divider, and the value with its coin icon and fiat figure, the fee and the gas price.
3. THE transaction page SHALL close its detail card with an expander that reads as More Details with a click-to-show-more control, holding the fields the overview does not show, and the logs, internal transactions, raw trace and state tabs SHALL render inside the same card as the overview.
4. THE block page SHALL carry the title with the block number, pill section tabs, and one detail card holding height with its previous and next controls, timestamp, the transactions sentence, hash, reward, difficulty, total difficulty, size, a divider, gas used with its percentage, burnt fees and the extra data field, closed by the same More Details expander.
5. THE block page's transactions and withdrawals tabs SHALL render in the shared table card with the same header, footer and pagination as the list pages.
6. EVERY changed component of these pages SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
7. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render these pages with every token they use resolving in each.
8. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the detail rows SHALL stack without a horizontal page scroll and without a clipped value.
9. EACH changed component SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own API payload mocks and asserts the rows, their order, their labels and their values.

## Requirement 1201: The Scan Entity Pages

**User Story:** As someone looking at an address or a token, I want its summary in three cards above tabs that hold everything else, so that the page tells me what this thing is before it tells me what it did.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE address page SHALL carry a title row with the identicon, the label Address, the full address, the copy control and the QR control, and an icon action row with the watchlist, API and menu entries.
2. THE address page SHALL render three cards - an overview card with the coin balance, its fiat value and the token-holdings selector; a more-information card with the name tags, the latest and first transactions sent and the funding source; and a third card that shows the linked Paxeer X account when the address has one and the contract information otherwise.
3. THE address page SHALL carry pill section tabs for transactions, internal transactions, token transfers and the remaining tabs it already has, with the advanced-filter entry on the right, and its transaction table card SHALL carry the latest-of-total count line, the download action, an OUT or IN direction badge on the counterparty column, a view-all footer row and the CSV export link beneath the card.
4. THE token page SHALL carry a title row with the token logo, the label Token, the name with its symbol and the verified mark, and beneath it a chip row with the token standard, the source-code chip, the implementation chip and the hashtag tags, with the project link, the API entry and the menu on the right.
5. THE token page SHALL render three cards - an overview card with the maximum total supply, the holders and the transfers with their total and daily selector; a market card with the price, the onchain market capitalisation and the circulating supply market capitalisation; and an other-information card with the token contract and its decimals - above pill section tabs for transfers, holders, information, contract and analytics, whose transfers tab is the shared table card with its count line, its download and advanced-filter actions, its pagination and its show-records footer.
6. EVERY changed component of these pages SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
7. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render these pages with every token they use resolving in each.
8. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the three cards SHALL stack and the existing list-item variants SHALL stay in use with no horizontal page scroll.
9. EACH changed component SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own API payload mocks and asserts the cards, the tabs, the direction badges and the footer entries.

## Requirement 1202: The Statistics Page

**User Story:** As someone studying the network rather than a single transaction, I want the numbers and the charts on one page grouped by subject with a navigation that follows me down it, so that I can move between sections without losing my place.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE statistics page SHALL carry a sticky section navigation on the left listing the overview statistics, market data, blockchain data, network data and contract sections, with the section in view marked.
2. THE overview statistics SHALL render as a grid of small stat cards, four to a row on the desktop, each with its label, its information icon, its value and its delta in the success or destructive tone.
3. EACH section SHALL render its charts as a two-column grid of chart cards, each carrying its title with the interval and an information icon, a view link on the right, the current value beneath the title, and the chart itself with its dated horizontal axis.
4. THE chart data, the interval selector, the resolution and the query hooks SHALL be exactly what they are now; only the frame, the grid and the chart's own colours change, and the chart colours SHALL come from theme tokens.
5. EVERY changed component of this page SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
6. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render the page and its charts with every token they use resolving in each.
7. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the section navigation SHALL collapse and the grids SHALL fall to one column with no horizontal page scroll.
8. EACH changed component SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own statistics mocks and asserts the sections, the stat cards and the chart card structure.

## Requirement 1203: The Kernel Pages Match the Chain Pages

**User Story:** As someone following a kernel account through the explorer, I want its pages built from the same cards and tables as the chain pages, so that the kernel is part of the explorer rather than a second surface inside it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE unified account page SHALL render its summary in the same cards the address page uses and its identities, assets and activity in the shared pill section tabs and the shared table card, with the same count line, header actions, pagination and show-rows footer.
2. THE anchors list SHALL render in the shared table card with the columns it already carries, and its settlement rung SHALL render through the existing status ladder component restyled on the shared badge.
3. THE receipt detail page SHALL render its fields in the shared key-value detail rows with their tooltip labels and divider groups, keeping every field, link and not-found state the page already has.
4. NO API resource, route, feature flag, query hook or payload type of the kernel pages SHALL change, and the existing kernel specs SHALL keep asserting what they assert now.
5. EVERY changed component of these pages SHALL take its colour, typeface, radius and shadow from a theme semantic token or a recipe, and SHALL carry no literal colour, font family, radius or shadow value.
6. BOTH the light and the dark appearance SHALL render these pages with every token they use resolving in each.
7. THE desktop structure at 1280px and above SHALL match the scan layout the reference defines, and at 375px the list-item variants SHALL stay in use with no horizontal page scroll and no clipped table.
8. EACH changed component SHALL have a vitest spec that renders the real component through the real theme provider of the frontend test harness with the repository's own kernel payload mocks and asserts the cards, the tabs and the rows.

## Requirement 1204: Threshold Custody Daemon

**User Story:** As the operator of the embedded wallet, I want every wallet key held as threshold shares across independent nodes, so that no host, process, database or backup can sign or leak a key on its own.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE attestor daemon under human/wallet/attestor SHALL generate secp256k1 keys by distributed key generation across five participants with threshold three (library threshold parameter three, the signer count) using the CGGMP implementation of the vendored library, SHALL produce Ethereum signatures with low s and a recovery id, and a test SHALL recover the signing address from a signature over a real EIP-1559 transaction digest produced by five in-process participants.
2. THE daemon SHALL generate Ed25519 keys by distributed key generation and sign with FROST, and every signature SHALL verify under the standard library's Ed25519 verifier and under the chain's strict verifier in layerxproof/verify with the same public key, proven by a test that signs the LX:PAXEER-BIND:v1 message and a receipt-domain digest.
3. THE daemon SHALL import an existing key by dealer split: given a whole key held only in the dealer's memory, five shares SHALL be derived, each node SHALL validate its share against the original public key during the refresh that follows, and the refreshed shares SHALL sign a message whose signature recovers the original address; a share that does not match the public key SHALL be refused by every node.
4. THE daemon SHALL refresh all shares of a key without changing the public key, for both curves, and SHALL add a share for a new participant followed by a refresh, proven by a test that removes one participant, adds a replacement and signs with a quorum that includes the replacement.
5. THE share store SHALL encrypt every share at rest under a per-node key supplied by file path or environment variable name, with the key id, curve, public key, refresh epoch and participant set as authenticated associated data, SHALL refuse to start when the node key is absent, and SHALL never log, return or serialise a share.
6. THE peer transport SHALL carry protocol messages between participants over mutual TLS with per-session ordering and replay refusal, SHALL bind every message to its session id and round, and a test SHALL run a full signing session across five participants on distinct listeners with certificates generated in the test.
7. THE daemon SHALL expose keys.generate, keys.import, keys.refresh, keys.addshare, sign and health exactly as [contract_context.111.decision] attestor_api describes, SHALL enable keys.import only when a ceremony flag is set at start and only for the operator identity, and SHALL record every request in a hash-chained audit log whose head is served by health.
8. A five-node in-process end-to-end test SHALL import a known secp256k1 key and a known Ed25519 key, refresh both, sign an EVM transaction, a typed-data digest, a binding message and an activity envelope, verify each signature, and assert the audit chain of every node covers every request.

## Requirement 1205: Policy-Bound Signing and Authentication

**User Story:** As a person whose wallet is held for them, I want every signature to be gated by my own login and by rules the signers apply themselves, so that neither a stolen gateway nor a stolen token alone can move my funds.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. EACH attestor SHALL verify a Supabase access token against the project's JWKS with issuer, audience, expiry, not-before and subject checks, SHALL cache and rotate keys by key id, SHALL refuse a token whose subject does not own the key id being signed for, and SHALL refuse to sign when the JWKS cannot be fetched and no cached key matches.
2. EACH attestor SHALL verify an agent request by the agent's Ed25519 signature over a canonical digest of method, key id, request bytes, nonce and expiry, against the agent's registered public key replicated to the node, SHALL refuse a replayed nonce and an expired request, and SHALL refuse a request whose principal is frozen.
3. EACH attestor SHALL decode an EVM transaction of legacy, access-list, dynamic-fee and set-code type from its bytes, SHALL pin the chain id to the configured chain, SHALL decode calldata to the network's precompiles with the ABI files under precompiles/, and SHALL evaluate per-account policy locally: per-transaction and rolling value caps per asset, request rate, destination and selector rules, and refusal of any transaction whose fields it cannot decode.
4. EACH attestor SHALL hash EIP-712 typed data itself from the supplied domain, types and message, SHALL accept a personal message only with the EIP-191 prefix applied by the attestor, and SHALL accept a bare digest only for the sponsored batch construction and the EIP-7702 authorisation construction, recomputed from the supplied fields, and for nothing else.
5. EACH attestor SHALL decode a kernel activity envelope from its canonical bytes, SHALL match it against the human service's disclosure fields supplied with the request, SHALL enforce allowed modules, operations, amounts and destinations per account, SHALL accept a binding message only for the account's own address and current nonce, and SHALL accept a 402 grant or receive preimage only within the account's caps.
6. THE policy SHALL be versioned per account with a default set in configuration, SHALL be evaluated identically by every node from the same inputs, and SHALL fail closed: an unknown request kind, an unknown policy version, a missing field or a decode error refuses the request with a typed reason that is logged and returned.
7. THE decoders SHALL be validated against the repository's golden vectors: the agent API goldens under agent/schema/agent-api/golden for activity envelopes and the binding vectors under layerxproof/testvectors and layerxproof/testdata for the binding message, and a vector the decoder cannot round-trip SHALL fail the test.

## Requirement 1206: Attestor Network Operations

**User Story:** As the operator, I want the attestor nodes deployed, backed up and observable as independent machines in independent regions, so that the loss of any two of them costs nothing and the compromise of any two reveals nothing.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE deployment definitions under human/wallet/deploy SHALL describe five attestor applications, one machine each, in five regions on at least two continents, each with a persistent volume, its own secrets named in the environment documentation, health checks bound to the daemon's health endpoint, and private-network-only peer ports; a check script SHALL validate the definitions without contacting the platform.
2. EACH node SHALL back up its encrypted share store to object storage on a schedule and after every keygen, import, refresh and add-share, under the node's own backup key, and a restore test SHALL bring a node back from its backup and sign with the quorum.
3. THE health endpoint SHALL report node id, region, share count, refresh epoch, audit head, reachability of every peer and readiness, and the gateway SHALL choose a signing quorum by health and measured latency and SHALL refuse to sign when fewer than three healthy nodes are reachable.
4. THE network SHALL be deployed from the definitions with the daemon image built from the repository, a test key SHALL be generated and signed with across three regions, and the record of that run - image digest, regions, health of every node, signature verification - SHALL be committed to the qualification log without any hostname, address or secret.
5. A load test tool under human/wallet/attestor SHALL drive concurrent signing sessions against a configured network for a bounded duration, SHALL report throughput, latency percentiles and refusals, and one run against the deployed network SHALL be recorded in the qualification log.

## Requirement 1207: Migration Ceremony

**User Story:** As the operator of the existing service, I want every current wallet moved into shares by a rehearsed, verifiable procedure, so that no user loses an address and no whole key survives the move.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE ceremony tool under human/wallet/ceremony SHALL read the existing wallet rows from a database connection, decrypt each key envelope with the master key supplied only through an environment variable name, verify the decrypted key derives the stored address, and refuse to continue on any mismatch; the tool SHALL hold keys only in memory and SHALL never write a key, a share or the master key to disk, a log or a temporary file.
2. THE tool SHALL split each key into five shares by a degree-two polynomial for both curves, SHALL deliver each share to its node over mutual TLS through keys.import, SHALL trigger keys.refresh on every node, SHALL request a test signature from three nodes, SHALL recover the address from that signature, and SHALL mark the wallet migrated only when the recovered address equals the stored address.
3. THE tool SHALL run in rehearsal mode against a restored copy of the database and five in-process or locally deployed nodes, SHALL produce a report counting wallets read, verified, imported, refreshed, test-signed and matched, and SHALL exit non-zero unless every wallet matched.
4. THE tool SHALL re-encrypt the funded wallets' rows into an archive file under a fresh passphrase supplied through an environment variable name, SHALL verify the archive decrypts to the same rows, and SHALL exclude those wallets from migration; the live tables drop them only after the archive verifies.
5. THE rehearsal SHALL be executed once in wave 5 against the production data read from the current wallet host read-only, and its report SHALL be recorded in the qualification log with counts only; the live ceremony SHALL run only after the rehearsal passes, the current host SHALL proxy the endpoint hostname to the new gateway, the old master key SHALL be retained sealed and never destroyed, and the old service SHALL be retired only after the new gateway has served the endpoint through the proxy.

## Requirement 1208: Wallet Gateway Without Keys

**User Story:** As a developer of an app on the network, I want the wallet API I already integrate to keep working while the keys behind it move to the attestors, so that nothing I shipped breaks and the service becomes safer without a migration on my side.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE gateway, SDK and demo SHALL be imported into human/wallet as one pnpm workspace with their existing tests passing, every secret, environment file and credential removed, an environment example that names variables only, and a secret scan over the imported tree that passes.
2. THE gateway SHALL keep the public routes under /v1/wallet, /v1/agent and /v1/agents with their request and response shapes, SHALL sign through the attestor API for every wallet flagged migrated and through the legacy envelope path only for wallets not yet migrated, and SHALL flip a wallet to the attestor path atomically with the ceremony's migrated mark.
3. THE gateway SHALL allocate transaction nonces through a shared store with a per-address lock that holds across worker processes and instances, SHALL broadcast through a pool of RPC endpoints with health checks and failover, and SHALL estimate gas and simulate before requesting a signature.
4. THE gateway SHALL remove the funded routes, the treasury evaluator, the tier tables and the fund and sweep paths, SHALL refuse a request that names a funded wallet, and SHALL keep no treasury key in any configuration.
5. THE gateway SHALL bind an agent to a human owner only through an authenticated claim route, SHALL accept a value-moving agent request only with the agent's end-to-end signature that the attestors also verify, and SHALL scope the gateway-minted agent token to read routes.
6. THE gateway SHALL rate-limit per client and per account at the HTTP layer, SHALL record every signing request, refusal and broadcast with the attestor audit sequence in its own audit table, and SHALL expose readiness that reports the attestor quorum, the nonce store, the RPC pool and the identity provider.
7. END-TO-END tests SHALL spawn the real attestor daemon built from the repository, provision a wallet, sign and verify a transaction, a message and typed data, refuse a request with an invalid token, and refuse a transaction outside policy.

## Requirement 1209: Unified Account Provisioning

**User Story:** As a person signing up, I want one account that exists on both networks the moment I sign in, so that I never learn there are two.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a wallet is provisioned THE gateway SHALL request a secp256k1 key and an Ed25519 key from the attestors, SHALL derive the address, the DID as did:layerx plus the public key hex, and the main account id exactly as the chain's DeriveAccountID, and SHALL store all three with the wallet row.
2. WHEN both keys exist THE gateway SHALL send the setup top-up from the sponsor account for the exact binding gas within the configured cap, SHALL request the Ed25519 signature over the LX:PAXEER-BIND:v1 message for the current binding nonce, SHALL build and sign the bindLayerX transaction from the wallet's address, SHALL broadcast it, and SHALL confirm through the precompile's getUnifiedAccount that the address is bound to the DID before reporting the account active.
3. THE provisioning SHALL be idempotent and resumable: a retry after any step completes the remaining steps without a second key, a second top-up or a second binding, and a binding that already names a different DID SHALL be refused and recorded.
4. THE /v1/wallet/me response SHALL carry the address, the DID, the main account id, the binding state and the kernel availability state, and an existing client that reads only the address SHALL keep working.
5. A backfill command SHALL provision the Ed25519 key and the binding for every migrated wallet that lacks them, in bounded batches with a resumable cursor, SHALL use the agent's own key for agent wallets where the agent has registered it, and SHALL report per-wallet outcomes without secrets.
6. THE agent provisioning SHALL derive an agent's DID from the Ed25519 public key the agent registered, SHALL require the agent's own signature over the binding message, and SHALL refuse to bind an agent wallet to any other key.

## Requirement 1210: Shared Endpoint Client and Reads

**User Story:** As a user, I want one balance, one history and one status for everything I do, so that the network reads as one place.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SDK SHALL talk to one RPC base, the hosted endpoint, SHALL route eth_ methods to the chain, lx_ methods to the kernel and px_ methods to the joins through that base, and SHALL batch mixed calls in one JSON-RPC batch.
2. THE SDK SHALL resolve the account with px_resolveAccount on sign-in, SHALL read joined balances with px_getBalances and complete them with eth_getBalance and ERC-20 calls for assets outside the custody map, SHALL surface the join limit, and SHALL read history with px_getUnifiedHistory by cursor.
3. THE SDK SHALL map the explorer's per-transaction status, the human service's journey states and the anchor states to one ladder - instant, sealed, final - with the source of each rung, and the app SHALL show that ladder and nothing else.
4. THE SDK SHALL plan a value movement with the human service's intent plan operation, SHALL present the legs, domains, fees per leg, total fee and signers, SHALL submit with the plan digest and bindings, and SHALL track progress through the journey operation.
5. WHEN the endpoint reports the kernel unreachable or the anchor precompile reports no finalised checkpoint THE SDK SHALL expose a kernel availability state with the reason, and every kernel-side operation SHALL refuse with that state instead of timing out or inventing a result.

## Requirement 1211: Kernel-Side Custody Plane

**User Story:** As the network, I want the human service to sign kernel activities for embedded accounts through the same attestors and under the same login, so that one custody plane serves both networks.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE identity provider under human/crates/layerx-human-identity-provider SHALL accept the wallet's identity assertion - a Supabase access token verified against a configured JWKS - as a login principal, SHALL open or create the application account mapped to that subject and to the wallet's DID, and SHALL keep the passkey path unchanged for accounts that use it.
2. THE human service's custody signer SHALL have an attestor-backed implementation in human/crates/layerx-human-kms that signs an activity's preimage through the attestor sign operation with the request kind lx_activity, the disclosure fields and the user's assertion, SHALL refuse when the quorum refuses, and SHALL be tested against the real daemon spawned from the repository.
3. THE human service's intent submit operation SHALL verify the signed digest and every leg binding against the re-planned plan, SHALL create a journey and drive its legs through the existing movement journeys, SHALL return the intent submission shape the contract declares, and the TypeScript SDK's submit decoder SHALL accept the live response.
4. AN end-to-end test SHALL sign in with a wallet assertion, plan a kernel send, submit it, and observe the journey reach a receipt-verified state against the human service and the daemon in process.

## Requirement 1212: Wallet SDK

**User Story:** As a dapp developer, I want to integrate the embedded wallet like any injected wallet and reach the network's own surfaces through typed calls, so that one integration covers every user.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SDK SHALL provide an EIP-1193 provider announced through EIP-6963 and installed as window.paxeer, SHALL implement eth_requestAccounts, eth_accounts, eth_chainId, eth_sendTransaction, eth_signTypedData_v4, personal_sign and paxeer_signCustody, and SHALL implement eth_sign only for the two digest constructions the attestors accept, passing their fields, not a digest.
2. THE SDK SHALL discover injected wallets through EIP-6963 and present the embedded provider and every injected provider through one interface, so an app treats both custody modes identically.
3. THE SDK SHALL ship typed modules for the exchange, bridge, launchpad, fee token and web data precompiles, reusing the ABI builders under agent/sdk/typescript, and for the gas station's quote and submit with the sponsored batch signature.
4. THE SDK SHALL ship the shared endpoint client, the kernel read client, the human service intent and journey client and the status ladder of req.7, with response decoders validated against the schema goldens under human/schema and the attestor schema goldens.
5. THE SDK SHALL ship agent lane helpers that sign requests end to end with an Ed25519 key and derive the agent's DID, with tests against the gateway's verification.
6. THE SDK SHALL be published from human/wallet/sdk with a changelog, typed errors, and a demo under human/wallet/demo that exercises sign-in, provisioning, a transaction, typed data, a custody hand-off and a kernel plan.

## Requirement 1213: Wallet App on Embedded Custody

**User Story:** As a user of the app, I want one clear way to hold my account and every network surface in one place, so that the app is the network's front door and not a browser.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE app SHALL be committed under human/apps/wallet with every secret, test key and credential removed and a secret scan passing, before any other change to it.
2. THE app SHALL remove the self-custody vault, the PIN flow, the seed import and backup screens, the same-origin dapp proxy, the in-app browser and browser plane, and the ramp screen, and SHALL keep MetaMask and other injected wallets through the SDK's EIP-6963 discovery.
3. THE app SHALL sign in through the gateway's identity flow, provision through the gateway, and sign every transaction, message and typed data through the SDK provider, with no key material in the bundle.
4. THE app SHALL show the unified account: address, DID, binding state, one asset list with joined balances, one history, the status ladder per transaction, a custody deposit flow, and kernel-side plans with the kernel availability state.
5. THE app SHALL expose the exchange, bridge, launchpad, fee token choice and web data surfaces through the SDK modules, and the fee choice SHALL label every fee's denomination.
6. THE app SHALL carry its environment configuration and release tests in the repository, and its tests SHALL run under vitest and its end-to-end configuration under Playwright.
7. THE app SHALL offer a theme selection system - colour theme, accent, font family, size preset and density - resolved into design tokens applied before first paint, persisted on the device, with every surface rendered from those tokens and no hard-coded colour outside the theme module.
8. THE app SHALL ship as an installable progressive web application from its own origin with a self-hosted manifest, icons and service worker, SHALL load no third-party PWA service or script, SHALL produce no store build, and SHALL carry no native project scaffolding or its dependencies.

## Requirement 1214: Fees and Payments Across Both Networks

**User Story:** As a user, I want to know what I pay and in what, whichever route my action takes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE SDK and the app SHALL offer PAX gas, SID through the gas station's sponsored batch, and SID through the fee token precompile's preference, SHALL label each fee's denomination, and SHALL show the LayerX fee per leg separately from chain gas.
2. THE attestor policy SHALL treat the sponsored batch digest and the EIP-7702 authorisation as distinct request kinds with their own caps, and the gateway SHALL relay sponsored batches through the gas station's submit operation.
3. 402LXP payments SHALL draw from the kernel account under budget and allowance caps shown in the app, and contract calls to the web data precompile SHALL show the PAX value they carry.

## Requirement 1215: Shared Endpoint Deployment

**User Story:** As the operator, I want the shared endpoint running and truthful, so that the wallet has one base to talk to.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE hosted endpoint under platform/hosted/gateway SHALL start with the kernel backends unconfigured or unreachable, SHALL serve eth_ relay and the px_ joins that depend on chain state alone, SHALL answer kernel-dependent methods with a typed unavailable error naming the backend, and SHALL report per-backend readiness.
2. THE deployment definitions under human/wallet/deploy SHALL describe the endpoint's application with its environment variable names and health check, and the endpoint SHALL be deployed from the repository image with px_resolveAccount and eth_chainId answering against the chain; the record is committed to the qualification log without hosts.
3. Container source definitions reside in the canonical docker tree with matching ignore files and accurate referrers. Each recipe is checked using the same actual build context its producer supplies, including the verified generated registry builder context; no missing COPY input or existing check is bypassed. Source-layout qualification does not establish live endpoint deployment or API responses under ac_2.

## Requirement 1216: Release Gates, Runbooks and Review

**User Story:** As the owner, I want one bounded gate, a rehearsal record and an operations record before anything live changes.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE repository SHALL carry tools/wallet/gate-test.sh and tools/wallet/gate-lint.sh, each bounded by a budget from the environment with a documented default, each with a check mode, running the Go, TypeScript and Rust suites and lints this feature owns, and tools/wallet/scan-secrets.sh that fails on key-shaped, token-shaped or connection-string-shaped content.
2. THE runbooks under human/wallet/docs SHALL cover node loss and replacement, refresh cadence, backup restore, identity provider outage, RPC pool failure, and the operator cutover checklist with its approval gates, without hosts or secrets.
3. A security review document under human/wallet/docs SHALL record the delta review of the vendored threshold library since its published audit, the daemon's trust boundaries, and every open finding with severity.
4. THE merged gate SHALL run once on the merged feature tip in wave 5 with its evidence recorded, and the rehearsal SHALL run once with counts recorded; no task reruns either.

## Requirement 1217: The Sidecar Binary, Its Configuration and Its HTTP Server

**User Story:** As a node operator, I want one sidecar binary with one configuration file and no hidden defaults, so that I know exactly what my node serves and on what terms.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crate interop/crates/x-websearch SHALL build the binary x-websearch as a member of the interop workspace under its lints, SHALL use a std-library HTTP server with no axum, tokio or hyper dependency, and SHALL use std::net::TcpStream with native-tls for outbound HTTP as interop/crates/layerx-gas-station/src/rpc.rs does.
2. THE configuration loader SHALL decode a JSON file with unknown fields refused and SHALL refuse a missing or placeholder listen address, data directory, seed list, crawl budget, fetch limit, asset id, price, gateway endpoint, sequencer trust input, EVM endpoint or chain id, naming the field in every refusal.
3. THE sidecar SHALL read the attestor key, the submitter key and the 402 receiver key only from files named by X_WEBSEARCH_ATTESTOR_KEY_FILE, X_WEBSEARCH_SUBMITTER_KEY_FILE and X_WEBSEARCH_RECEIVER_KEY_FILE, SHALL refuse a key found in the configuration file, and SHALL never log key material.
4. THE HTTP server SHALL serve GET /health free and GET /search, GET /fetch and GET /content/<digest> as paid resources, SHALL bound the worker pool, the request line, the header size and the read time, and SHALL answer a malformed request with 400, an unknown path with 404 and an unsupported method with 405.
5. TESTS SHALL start the real server on the loopback interface and cover the configuration's acceptance and each refusal, the key-file rules, the health route, each bound and each error status.

## Requirement 1218: Fetch, Extraction and the Canonical Content Digest

**User Story:** As a contract or an agent relying on fetched data, I want two independent sidecars that saw the same page to produce the same 32 bytes, so that agreement on a digest means agreement on the content.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A FETCH SHALL accept only http and https, SHALL refuse loopback, private, link-local and multicast destinations after name resolution unless allow_loopback is set, SHALL enforce a 3 second connect limit, a 10 second total limit, a 2 MiB body limit and at most three redirects each re-checked, and SHALL refuse a URL robots.txt disallows for the user-agent token x-websearch.
2. EXTRACTION SHALL drop script, style, noscript and template elements from text/html, turn block elements into line breaks and decode entities, SHALL pass text/plain and application/json through, and SHALL refuse every other media type.
3. CANONICALISATION SHALL decode to UTF-8 from the declared charset refusing invalid input, turn CRLF and CR into LF, remove control characters other than LF and TAB, collapse runs of spaces and tabs to one space, remove trailing spaces from each line, collapse three or more LF to two, trim leading and trailing whitespace and apply Unicode NFC.
4. THE canonical bytes SHALL be the ASCII domain PAXEERX_WEB_CONTENT_V1, the kind byte, the payload with a big-endian uint32 length, the lower-case media type without parameters with a uint32 length, and the text with a big-endian uint64 length, and THE content digest SHALL be keccak256 of those bytes with no clock, header, host name or node identity in them.
5. THE sidecar SHALL write the canonical bytes to its content store under their digest, and GET /content/<digest> on any sidecar SHALL return exactly those bytes, retrieving a digest it does not hold from its configured peer sidecars and keeping it only when the recomputed digest matches, or 404 when no peer holds it.
6. TESTS SHALL fetch committed pages from a real loopback server and assert the extracted text and the digest against committed vectors, and SHALL cover each destination, limit, redirect, robots.txt and media-type refusal.

## Requirement 1219: The Crawler and the Local Index

**User Story:** As a node operator, I want my node to build its own search index from seeds I choose, so that search needs no outside vendor and no API key.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE crawler SHALL walk the configured seed list within the crawl budget - pages per cycle, pages per host, maximum depth and per-host politeness delay - through the same fetch path and refusals as a fetch, and SHALL honour robots.txt for x-websearch.
2. THE index SHALL be a tantivy index under the data directory with the fields url, title and body, and re-crawling a page SHALL replace its document rather than add a second.
3. SEARCH SHALL return at most ten results of url, title and snippet sorted by score descending then url ascending, and its canonical bytes SHALL be the compact JSON array in that order with no score in the bytes.
4. NO third-party search vendor, search API or API key SHALL appear in the crate, its configuration or its documentation.
5. TESTS SHALL crawl a committed site from a real loopback server and cover the budget limits, the depth limit, the politeness delay, a robots.txt disallow, a re-crawl replacing its document, and a search's order and canonical bytes.

## Requirement 1220: Pay Per Request Over 402LXP

**User Story:** As an agent, I want to pay a sidecar per request in the asset I hold and get the resource only when the payment has really settled, so that paying is simple and nobody is paid for nothing.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE sidecar SHALL be a 402LXP seller built on interop/crates/layerx-x402, offering on every paid route the metered scheme with one grant and one draw per request and the exact scheme as the fallback alternative, in PAYMENT-REQUIRED, and SHALL read the buyer's payment from PAYMENT-SIGNATURE.
2. THE accepted assets SHALL be exactly SID, PAX, USDC and USDL, each identified by its registered kernel asset id from the configuration, and the loader SHALL refuse a missing asset, an extra asset, a zero id and a placeholder id.
3. THE price per request SHALL be an operator-set amount per asset in that asset's base units, and the configuration example and the documentation SHALL state that its initial value equals one tenth of a US cent at the time of configuration.
4. SETTLEMENT SHALL be verified through the gateway as spec/402lxp/protocol.md defines - the draw submitted with lx_sendActivity, a pending result recovered with lx_getActivityStatus or lx_getReceipt, the receipt's sequencer signature verified against configured trust inputs - and the sidecar SHALL return PAYMENT-RESPONSE with lxp:<receipt_digest> only after that verification.
5. A PENDING or unknown settlement, a receipt for another request, a changed request under the same key and an unverified signature SHALL release nothing, and a retry of the same request SHALL reuse the same signed activity and idempotency key.
6. TESTS SHALL drive the real seller against a recorded gateway exchange in the existing fixture format and cover a metered success, an exact success, each asset, the pending recovery, each refusal above, and SHALL write the recorded client-side exchange the SDK and MCP tests replay.

## Requirement 1221: The xweb Module

**User Story:** As a contract author, I want a module that records my request, accepts only a majority-attested answer and pays the attestors who gave it, so that external data on chain is as trustworthy as its attestor set.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE module modules/xweb SHALL store each request under a monotonically increasing nonce with the requester, the kind, the payload hash, the callback gas, the fee and the height, and SHALL emit an XWebRequested event carrying every field an attestor needs.
2. FULFIL SHALL rebuild the 188-byte preimage modules/xweb/ATTESTATION.md specifies, SHALL verify 65-byte signatures with v in 27 or 28, s at or below half the order, strictly ascending recovered signers, every signer registered and at least the threshold, in the shape of modules/layerxbridge/keeper/bridge.go verifySignatures using modules/layerxbridge/types.RecoverSigner read-only.
3. FULFIL SHALL store at most 4096 bytes of response content with the 32-byte digest and the full length, SHALL refuse a longer response, a length shorter than the response, a fulfilled or refunded request and a paused module, and SHALL split the fee equally among the signers' payout accounts with the integer remainder to the lowest signer.
4. A REQUEST not fulfilled within the timeout in blocks SHALL be refundable to its requester exactly once, and a refunded request SHALL never be fulfilled.
5. GOVERNANCE messages carrying the gov authority SHALL register and remove attestors with their payout accounts, set the threshold, the fee, the payload and callback caps and the timeout, and pause and unpause; the keeper SHALL refuse a threshold at or below half the set or above it and SHALL raise the threshold to the majority when an attestor is added.
6. GO tests SHALL cover the request store and event, a fulfilment at threshold with the fee split, each signature refusal, each size refusal, the timeout refund and its refusals, each governance message and its refusals, and the preimage against the shared vector.

## Requirement 1222: The xweb Precompile and Its Solidity Interface

**User Story:** As a Solidity developer, I want one address and one interface for web data with a callback I can trust, so that using it is a call and a function.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE precompile SHALL live at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001019 in the package precompiles/xweb with XWeb.sol, abi.json, xweb.go, setup.go generated by scripts/bump_version and a versions file, SHALL be registered in precompiles/setup.go, and its interface SHALL be contracts/src/precompiles/IXWeb.sol.
2. request(uint8,bytes,uint64) SHALL be payable with exactly the current fee in PAX and return the request id, fulfil(uint64,bytes,bytes32,uint32,bytes[]) SHALL call the module's fulfilment, and refund(uint64) SHALL call the module's refund; view methods SHALL return the request, the result, the attestor set, the threshold and the fee.
3. AFTER a fulfilment the precompile SHALL call onXWebResponse(uint64,bytes32,uint32,bytes) on the requester with gas bounded by the request's callback gas and the module's maximum, and a callback that reverts or runs out of gas SHALL be recorded without undoing the fulfilment.
4. A REFERENCE consumer under contracts/src/xweb SHALL accept the callback only from the precompile address and only for a request id it issued, and Foundry tests SHALL cover its acceptance and refusals and the interface's selectors against abi.json.
5. GO tests SHALL drive the precompile through the EVM with the real keeper, covering request, fulfil with the callback succeeding, reverting and running out of gas, refund, each view, a wrong fee and a read-only call to a state-changing method.

## Requirement 1223: The Kernel Web Observation Activity

**User Story:** As a kernel program author, I want attested web data committed through the sequencer like oracle prices are, so that a program reads it deterministically and replay reproduces it.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. include/layerx/lx_web.h SHALL define the web observation activity id, the observation layout carrying the origin-2 preimage fields, the stored response of at most 4096 bytes and the signatures, and the web request record topic, beside lx_oracle.h and without changing it.
2. INTAKE SHALL rebuild the preimage, recover each signer with lxp_secp256k1_recover_address, require strictly ascending registered signers at the kernel web attestor threshold, require low s and a pending program web request with the same program id, request id, kind and payload hash, and commit the observation exactly once.
3. THE kernel web attestor set SHALL be registered through a kernel activity accepted only from the kernel's existing parameter authority, and SHALL refuse a threshold at or below half the set.
4. THE sequencer SHALL fold committed observations into a web root in the shape src/sequencer/lx_oracle_root.c uses, and src/network/lx_web_adapter.c SHALL encode the activity in the shape of src/network/lx_oracle_adapter.c with a committed encoding vector.
5. C tests with make targets SHALL cover an accepted observation, each signature, threshold and request refusal, a replay producing the same root, and the adapter's encoding against the vector.

## Requirement 1224: The web_read Host Import

**User Story:** As a kernel program, I want to read an attested web response by request id without ever dialling out, so that my execution stays deterministic.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE runtime SHALL allocate guest ABI 4 end to end in the shape of the v3 allocation, adding web_read(i32,i32,i32,i32)->i32 in a new layerx_v4 ABI group after layerx_v3, SHALL leave the v1 to v3 manifests, their frozen vectors and their checksum lines in programs/abi-frozen.sha256 byte-identical, SHALL append the v4 vector and its checksum line, and SHALL validate the import like oracle_read.
2. web_read SHALL return the committed response, digest and full length for a request id owned by the calling program, SHALL return the absent code for a request with no committed observation, and SHALL refuse an output buffer too small or out of bounds.
3. THE call bridge in src/modules/programs/call.c SHALL expose the committed observation to the runtime in the shape of the oracle view, and SHALL never perform network input or output.
4. programs/sdk/rust SHALL expose a safe wrapper for web_read beside its oracle wrapper.
5. TESTS in Rust and C SHALL cover a present read, an absent read, a read of another program's request, each buffer refusal and the unchanged frozen v1 to v3 manifests.

## Requirement 1225: Agent Clients and the MCP Tool

**User Story:** As an agent developer, I want a client that pays and fetches in one call and refuses content whose settlement or digest does not check out, so that I do not hand-roll the 402 exchange.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. agent/sdk/typescript and agent/sdk/python SHALL each expose search, fetch and content-by-digest against any sidecar endpoint, performing the 402LXP exchange with the SDK's existing grant, draw and settlement helpers.
2. EACH client SHALL verify PAYMENT-RESPONSE before returning content, SHALL refuse a settlement whose payer or purpose does not match the challenge, and SHALL recompute the content digest of a fetch or content response and refuse a mismatch.
3. agent/crates/layerx-mcp SHALL expose a web tool with search, fetch and content operations that pays through the same exchange and passes every spend through the crate's existing approval boundary.
4. TESTS SHALL replay the sidecar's recorded exchange from a real loopback server and cover a paid success in each asset, a refused settlement, a digest mismatch and, for the MCP tool, an unapproved spend.

## Requirement 1226: Attestor Signing and the Submitter

**User Story:** As an attestor operator, I want my sidecar to answer requests on its own and get the answer posted once a majority agrees, so that I run one binary and not a relay.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. AN ATTESTOR sidecar SHALL watch XWebRequested events from the configured EVM endpoint to the configured confirmation depth, fetch the payload independently, build the origin-1 preimage and sign its digest with the web-attestor key.
2. ATTESTORS SHALL exchange signatures with the configured peer sidecars over an authenticated route, and a signature over a different digest SHALL be discarded and recorded.
3. THE submitter SHALL post fulfil once the threshold is reached with signatures in ascending signer order, SHALL sign the EVM transaction with the submitter key, SHALL journal the signed bytes before broadcast so a restart rebroadcasts rather than re-signs, and SHALL treat an already-fulfilled request as completed.
4. THE attestor key SHALL be distinct from any consensus, validator, bridge, submitter or receiver key, and the sidecar SHALL refuse to start when two key files hold the same key.
5. TESTS SHALL cover the watch against a recorded exchange, the preimage against the shared vector, the signature exchange and its refusal, the ascending order, the journal before broadcast, a restart rebroadcast and an already-fulfilled request.

## Requirement 1227: The Program Request Path End to End

**User Story:** As a kernel program author, I want to emit a request, pay for it and read the answer later, so that web data is one call away from my program.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A PROGRAM SHALL request a fetch by emitting the web request record and paying the web fee account with transfer_402 in the same call, and the call bridge SHALL record the pending request only when both succeed.
2. ATTESTOR sidecars SHALL watch program web request records through the gateway, fetch independently, sign the origin-2 digest and post the web observation activity through lx_sendActivity once the threshold is reached, in bytes equal to the C adapter's encoding vector.
3. THE fee SHALL be split equally among the signing attestors' kernel accounts at intake with the remainder to the lowest signer.
4. AN END-TO-END C test SHALL run a reference program that requests, pays, receives an observation and reads it with web_read, and a Rust test SHALL assert the sidecar's activity bytes equal the vector.

## Requirement 1228: Packaging and the Node Image

**User Story:** As an operator, I want the sidecar to come with my node the way everything else does, so that running it is configuration, not assembly.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. interop/deploy/x-websearch SHALL carry a Dockerfile building x-websearch from the interop workspace on pinned base images, a systemd unit running it with a dedicated user and a hardened sandbox, and a configuration example whose placeholders the loader refuses and whose allow_loopback is false.
2. docker/docker-compose.yml SHALL gain an x-websearch service beside the node services, and the root Dockerfile SHALL build the binary and copy it into the node image.
3. A CHECK script SHALL assert the Dockerfile's pinned bases, the unit's user and sandbox directives, the compose entry, the node image's copy of the binary, and that the loader refuses the configuration example.

## Requirement 1229: The v6.8 Upgrade Plan

**User Story:** As a validator, I want the chain half of this feature behind one named upgrade, so that nothing changes on my node until governance says so.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE name v6.8 SHALL be appended to node/tags and its handler registered in node/upgrades.go, adding the xweb store key through the upgrade's store loader and initialising the module's parameters to their documented defaults with an empty attestor set and the module paused.
2. node/app.go SHALL wire the xweb keeper, module and store key, and the precompile's keeper accessor, and precompiles/xweb/versions and setup.go SHALL name v6.8 as regenerated by scripts/bump_version.
3. NO state change of this feature SHALL take effect before the upgrade height, and a node replaying blocks below it SHALL produce exactly the state it produces without this feature.
4. TESTS SHALL assert the handler is registered under the name in node/tags, the store is added, the defaults are set, the module is paused and the precompile answers only after the upgrade.

## Requirement 1230: The Documentation Page

**User Story:** As a developer arriving cold, I want one page that says what the web service is, how to pay for it and how to call it from a contract or a program, so that I can use it without reading the code.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. docs/site/docs/protocol/xweb.md SHALL follow the shape of docs/site/docs/protocol/sidiora.md and describe the sidecar, the four assets and the price rule, the three routes and GET /content/<digest>, the contract path with the precompile address and the callback, the attestor majority, the kernel path with web_read, and that the chain change arrives through the v6.8 upgrade and a governance proposal.
2. THE page SHALL be linked from docs/site/mkdocs.yml, SHALL carry no date, hostname, IP address, node count, internal URL or credential, SHALL name the product Paxeer X Network, and SHALL use no link but https://paxeer.app, paths under github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network and relative links inside the site.
3. THE site SHALL build with mkdocs build --strict.

## Requirement 1231: A Local Dry Run

**User Story:** As the person who will turn this on, I want the sidecar loop proven end to end against local nodes first, so that the first real run is not the first run.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A DRY RUN script SHALL start anvil, a real loopback web server serving committed pages, and three local x-websearch processes with run-local attestor keys and allow_loopback set, and SHALL deploy the reference consumer to anvil.
2. THE three sidecars SHALL fetch the same page independently and produce the same digest and valid ascending signatures over the origin-1 preimage, the submitter SHALL assemble fulfil calldata that decodes against precompiles/xweb/abi.json, and the consumer's callback SHALL be delivered on anvil from the impersonated precompile address with the attested response and the bounded gas.
3. THE run SHALL touch no public network, SHALL stop with a message naming a missing tool rather than skipping a step, and SHALL record its exchange as a replayable fixture carrying no key material, no endpoint but the loopback ones it started and no date or hostname.

## Requirement 1232: One Workflow and One Recorded Run

**User Story:** As a reviewer, I want one workflow whose filters and job names are true and one recorded run on the merged revision, so that a green check means this feature was tested.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. ONE workflow .github/workflows/xweb-test.yml SHALL run on pull requests and pushes touching the trees this feature changes, with a concurrency group per ref and cancel-in-progress, and SHALL carry legs named for what they run: the x-websearch crate, modules/xweb with precompiles/xweb, the Foundry consumer tests, the kernel web make targets with the runtime web_read test, and the SDK and MCP tests.
2. NO job SHALL carry continue-on-error, every action SHALL be pinned the way the repository's existing workflows pin theirs, and a check script SHALL assert that every path filter names a path that exists and that every leg's command runs from the repository root.
3. THE legs SHALL be run once on the merged revision of waves 1 and 2 and recorded in spec/paxeer-x-web/qualification.kvx as gate records carrying the task, the requirements, the revision, the command, the exit code and the log path, written only by having executed the command.
4. ANY failure the run exposes that belongs to no task in this feature SHALL be recorded once as an observation and not chased, no gate SHALL be rerun to confirm a pass, and nothing SHALL be deployed.

## Requirement 1233: A Contract Calls an API Beyond the Network

**User Story:** As a contract developer, I want my contract to call an HTTP API, with a credential when the API needs one, and receive an attested answer, so that on-chain logic can act on data that exists outside the network without my running an oracle.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE xweb module SHALL accept a request kind api whose payload names the method (GET or POST), an https URL, public request headers, a request body, a list of JSON pointers selecting the attested fields, an attestation level (majority, or single with a named attestor) and zero or more credential envelopes, SHALL bound each part and the whole within the payload cap, and SHALL refuse a payload naming an attestor outside the registered set or carrying more envelopes than registered attestors.
2. A CREDENTIAL ENVELOPE SHALL be encrypted to one attestor's registered secp256k1 key with an ephemeral sender key (ECIES over secp256k1 with HKDF-SHA256 and AES-256-GCM), SHALL carry that attestor's address in the clear so each sidecar picks its own, and SHALL be decrypted by the sidecar in memory only: the plaintext SHALL never be written to a log, a fixture, the index, the content store or any file.
3. THE SIDECAR SHALL perform an api request with the public headers plus the decrypted credential headers under the fetch limits and destination refusals of requirement 2, SHALL apply the JSON pointers to a JSON response and canonicalise the selected values in RFC 8785 form, SHALL treat an empty pointer list as the raw bounded body, and SHALL refuse a response that is not JSON when pointers are given or a pointer that resolves to nothing, naming the pointer.
4. UNDER the majority level the module SHALL require the threshold of signatures over the canonical answer exactly as for a fetch; UNDER the single level it SHALL accept one signature from the named attestor only, and SHALL record the level in the stored result and in XWebFulfilled so a consumer can tell the two apart.
5. THE Solidity library XWebApi SHALL let a contract build an api payload with get, post, select, withCredential and single and submit it through the precompile in one statement, and the TypeScript and Python clients SHALL build envelopes from the attestor set the precompile exposes, so a developer needs no encoding knowledge.
6. TESTS SHALL cover the payload codec and every refusal in Go, the envelope round trip against one vector file shared by Go, Rust, TypeScript and Python, the sidecar's api call against a loopback server that refuses a call without the credential header, the absence of the credential from every file the sidecar writes and from its log output, the pointer selection and canonicalisation vectors, both attestation levels through the precompile, and the library through a Foundry consumer.

## Requirement 1234: Sponsored Gas Paid in Sidiora

**User Story:** As someone who holds Sidiora and no Paxeer coin, I want to sign a batch that a sponsor pays for and that repays the sponsor in Sidiora in the same transaction, so that I can transact without first acquiring the network coin.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE sponsored batch contract SHALL execute a batch only when it carries both the account's authorisation over the batch and a relayer quote signed by the relayer named in that quote, and SHALL revert when either signature is absent, recovers to a different address, or covers different bytes.
2. THE quote SHALL carry the sponsor address, the Sidiora token address, the maximum Sidiora amount the account will pay, the quoted amount, a deadline and a quote nonce, and the contract SHALL revert when the block timestamp is past the deadline, when the quoted amount exceeds the maximum, or when the quote nonce has already been consumed.
3. THE contract SHALL transfer the quoted Sidiora amount from the account to the sponsor inside the same batch execution, before or after the batch calls as the ordering the contract documents requires, and SHALL revert the whole batch when that transfer fails, so a batch that executes and a sponsor that is repaid are the same event.
4. THE quoted amount SHALL be checked against the paymaster's owner-set Sidiora rate and the staleness bound that rate carries, and a quote whose implied rate lies outside the contract's declared spread from that rate SHALL be rejected; a rate the paymaster has held longer than its staleness bound allows SHALL reject the quote rather than skip the check.
5. THE batch nonce SHALL keep protecting the account's authorisation against replay exactly as it does now, and the quote nonce SHALL protect the relayer's quote against replay independently, so replaying either half alone reverts.
6. THE direct execution path, which the account itself calls with no signature, SHALL keep working and SHALL require no quote, and the contract SHALL keep receiving the network coin.
7. A Foundry test SHALL cover a successful sponsored batch with the sponsor repaid, a missing and a wrong account signature, a missing and a wrong relayer signature, an expired deadline, a quoted amount above the maximum, a replayed quote nonce, a replayed batch nonce, a failing Sidiora transfer reverting the whole batch, a quote outside the declared spread from the governed rate, a governed rate that is missing or stale, and the direct execution path.

## Requirement 1235: The Gas Station

**User Story:** As the operator of the sponsored path, I want a service that quotes a Sidiora price, submits the transaction, pays the Paxeer coin and collects the Sidiora, so that sponsorship is a running system rather than a contract nobody drives.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE gas station SHALL be a Rust crate in the interop workspace, built as a library plus a thin binary that takes a configuration file path, in the shape interop/crates/layerx-bridge-relayer already uses, and SHALL compile under the workspace lints interop/Cargo.toml declares with no allow added at crate scope.
2. THE quote it signs SHALL carry exactly the fields the contract verifies, SHALL be produced over the digest the contract recovers, and SHALL be priced from the paymaster's governed rate plus the station's configured margin, refusing to quote when the rate is absent, stale beyond the configured age or outside the configured spread.
3. THE station SHALL refuse a quote that would exceed its configured per-account, per-interval or per-quote limits, and SHALL refuse to quote at all when its Paxeer balance is below its configured floor, so it cannot promise gas it cannot pay for.
4. THE submission path SHALL build the EIP-7702 transaction carrying the account's authorisation and the signed quote, SHALL record the exact signed bytes in an append-only journal before broadcast so a restart rebroadcasts rather than re-signs, and SHALL treat a consumed quote nonce observed on chain as a completed submission rather than an error to retry.
5. THE relayer key SHALL enter the process through configuration and SHALL never be logged, printed in an error, or written to the journal; the journal SHALL carry no key material and no credential.
6. UNIT tests SHALL cover the quote digest against a vector the contract test also asserts, the pricing refusals, each limit refusal, the balance floor refusal and the journal's replay behaviour; AN integration test SHALL drive a full quote, submit and collect cycle against a local node or a recorded node fixture carried in the crate and SHALL assert the Sidiora that moved and the Paxeer that was spent.

## Requirement 1236: Signing the Authorisation

**User Story:** As someone using the wallet or the SDK, I want the authorisation and the quote presented and signed the way any other transaction is, so that sponsored gas is something I can see and agree to rather than something that happens to me.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. THE TypeScript SDK SHALL expose the calls that request a quote from a gas station, build the sponsored batch, produce the digest the account signs and assemble the EIP-7702 authorisation, using the same call-construction style the SDK's existing precompile call builders use and adding no runtime dependency.
2. THE SDK SHALL refuse to build a sponsored batch whose quote is expired, whose maximum is below the quoted amount, whose sponsor or token address is not the one configured, or whose decimals do not match Sidiora's six, and each refusal SHALL be a typed result rather than a thrown string.
3. THE human web application SHALL let a person choose to pay a transaction's fee in Sidiora, SHALL show the quoted Sidiora amount, the maximum they are agreeing to and the deadline before they sign, and SHALL surface the unavailable, refused and cancelled outcomes through the same outcome shape the wallet path already returns.
4. EVERY string the web application shows for this journey SHALL come from the copy catalogue, and no literal endpoint, host or address SHALL appear in the application's source; the gas station's location SHALL be a documented configuration value.
5. A SDK test SHALL assert the digest against the same vector the contract and the gas station assert, and each refusal; A web application test SHALL assert the quote presentation, the consent, and the unavailable, refused and cancelled outcomes.

## Requirement 1237: Sidiora Fees Read Correctly in the Explorer

**User Story:** As someone reading a transaction in the explorer, I want a fee paid in Sidiora to read as Sidiora with six decimals, so that I am not shown a Paxeer-shaped number for a Sidiora payment.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHERE a transaction's fee was paid in a token other than the network coin THE explorer SHALL render the amount with that token's decimals and symbol rather than the network coin's eighteen decimals and symbol.
2. THE Sidiora case SHALL render six decimals and the SID symbol, and the existing Paxeer case SHALL keep rendering exactly what it renders now, including its wei and gwei unit names and its exchange-rate toggle.
3. THE types describing the fee payload SHALL declare the fee token's symbol and decimals as optional fields, and their absence SHALL mean the network coin, so a chain that pays only in the network coin renders unchanged.
4. A test SHALL render a Sidiora fee, a Paxeer fee and a fee with no token declared, and SHALL assert the rendered amount, decimals and symbol for each.

## Requirement 1238: Sidiora as a Native Denom the Bridge Alone Mints

**User Story:** As a holder who moves Sidiora across chains, I want the bridge to be the only thing that can create or destroy it on Paxeer X Network, so that the supply on this chain is exactly what the bridge has admitted.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. SIDIORA SHALL exist on chain as a tokenfactory denom whose creator is the x/layerxbridge module account and whose subdenom names Sidiora's base unit, giving six decimals against a whole SID, and its denom metadata SHALL declare the display symbol SID, the six-decimal exponent and the description.
